sentences.zh: 志六十九

translations.literal: Treatise Sixty-Nine
translations.idiomatic: Treatise Sixty-Nine

sentences.zh: 樂一

translations.literal: Music I
translations.idiomatic: Music, Part One

sentences.zh: 記曰：「安上治民，莫善於禮。」

translations.literal: The Record says: "For securing the sovereign above and governing the people, nothing is better than ritual."
translations.idiomatic: The Record says: "For securing the ruler and governing the people, nothing is better than ritual."

sentences.zh: 「移風易俗，莫善於樂。」

translations.literal: "For changing customs and transforming habits, nothing is better than music."
translations.idiomatic: "For changing customs and transforming habits, nothing is better than music."

sentences.zh: 樂也者，考神納賓，類物表庸，以其德馨殷薦上帝者也。

translations.literal: Music is that which examines the spirits and receives guests, classifies things by kind and displays merit, and with fragrant virtue richly offers to the Lord on High.
translations.idiomatic: Music is the means by which one examines the spirits and receives guests, arranges things by kind and displays merit, and with fragrant virtue richly presents offerings to the Lord on High.

sentences.zh: 聖道四達，聲與政通，於是有綴兆之容，箾籥之音，被服其光輝，膏潤其猷烈，以與民康之，民無憔悴揫傷之嗟，放僻嫚蕩之志，夫然後雅頌作焉。

translations.literal: When the sage Way extends in all four directions and sound is in accord with government, then there are the forms of linked dance patterns and the tones of reed-pipes, clothing themselves in its radiance and anointing its great achievements, thereby bringing ease to the people; the people have no sighs of withered and wounded distress, nor ambitions of perverse indulgence and dissipation—only then are the Ya and Song composed.
translations.idiomatic: When the sage Way reaches everywhere and music aligns with governance, there arise patterned dance formations and reed-pipe melodies; people clothe themselves in its brilliance and are nourished by its great deeds, and the people are brought to well-being. Without the people's sighs of exhaustion and injury, or their impulses toward wayward excess, only then do the Ya and Song odes take shape.

sentences.zh: 蓋三苗格而韶舞，十一稅而頌謳，玄鳥歌而商祚興，靈台奏而周道昌。

translations.literal: For when the Three Miao submitted, the Shao dance was performed; when the tithe was one in eleven, songs of praise were sung; when the dark bird sang, the fortune of Shang rose; when the Spirit Terrace was played upon, the Way of Zhou flourished.
translations.idiomatic: When the Three Miao submitted, the Shao dance was performed; when the levy was one part in eleven, hymns of praise were sung; when the dark bird was hymned, the house of Shang rose; when music sounded at the Spirit Terrace, the Zhou dynasty flourished.

sentences.zh: 王官失守，神不降祉。

translations.literal: The royal offices lost their charge, and the spirits did not bestow blessings.
translations.idiomatic: The royal music offices lost their proper function, and the spirits ceased to send down blessings.

sentences.zh: 移及春秋，脊脊大亂。

translations.literal: Extending into the Spring and Autumn period, there was great disorder piled upon disorder.
translations.idiomatic: By the Spring and Autumn period, disorder had mounted upon disorder.

sentences.zh: 仲尼序詩，列黍離於國風，齊王德於邦君，明其不能復雅。

translations.literal: Confucius arranged the Odes, placing "Thorn-apple Millet" among the Airs of the States and ranking the virtue of kings with that of feudal lords, thereby showing that the Ya could not be restored.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius arranged the Odes, placing "Thorn-apple Millet" among the Airs of the States and setting the virtue of kings alongside that of feudal lords, making clear that the grand Ya style could no longer be recovered.

sentences.zh: 中更暴秦，樂經埃滅，音之鄭衛，自此而階，郊廟登歌，聲不逮下。

translations.literal: In the midst came violent Qin; the Music Classic was buried in dust; the sounds of Zheng and Wei from then on ascended the steps; at suburban and temple sacrifices the ascending songs did not reach below.
translations.idiomatic: Then came the tyranny of Qin, and the Music Classic was lost to dust; the sounds of Zheng and Wei thereafter gained the upper hand, and at suburban and temple rites the ascending hymns no longer reached the ranks below.

sentences.zh: 擾民齊教，無聞焉爾。

translations.literal: To harmonize the people through instruction—of this nothing more was heard.
translations.idiomatic: As for harmonizing the people through instruction by music, nothing more was heard of it.

sentences.zh: 然而歷代創興，莫不舖陳南雅，自製郊辭，繩祖業之維艱，頌帝功之有赫，考較鐘懸，裁定縟典。

translations.literal: Yet whenever a dynasty was newly founded, none failed to spread forth the southern Ya, compose their own suburban hymns, bind themselves to the arduous legacy of their ancestors, praise the splendor of imperial achievement, examine and compare bell-frames, and fix ritual regulations.
translations.idiomatic: Yet each newly founded dynasty spread forth the southern Ya odes, composed its own suburban hymns, bound itself to the arduous work of its forebears, praised the splendor of imperial merit, compared bell-chime arrangements, and settled the ritual canon.

sentences.zh: 雖渾灝三五，炳焉同風，而寤想聞韶，跂之彌卲。

translations.literal: Although the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors were vast and luminous with a single wind, yet upon waking one thinks of hearing the Shao, and the more one strains toward it, the farther it recedes.
translations.idiomatic: Though the Three Sovereigns and Five Emperors shine with a common grandeur, to dream of hearing the Shao is only to find it recede the more one reaches for it.

sentences.zh: 是則前誥所譏，鄰於夜誦者也。

translations.literal: This, then, is what the former edicts ridiculed as bordering on recitation by night.
translations.idiomatic: This is what earlier imperial pronouncements mocked as little better than chanting lessons through the night.

sentences.zh: 清起僻遠，迎神祭天，初沿邊俗。

translations.literal: The Qing arose in a remote borderland; in welcoming the spirits and sacrificing to Heaven they at first followed frontier custom.
translations.idiomatic: The Qing dynasty arose in a remote frontier region; in welcoming the spirits and sacrificing to Heaven it at first followed borderland custom.

sentences.zh: 及太祖受命，始習華風。

translations.literal: When the Taizu received the Mandate, they began to adopt Chinese court style.
translations.idiomatic: Once the Taizu received the Mandate, the court began to adopt Chinese ritual and musical practice.

sentences.zh: 天命、崇德中，征瓦爾喀，臣朝鮮，平定察哈爾，得其宮懸，以備四裔燕樂。

translations.literal: During the Tianming and Chongde reigns, they campaigned against the Warka, brought Korea to submission, pacified the Chahar, obtained their court bell-sets, and thereby equipped music for banquets of the four border peoples.
translations.idiomatic: During the Tianming and Chongde periods the court campaigned against the Warka, received Korea as a tributary state, pacified the Chahar, and took over their palace bell-sets to furnish banquet music for the four frontier peoples.

sentences.zh: 世祖入關，修明之舊，有中和韶樂，郊廟朝會用之。

translations.literal: When the Shizu entered the Pass, he restored Ming institutions; there was the Harmonious and Central Shao music, used at suburban sacrifices, temples, and court assemblies.
translations.idiomatic: When the Shizu entered the Pass he restored Ming practice; there was Harmonious Central Shao music for suburban rites, temples, and court assemblies.

sentences.zh: 有丹陛大樂，王公百僚慶賀用之。

translations.literal: There was the Great Music of the Cinnabar Steps, used when princes, dukes, and the hundred officials offered congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: There was the Great Music of the Cinnabar Steps for congratulatory ceremonies of princes, dukes, and the hundred officials.

sentences.zh: 有中和清樂、丹陛清樂，宮中筵宴用之。

translations.literal: There was Harmonious Central clear music and Cinnabar Steps clear music, used at banquets within the palace.
translations.idiomatic: There was Harmonious Central clear music and Cinnabar Steps clear music for palace banquets.

sentences.zh: 有鹵簿導迎樂，巡蹕用之。

translations.literal: There was the guard-of-honor conducting and welcoming music, used when the emperor toured.
translations.idiomatic: There was guard-of-honor conducting music for imperial progresses.

sentences.zh: 又制鐃歌法曲，奮武敵愾，宣鬯八風，以儷漢世短簫。

translations.literal: They also devised nao-song regulated pieces to rouse martial spirit and match the enemy's ardor, spreading the eight winds in harmony, to pair with the Han dynasty's short panpipes.
translations.idiomatic: They also composed regulated nao-song pieces to rouse martial spirit against the foe and spread harmony through the eight winds, matching the Han dynasty's short panpipe music.

sentences.zh: 而滿洲舊舞，是曰莽式，率以蘭錡世裔充選，所陳皆遼瀋故事，作麾旄弢矢躍馬蒞陣之容，屈伸進反輕蹻俯仰之節，歌辭異漢，不頒太常，所謂纘業垂統，前王不忘者歟？

translations.literal: As for the old Manchu dance called Mangshi, selection was generally drawn from descendants of the Lanqi clan; what was presented were all stories of Liaodong and Shenyang, portraying banners and feathers, sheathed arrows, leaping horses, and taking the battlefield; with bending and stretching, advancing and retreating, light-footed steps and bowing and rising in rhythm; the lyrics differed from Chinese and were not issued by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices—is this not what is meant by continuing the enterprise and handing down the tradition, that former kings are not forgotten?
translations.idiomatic: The old Manchu dance called Mangshi was performed chiefly by descendants of the Lanqi line; the scenes enacted were all tales of Liaodong and Shenyang—banners and plumes, sheathed arrows, mounted charges upon the field, with bending, advancing, retreating, and light-footed rhythms of bow and rise. The songs were not in Chinese and were not distributed by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices—is this not the meaning of carrying on the founding work and transmitting the tradition, that former kings are not forgotten?

sentences.zh: 聖祖、高宗，製作自任，臣匪師曠之聰，君逾姬旦之美。

translations.literal: The Sage Ancestor and the High Ancestor took creation upon themselves; ministers were not as acute-eared as Master Kuang, yet the sovereigns surpassed the beauty of the Duke of Zhou.
translations.idiomatic: The Kangxi and Qianlong emperors took musical creation upon themselves; their ministers were no Shi Kuang in discernment, yet the sovereigns surpassed even the Duke of Zhou in accomplishment.

sentences.zh: 考音諧金石，昭德摛天漢，帝秩皇造，於斯為盛。

translations.literal: They examined tones to harmonize metal and stone, displayed virtue spreading across the Milky Way; the imperial ordering of the royal creation reached its greatest height here.
translations.idiomatic: They tuned sound to harmonize bells and chimes, displayed virtue spanning the heavens, and the imperial ordering of ritual music reached its fullest flowering.

sentences.zh: 但觀其命伶倫使協律。

translations.literal: Yet observe how they ordered Ling Lun to harmonize the pitch-pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet consider how they charged Ling Lun with harmonizing the pitch-pipes.

sentences.zh: 召咸黑以賡歌，非不陶英鑄莖，四隅率同，而繼體再傳，頌聲浸廢。

translations.literal: They summoned Xian Hei to continue the songs; it was not that they failed to mold the flower and cast the stem, making the four corners uniformly alike, yet after two generations of succession the songs of praise gradually fell into disuse.
translations.idiomatic: They summoned Xian Hei to carry on the hymns; it was not that they failed to refine tone and forge the standard, bringing the four quarters into accord, yet within two reigns of succession the songs of praise gradually decayed.

sentences.zh: 魏文聽之而思臥，季札觀之而無譏，是知樂之為懿，覘國隆洿，謳歌在民，匪所自致，而三古承流，曾靡先覺，可為惋欷者也。

translations.literal: King Wen of Wei heard it and wished to lie down; Ji Zha watched it and found no fault—thus one knows that music as excellence mirrors whether a state rises or declines; songs among the people are not brought about by the ruler alone, yet the three antiquities inherited the current without anyone foreseeing it first—this is cause for sighing in regret.
translations.idiomatic: King Wen of Wei heard it and wished only to sleep; Ji Zha observed it and found no fault to speak of. Thus music as a sign of excellence reveals whether a state flourishes or declines; the people's songs are not produced by the court alone, yet the three antiquities passed down the tradition without anyone truly foreseeing the end—this is indeed cause for sorrow.

translations.literal: and Li Shou thereby took his measured steps.
translations.idiomatic: and Li Shou thereby took his measured steps.

sentences.zh: 將欲起元音之廢，復淳樸之真，弘我夏聲，秕□乞西奏。

translations.literal: They wished to revive the abandoned primal tones, restore pristine truth, expand our Xia sounds, and (text corrupt) reject Western tunes.
translations.idiomatic: They wished to revive the abandoned primal tones, restore pristine simplicity, exalt our Chinese music, and (text corrupt) set aside Western performance.

sentences.zh: 澹欲繕性，一綖庶幾，有庇經誥，其或在此。

translations.literal: To calm desire and repair the nature, a single thread might nearly suffice; to shelter the classics and edicts—perhaps it lies here.
translations.idiomatic: To calm desire and cultivate character, a single thread may nearly suffice; to uphold the classics and imperial instructions—perhaps the means lie here.

sentences.zh: 必監前憲，我則優矣。

translations.literal: If one must take former statutes as mirror, then we are the superior.
translations.idiomatic: If one must take earlier statutes as the standard, then we are indeed the better.

sentences.zh: 國宬所書，聲容器數之次第，管律弦度之討論，煥乎秩秩，可謂有文。

translations.literal: What the Director of Music recorded—the order of sound, vessels, and numbers, the discussion of pipe pitches and string measures—is splendidly orderly and may be called cultured.
translations.idiomatic: What the Director of Music recorded—the ordering of sound, instruments, and numbers, the discussion of pipe pitches and string measures—is splendidly systematic and truly literate.

sentences.zh: 今掇其要，以備簡籍。

translations.literal: Now I gather the essentials to complete the annal record.
translations.idiomatic: Here I gather the essentials for the historical record.

sentences.zh: 太祖肇啟東陲，戡亂用武，聲物弇樸，率緣遼舊。

translations.literal: The Taizu first opened the eastern frontier, quelling disorder by force; music and objects were plain and simple, generally following Liaodong custom.
translations.idiomatic: The Taizu first rose on the eastern frontier, quelling disorder through arms; musical practice was plain and simple, generally following Liaodong tradition.

sentences.zh: 天命元年，即尊位瀋陽，諸貝勒群臣廷賀上壽，始制鹵簿用樂。

translations.literal: In the first year of Tianming, upon taking the exalted seat at Shenyang, when all beile and ministers congratulated him in court and offered longevity wishes, he first instituted music for the guard of honor.
translations.idiomatic: In the first year of Tianming, upon taking the throne at Shenyang, when the beile and ministers congratulated him in court and offered wishes for long life, he first instituted music for the imperial guard of honor.

sentences.zh: 八年，定凱旋拜天行禮筵宴樂制。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, he fixed the regulations for music at the banquet following the triumphant return and worship of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year he fixed the music for the banquet following a victorious return and the rite of worshipping Heaven.

sentences.zh: 太宗天聰八年，又定出師謁堂子拜天行禮樂制、元旦朝賀樂制。

translations.literal: In the eighth year of Tiancong under the Taizong, he further fixed the music for the rite of setting out on campaign, visiting the Tangzi, and worshipping Heaven, and the music for New Year's Day court congratulations.
translations.idiomatic: In the Taizong's eighth year of Tiancong he further fixed the music for departing on campaign, visiting the Tangzi altar, and worshipping Heaven, and the music for New Year's court congratulations.

sentences.zh: 九年，停止元旦雜劇。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, miscellaneous drama at New Year's Day was discontinued.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year miscellaneous drama at New Year's was discontinued.

sentences.zh: 先是梅勒章京張存仁上言：「元旦朝賀，大體所關，雜劇戲謔，不宜陳殿陛。

translations.literal: Earlier, Meile Zhangjing Zhang Cunren memorialized: "New Year's court congratulations concern the great body of ritual; miscellaneous drama and jesting should not be presented before the palace steps.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Meile Zhangjing Zhang Cunren memorialized: "New Year's court congratulations concern the great body of state ritual; miscellaneous drama and jesting ought not be presented before the palace steps.

sentences.zh: 故事，八旗設宴，惟用雅樂。」

translations.literal: By precedent, when the Eight Banners set banquets, only elegant music was used."
translations.idiomatic: By precedent, when the Eight Banners held banquets, only elegant music was used."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The proposal was followed.
translations.idiomatic: The proposal was adopted.

sentences.zh: 十年，建國號曰清，改元崇德。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, the state name Qing was established and the reign title changed to Chongde.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year the state was named Qing and the reign title was changed to Chongde.

sentences.zh: 其明年，遂有事太廟，追尊列祖，四孟時享、歲暮祫祭並奏樂。

translations.literal: The following year, they first sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, posthumously honoring the successive ancestors; seasonal offerings in the four months and the year-end joint sacrifice all had music performed.
translations.idiomatic: The following year they first sacrificed at the Imperial Ancestral Temple and posthumously honored the successive ancestors; seasonal offerings in the four ritual months and the year-end joint sacrifice all included music.

sentences.zh: 皇帝冬至、萬壽二節與元旦同。

translations.literal: The emperor's Winter Solstice and Longevity festivals were treated the same as New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's Winter Solstice and Longevity festivals were treated the same as New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 御前儀仗樂器，鑼二，鼓二，畫角四，簫二，笙二，架鼓四，橫笛二，龍頭橫笛二，檀板二，大鼓二，小銅鈸四，小銅鑼二，大銅鑼四，雲鑼二，嗩吶四。

translations.literal: Musical instruments for the imperial guard of honor: two gongs, two drums, four painted horns, two xiao flutes, two sheng mouth-organs, four frame drums, two transverse flutes, two dragon-head transverse flutes, two clappers, two large drums, four small bronze cymbals, two small bronze gongs, four large bronze gongs, two cloud gongs, and four suona horns.
translations.idiomatic: Musical instruments for the imperial guard of honor included two gongs, two drums, four painted horns, two xiao, two sheng, four frame drums, two transverse flutes, two dragon-head transverse flutes, two clappers, two large drums, four small bronze cymbals, two small bronze gongs, four large bronze gongs, two cloud gongs, and four suona.

sentences.zh: 樂人綠衣黃褂紅帶，六瓣紅絨帽，銅頂上綴黃翎，從內院官奏請也。

translations.literal: Musicians wore green robes, yellow jackets, and red sashes, six-petaled red velvet caps with bronze finials topped by yellow plumes, as requested by the Inner Court officials.
translations.idiomatic: Musicians wore green robes, yellow jackets, and red sashes, with six-petaled red velvet caps bearing bronze finials topped by yellow plumes, as requested by Inner Court officials.

sentences.zh: 又詔公主冊封、諸王家祭、受降獻馘皆用樂。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered that music be used at the investiture of princesses, domestic sacrifices of princely houses, and the presentation of surrendered enemies and severed heads.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also required music at the investiture of princesses, domestic sacrifices of princely houses, and ceremonies presenting surrendered enemies and severed heads.

sentences.zh: 世祖順治元年，攝政睿親王多爾袞既定燕都，將於十月告祭天地宗廟社稷，大學士馮銓、洪承疇等言：「郊廟及社稷樂章，前代各取嘉名，以昭一代之制，梁用『雅』，北齊及隋用『夏』，唐用『和』，宋用『安』，金用『寧』，元宗廟用『寧』、郊社用『咸』，前明用『和』。

translations.literal: In the first year of Shunzhi under the Shizu, after the regent Prince Rui Dorgon had secured Yanjing and was about in the tenth month to announce sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars of soil and grain, Grand Secretaries Feng Quan, Hong Chengchou, and others said: "For suburban, temple, and altars-of-soil-and-grain hymn titles, each former dynasty took an auspicious word to display the institutions of its age: Liang used 'Ya,' Northern Qi and Sui used 'Xia,' Tang used 'He,' Song used 'An,' Jin used 'Ning,' Yuan used 'Ning' for the ancestral temple and 'Xian' for suburban and altars, and the former Ming used 'He.
translations.idiomatic: In the Shizu's first year of Shunzhi, after the regent Prince Rui Dorgon had secured Yanjing and was to announce sacrifices to Heaven and Earth, the ancestral temple, and the altars of soil and grain that October, Grand Secretaries Feng Quan and Hong Chengchou said: "Suburban, temple, and soil-and-grain hymn titles each dynasty took from an auspicious word to mark its age: Liang used Ya, Northern Qi and Sui used Xia, Tang used He, Song used An, Jin used Ning, Yuan used Ning for the ancestral temple and Xian for suburban rites, and the Ming used He.

sentences.zh: 我朝削平寇亂，以有天下，宜改用『平』。

translations.literal: Our dynasty has cut down rebellion and disorder and thereby gained the realm; we should change to using "Ping."
translations.idiomatic: Our dynasty has quelled rebellion and gained the realm; we should adopt "Ping."

sentences.zh: 郊社九奏，宗廟六奏，社稷七奏。」

translations.literal: Suburban and altar rites: nine performances; ancestral temple: six performances; altars of soil and grain: seven performances."
translations.idiomatic: Suburban and altar rites should have nine performances, the ancestral temple six, and the altars of soil and grain seven."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was followed.
translations.idiomatic: This was adopted.

sentences.zh: 於是定圜丘大祀，皇帝出宮，午門聲鐘，不作樂。

translations.literal: Thereupon they fixed the great sacrifice at the Circular Mound: when the emperor left the palace, bells sounded at the Meridian Gate and no music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: They then fixed the great sacrifice at the Circular Mound: when the emperor left the palace, bells sounded at the Meridian Gate and no music was played.

sentences.zh: 致祭燔柴迎神奏始平，奠玉帛奏景平，進俎奏咸平，初獻奏壽平，亞獻奏嘉平，終獻奏雍平，徹饌奏熙平，送神奏太平，望燎奏安平。

translations.literal: At the sacrifice, burning firewood and welcoming the spirits: Shiping; presenting jade and silk: Jingping; presenting the offering tray: Xianping; first offering: Shouping; second offering: Jiaping; final offering: Yongping; withdrawing the feast: Xiping; sending off the spirits: Taiping; gazing at the burning: Anping.
translations.idiomatic: At the sacrifice: for burning firewood and welcoming the spirits, Shiping; for presenting jade and silk, Jingping; for presenting the offering tray, Xianping; for the first offering, Shouping; for the second, Jiaping; for the final, Yongping; for withdrawing the feast, Xiping; for sending off the spirits, Taiping; for gazing at the burning, Anping.

sentences.zh: 禮成，教坊司導迎，樂奏祐平。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, the Directorate of Ceremonial Music conducted the welcome and Youping was performed.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, the Directorate of Ceremonial Music conducted the welcome and performed Youping.

sentences.zh: 午門鐘作，還宮。

translations.literal: Bells sounded at the Meridian Gate, and he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Bells sounded at the Meridian Gate, and the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 方澤大祀，皇帝出宮，午門聲鐘，不作樂。

translations.literal: At the great sacrifice at the Square Mound, when the emperor left the palace, bells sounded at the Meridian Gate and no music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: At the great sacrifice at the Square Mound, when the emperor left the palace the Meridian Gate bells sounded and no music was played.

sentences.zh: 致祭瘞毛血迎神奏中平，奠玉帛奏廣平，進俎奏咸平，初獻奏壽平，亞獻奏安平，終獻奏時平，徹饌奏貞平，送神望瘞奏寧平。

translations.literal: At the sacrifice, burying fur and blood and welcoming the spirits: Zhongping; presenting jade and silk: Guangping; presenting the offering tray: Xianping; first offering: Shouping; second offering: Anping; final offering: Shiping; withdrawing the feast: Zhenping; sending off the spirits and gazing at the burial: Ningping.
translations.idiomatic: At the sacrifice: for burying fur and blood and welcoming the spirits, Zhongping; for presenting jade and silk, Guangping; for the offering tray, Xianping; for the first offering, Shouping; for the second, Anping; for the final, Shiping; for withdrawing the feast, Zhenping; for sending off the spirits and gazing at the burial, Ningping.

sentences.zh: 禮成，教坊司導迎，樂奏祐平。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, the Directorate conducted the welcome and Youping was performed.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, the Directorate conducted the welcome and performed Youping.

sentences.zh: 午門鐘作，還宮。

translations.literal: Bells sounded at the Meridian Gate, and he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: Bells sounded at the Meridian Gate, and the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 祈穀，皇帝出宮，午門聲鐘，不作樂。

translations.literal: For the Prayer for Grain, when the emperor left the palace, bells sounded at the Meridian Gate and no music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: For the Prayer for Grain, when the emperor left the palace the Meridian Gate bells sounded and no music was played.

sentences.zh: 燔柴迎神奏中平，奠玉帛奏肅平，進俎奏咸平，初獻奏壽平，亞獻奏景平，終獻奏永平，徹饌奏凝平，送神奏清平，望燎奏太平。

translations.literal: Burning firewood and welcoming the spirits: Zhongping; presenting jade and silk: Suping; presenting the offering tray: Xianping; first offering: Shouping; second offering: Jingping; final offering: Yongping; withdrawing the feast: Ningping; sending off the spirits: Qingping; gazing at the burning: Taiping.
translations.idiomatic: For burning firewood and welcoming the spirits, Zhongping; for presenting jade and silk, Suping; for the offering tray, Xianping; for the first offering, Shouping; for the second, Jingping; for the final, Yongping; for withdrawing the feast, Ningping; for sending off the spirits, Qingping; for gazing at the burning, Taiping.

sentences.zh: 餘與圜丘、方澤同。

translations.literal: The remainder was the same as for the Circular Mound and Square Mound.
translations.idiomatic: The remainder followed the Circular Mound and Square Mound rites.

sentences.zh: 太廟時享，皇帝出宮，鐘止，不作樂。

translations.literal: For seasonal offerings at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, when the emperor left the palace the bells ceased and no music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: For seasonal offerings at the Imperial Ancestral Temple, when the emperor left the palace the bells stopped and no music was played.

sentences.zh: 致祭迎神奏開平，奠帛初獻奏壽平，亞獻奏嘉平，終獻奏雍平，徹饌奏熙平，送神望燎奏成平。

translations.literal: At the sacrifice, welcoming the spirits: Kaiping; presenting silk and first offering: Shouping; second offering: Jiaping; final offering: Yongping; withdrawing the feast: Xiping; sending off the spirits and gazing at the burning: Chengping.
translations.idiomatic: At the sacrifice: for welcoming the spirits, Kaiping; for presenting silk and the first offering, Shouping; for the second, Jiaping; for the final, Yongping; for withdrawing the feast, Xiping; for sending off the spirits and gazing at the burning, Chengping.

sentences.zh: 禮成，教坊司導迎奏禧平，聲鐘還宮。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, the Directorate conducted the welcome and performed Xiping; bells sounded as he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, the Directorate conducted the welcome and performed Xiping; bells sounded as the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 社稷壇，皇帝出宮，聲鐘，不作樂。

translations.literal: At the altars of soil and grain, when the emperor left the palace, bells sounded and no music was performed.
translations.idiomatic: At the altars of soil and grain, when the emperor left the palace bells sounded and no music was played.

sentences.zh: 致祭瘞毛血迎神奏廣平，奠玉帛初獻奏壽平，亞獻奏嘉平，終獻奏雍平，徹饌奏熙平，送神望瘞奏成平。

translations.literal: At the sacrifice, burying fur and blood and welcoming the spirits: Guangping; presenting jade and silk and first offering: Shouping; second offering: Jiaping; final offering: Yongping; withdrawing the feast: Xiping; sending off the spirits and gazing at the burial: Chengping.
translations.idiomatic: At the sacrifice: for burying fur and blood and welcoming the spirits, Guangping; for presenting jade and silk and the first offering, Shouping; for the second, Jiaping; for the final, Yongping; for withdrawing the feast, Xiping; for sending off the spirits and gazing at the burial, Chengping.

sentences.zh: 禮成，教坊司導迎奏祐平，聲鐘還宮。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, the Directorate conducted the welcome and performed Youping; bells sounded as he returned to the palace.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, the Directorate conducted the welcome and performed Youping; bells sounded as the emperor returned to the palace.

sentences.zh: 舞皆八佾，初獻武舞，亞獻、終獻文舞，文武舞生各六十四人，執干戚羽籥於樂懸之次，引舞旌節四，舞生四人司之。

translations.literal: All dances used eight rows; at the first offering the martial dance, at the second and final offerings the civil dance; martial and civil dancers numbered sixty-four each, holding shields, axes, feathers, and flutes beside the bell-frame; four dance banners and staffs for leading the dance, managed by four dancers.
translations.idiomatic: All dances used eight rows; the first offering used the martial dance, the second and final the civil dance. Martial and civil dancers numbered sixty-four each, holding shields, axes, feathers, and flutes beside the bell-frame; four leading banners and staffs were managed by four dancers.

sentences.zh: 祭之日，初獻樂作，司樂執旌節，引武舞生執干戚進，奏武功之舞。

translations.literal: On the day of sacrifice, when the music for the first offering began, the director of music held the banner and staff, led in the martial dancers bearing shields and axes, and performed the dance of martial achievement.
translations.idiomatic: On the day of sacrifice, when the first-offering music began, the director of music held the banner and staff, led in martial dancers bearing shields and axes, and performed the dance of martial achievement.

sentences.zh: 亞獻、終獻樂作，司樂執旌節，引文舞生執羽籥進，奏文德之舞。

translations.literal: When the music for the second and final offerings began, the director held the banner and staff, led in the civil dancers bearing feathers and flutes, and performed the dance of civil virtue.
translations.idiomatic: When the second- and final-offering music began, the director held the banner and staff, led in civil dancers bearing feathers and flutes, and performed the dance of civil virtue.

sentences.zh: 惟先師廟祗文舞六佾。

translations.literal: Only at the temple of the Former Master was the civil dance alone performed in six rows.
translations.idiomatic: Only at the temple of the Former Master was the civil dance alone performed in six rows.

sentences.zh: 其三大節、常朝及皇帝升殿、還宮，俱奏中和韶樂，群臣行禮，奏丹陛大樂。

translations.literal: For the three great festivals, regular court audiences, and when the emperor ascended or left the hall, Harmonious Central Shao music was performed throughout; when the ministers performed rites, the Great Music of the Cinnabar Steps was played.
translations.idiomatic: For the three great festivals, regular court audiences, and when the emperor ascended or left the hall, Harmonious Central Shao music was played throughout; when ministers performed rites, the Great Music of the Cinnabar Steps was used.

sentences.zh: 親祭壇廟，乘輿出入，用導迎樂，樂章均用「平」字。

translations.literal: When the emperor personally sacrificed at altars and temples and entered or left by imperial carriage, conducting and welcoming music was used; all hymn titles used the character "ping".
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor personally sacrificed at altars and temples and entered or left by carriage, conducting music was used, and all hymn titles used the character "ping".

sentences.zh: 宴享清樂，則以樂詞之首為章名。

translations.literal: For banquet clear music, the opening words of the song text served as the title of the piece.
translations.idiomatic: For banquet clear music, the opening words of the lyric served as the title of the piece.

sentences.zh: 是年世祖至京行受寶禮，先期錦衣衛設鹵簿儀仗，旗手衛設金鼓旗幟，教坊司設大樂於行殿西前導。

translations.literal: That year, when the Shizu came to the capital to perform the ceremony of receiving the imperial seal, beforehand the Embroidered-Uniform Guard set out the guard of honor, the Banner-Bearer Guard set out golden drums and flags, and the Directorate of Ceremonial Music placed great music west of the traveling hall to conduct ahead.
translations.idiomatic: That year, when the Shizu came to the capital for the ceremony of receiving the imperial seal, the Embroidered-Uniform Guard beforehand set out the guard of honor, the Banner-Bearer Guard set out golden drums and flags, and the Directorate placed great music west of the traveling hall to lead the procession.

sentences.zh: 時龜鼎初奠，官懸備物，未遑潤色，沿明舊制雜用之。

translations.literal: At the time the tortoise tripod had only just been set in place and the court bell-sets and vessels were in readiness; there was no leisure to refine them, and Ming institutions were mixed in for use.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the tortoise tripod had only just been set in place and the court instruments were in readiness; there was no leisure to refine them, and Ming practice was mixed in for use.

sentences.zh: 教坊司置奉鑾一人，左右韶舞各一人，協同官十有五人，俳長二十人，色長十七人，歌工九十八人。

translations.literal: The Directorate appointed one bearer of the imperial music carriage, one Shao dancer to the left and one to the right, fifteen coordinating officials, twenty leaders of comic performers, seventeen leaders of variety acts, and ninety-eight singing artisans.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate appointed one bearer of the imperial music carriage, one Shao dancer to the left and one to the right, fifteen coordinating officials, twenty leaders of comic performers, seventeen leaders of variety acts, and ninety-eight singing artisans.

sentences.zh: 宮內宴禮，領樂官妻四人，領教坊女樂二十四人。

translations.literal: For palace banquet rites, four wives of music officials led, and twenty-four female musicians of the Directorate led.
translations.idiomatic: For palace banquets, four wives of music officials and twenty-four female musicians of the Directorate led the performance.

sentences.zh: 祠祭諸樂，則太常寺神樂觀司之。

translations.literal: Music for temple sacrifices was managed by the Temple of Divine Music under the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Music for temple sacrifices was managed by the Temple of Divine Music under the Court of Imperial Sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 以協律郎教習樂生，月三、六、九日演於凝禧殿。

translations.literal: Pitch-pipe masters instructed music students, who performed on the third, sixth, and ninth days of each month in the Hall of Concentrated Felicity.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch masters instructed music students, who performed on the third, sixth, and ninth days of each month in the Hall of Concentrated Felicity.

sentences.zh: 二年，從有司言，春秋上丁釋奠先師，樂六奏，迎神奏咸平，奠帛初獻奏寧平，亞獻奏安平，終獻奏景平，徹饌送神奏咸平。

translations.literal: In the second year, following the relevant offices, for the spring and autumn upper ding libation sacrifices to the Former Master, music was performed in six parts: welcoming the spirits, Xianping; presenting silk and first offering, Ningping; second offering, Anping; final offering, Jingping; withdrawing the feast and sending off the spirits, Xianping.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year, following the relevant offices, for the spring and autumn upper ding sacrifices to Confucius, six musical performances were prescribed: for welcoming the spirits, Xianping; for presenting silk and the first offering, Ningping; for the second, Anping; for the final, Jingping; for withdrawing the feast and sending off the spirits, Xianping.

sentences.zh: 祭歷代帝王樂六奏，迎神奏雍平，奠帛初獻奏安平，亞獻奏中平，終獻奏肅平，徹饌奏凝平，送神望燎奏壽平。

translations.literal: For sacrifice to the emperors of successive dynasties, six performances: welcoming the spirits, Yongping; presenting silk and first offering, Anping; second offering, Zhongping; final offering, Suping; withdrawing the feast, Ningping; sending off the spirits and gazing at the burning, Shouping.
translations.idiomatic: For sacrifice to the emperors of successive dynasties, six performances: for welcoming the spirits, Yongping; for presenting silk and the first offering, Anping; for the second, Zhongping; for the final, Suping; for withdrawing the feast, Ningping; for sending off the spirits and gazing at the burning, Shouping.

sentences.zh: 八年，制：朝日七奏，樂章用「曦」，迎神奏寅曦，奠玉帛奏朝曦，初獻奏清曦，亞獻奏咸曦，終獻奏純曦，徹饌奏延曦，送神奏歸曦。

translations.literal: In the eighth year regulations were made: for the Morning Sun, seven performances with hymn titles using "xi": welcoming the spirits, Yinxii; presenting jade and silk, Chaoxi; first offering, Qingxi; second offering, Xianxi; final offering, Chunxi; withdrawing the feast, Yanxi; sending off the spirits, Guixi.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year regulations were made: for the Morning Sun rite, seven performances with hymn titles using "xi": for welcoming the spirits, Yinxii; for presenting jade and silk, Chaoxi; for the first offering, Qingxi; for the second, Xianxi; for the final, Chunxi; for withdrawing the feast, Yanxi; for sending off the spirits, Guixi.

sentences.zh: 夕月六奏，樂章用「光」，迎神奏迎光，奠玉帛初獻奏升光，亞獻奏瑤光，終獻奏瑞光，徹饌奏涵光，送神奏保光，皆中和韶樂。

translations.literal: For the Evening Moon, six performances with hymn titles using "guang": welcoming the spirits, Yingguang; presenting jade and silk and first offering, Shengguang; second offering, Yaoguang; final offering, Ruiguang; withdrawing the feast, Hanguang; sending off the spirits, Baoguang—all Harmonious Central Shao music.
translations.idiomatic: For the Evening Moon, six performances with hymn titles using "guang": for welcoming the spirits, Yingguang; for presenting jade and silk and the first offering, Shengguang; for the second, Yaoguang; for the final, Ruiguang; for withdrawing the feast, Hanguang; for sending off the spirits, Baoguang—all Harmonious Central Shao music.

sentences.zh: 皇太后、皇后三大節慶賀，皇帝大婚行禮，皆丹陛大樂。

translations.literal: Congratulations on the three great festivals of the Empress Dowager and Empress, and the emperor's grand wedding ceremony, all used the Great Music of the Cinnabar Steps.
translations.idiomatic: Congratulations on the three great festivals of the Empress Dowager and Empress, and the emperor's grand wedding ceremony, all used the Great Music of the Cinnabar Steps.

sentences.zh: 祭真武、東嶽、城隍廟，教坊司作樂如群祀。

translations.literal: Sacrifices at the temples of the Perfected Warrior, the Eastern Peak, and the City God were performed with music by the Directorate as for group sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Sacrifices at the temples of the Perfected Warrior, the Eastern Peak, and the City God used music by the Directorate as for other group sacrifices.

sentences.zh: 是年又允禮部請，更定樂舞、樂章、樂器之數，享廟大樂於殿內奏之，文武佾舞備列樂章卒歌樂器俱設，補舞生舊額五百七十人。

translations.literal: That year the Ministry of Rites' request was also approved to revise the numbers of dances, hymn pieces, and instruments; great temple music was performed inside the hall; martial and civil row-dances were fully arranged, hymn texts, concluding songs, and instruments all provided; and five hundred seventy dance students were added to the former quota.
translations.idiomatic: That year the Ministry of Rites' request was also approved to revise the numbers of dances, hymns, and instruments; great temple music was performed inside the hall; martial and civil dances were fully arranged with hymns, concluding songs, and instruments all provided; and five hundred seventy dance students were added to the former quota.

sentences.zh: 其後又定常朝升殿中和韶樂奏隆平，王公百官行禮丹陛大樂奏慶平，外籓行禮丹陛大樂奏治平，還宮中和韶樂奏顯平。

translations.literal: Later they further fixed that at regular court audiences, upon ascending the hall Harmonious Central Shao music performed Longping; when princes, dukes, and the hundred officials performed rites, the Great Music of the Cinnabar Steps performed Qingping; when foreign tributaries performed rites, the Great Music performed Zhiping; upon returning to the palace, Harmonious Central Shao performed Xianping.
translations.idiomatic: Later they further fixed that at regular court audiences, upon ascending the hall Harmonious Central Shao played Longping; when princes, dukes, and officials performed rites, the Cinnabar Steps music played Qingping; when foreign tributaries performed rites, it played Zhiping; upon returning to the palace, Harmonious Central Shao played Xianping.

sentences.zh: 耤田饗先農，樂章七奏，用「豐」，迎神奏永豐，奠帛初獻奏時豐，亞獻奏咸豐，終獻奏大豐，徹饌奏屢豐，送神奏報豐，望瘞奏慶豐。

translations.literal: At the plowing field and feast to the God of Agriculture, seven hymn performances using "feng": welcoming the spirits, Yongfeng; presenting silk and first offering, Shifeng; second offering, Xianfeng; final offering, Dafeng; withdrawing the feast, Lüfeng; sending off the spirits, Baofeng; gazing at the burial, Qingfeng.
translations.idiomatic: At the plowing field and feast to the God of Agriculture, seven hymn performances using "feng": for welcoming the spirits, Yongfeng; for presenting silk and the first offering, Shifeng; for the second, Xianfeng; for the final, Dafeng; for withdrawing the feast, Lüfeng; for sending off the spirits, Baofeng; for gazing at the burial, Qingfeng.

sentences.zh: 禮成，御齋宮，導迎大樂奏天下樂，升座奏萬歲樂，群臣行禮丹陛大樂奏朝天子，筵宴上壽奏三月韶光，進饌清樂奏太清歌。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, he proceeded to the fasting palace; conducting music performed Tianxia Yue; upon taking the seat, Wansui Yue; when the ministers performed rites, the Great Music performed Chao Tianzi; at the banquet offering longevity wishes, Sanyue Shaoguang; when dishes were brought in, clear music performed Taiqing Ge.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite was complete, the emperor proceeded to the fasting palace; conducting music played Tianxia Yue; upon taking the seat, Wansui Yue; when ministers performed rites, the Cinnabar Steps music played Chao Tianzi; at the banquet offering longevity wishes, Sanyue Shaoguang; when dishes were served, clear music played Taiqing Ge.

sentences.zh: 太廟祫祭迎神奏貞平，奠帛初獻奏壽平，亞獻奏嘉平，終獻奏雍平，徹饌奏熙平，送神奏清平。

translations.literal: For the year-end joint sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple: welcoming the spirits, Zhenping; presenting silk and first offering, Shouping; second offering, Jiaping; final offering, Yongping; withdrawing the feast, Xiping; sending off the spirits, Qingping.
translations.idiomatic: For the year-end joint sacrifice at the Imperial Ancestral Temple: for welcoming the spirits, Zhenping; for presenting silk and the first offering, Shouping; for the second, Jiaping; for the final, Yongping; for withdrawing the feast, Xiping; for sending off the spirits, Qingping.

sentences.zh: 大享殿合祀天地百神，樂章九奏，用「和」，迎神奏元和，奠玉帛奏景和，進俎奏肅和，初獻奏壽和，亞獻奏安和，終獻奏永和，徹饌奏協和，送神奏泰和，望燎瘞奏清和。

translations.literal: At the Hall of Great Enjoyment, where Heaven and Earth and the hundred spirits were jointly sacrificed to, nine hymn performances using "he": welcoming the spirits, Yuanhe; presenting jade and silk, Jinghe; presenting the offering tray, Suhe; first offering, Shouhe; second offering, Anhe; final offering, Yonghe; withdrawing the feast, Xiehe; sending off the spirits, Taihe; gazing at the burning and burial, Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: At the Hall of Great Enjoyment, where Heaven and Earth and the hundred spirits were jointly sacrificed to, nine hymn performances using "he": for welcoming the spirits, Yuanhe; for presenting jade and silk, Jinghe; for the offering tray, Suhe; for the first offering, Shouhe; for the second, Anhe; for the final, Yonghe; for withdrawing the feast, Xiehe; for sending off the spirits, Taihe; for gazing at the burning and burial, Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 其上皇太后徽號冊寶、尊封太妃、冊立中宮、太和殿策士諸慶典，皆特詔用樂。

translations.literal: Above these: the empress dowager's honorific title, seals and credentials; honoring and enfeoffing imperial consorts; establishing the empress; the palace examination at the Hall of Supreme Harmony and other celebratory ceremonies—all were specially decreed to use music.
translations.idiomatic: Beyond those occasions, presenting the empress dowager's honorific title and regalia, ennobling imperial consorts, investing the empress, the palace examination at the Hall of Supreme Harmony, and other state celebrations all required special imperial edicts mandating music.

sentences.zh: 自後幸盛京、謁陵，進實錄、玉牒亦如之。

translations.literal: Afterward, imperial visits to Shengjing, tomb visits, and presenting the veritable records and jade genealogy were likewise [so treated].
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, imperial tours to Shengjing, visits to the imperial tombs, and the presentation of the veritable records and jade genealogy were handled the same way.

sentences.zh: 康熙初，聖祖踐阼幼沖，率承舊憲，無所改作。

translations.literal: Early in the Kangxi reign, the Sage Ancestor ascended the throne in his minority, generally inheriting the old statutes, with nothing revised or created anew.
translations.idiomatic: In the early Kangxi years the Sage Ancestor came to the throne as a minor and, for the most part, followed existing regulations without instituting reforms.

sentences.zh: 八年，惟詔定皇帝、太皇太后、皇太后、皇后三大節朝賀樂，皇帝元旦升座中和韶樂奏元平，還宮奏和平，冬至升座奏遂平，還宮奏允平，萬壽節升座奏乾平，還宮奏太平，群臣行禮丹陛大樂奏慶平，外籓奏治平，太皇太后升座奏昇平，還宮奏恆平，行禮奏晉平，皇太后升座奏豫平，還宮奏履平，行禮奏益平，皇后升座奏淑平，還宮奏順平，行禮奏正平。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, only an edict fixed the congratulatory music for the emperor, grand empress dowager, empress dowager, and empress on the three great festivals: on New Year's Day when the emperor took his seat, the Zhonghe shaoyue played Yuanping; on returning to the palace, Heping; on the winter solstice when taking his seat, Suiping; on returning, Yunping; on the Longevity Festival when taking his seat, Qianping; on returning, Taiping; when the ministers performed rites on the crimson steps, the great hall music played Qingping; for foreign tributaries, Zhiping; when the grand empress dowager took her seat, Shengping; on returning, Hengping; when performing rites, Jinping; when the empress dowager took her seat, Yuping; on returning, Lüping; when performing rites, Yiping; when the empress took her seat, Shuping; on returning, Shunping; when performing rites, Zhengping.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year an edict alone defined the court congratulatory music for the emperor, grand empress dowager, empress dowager, and empress on the three great festivals. On New Year's Day the emperor's ascent was accompanied by Yuanping in the Zhonghe shaoyue, and Heping on his return to the palace; at the winter solstice, Suiping on ascent and Yunping on return; on the Longevity Festival, Qianping on ascent and Taiping on return. Ministers' obeisance on the crimson steps used Qingping in the great hall music, tributary envoys Zhiping, the grand empress dowager Shengping on ascent and Hengping on return with Jinping for the rite, the empress dowager Yuping and Lüping with Yiping for the rite, and the empress Shuping and Shunping with Zhengping for the rite.

sentences.zh: 而有司肄習日久，樂句律度，凌厲失所，伶倫應官，比於制氏，但紀鏗鏘鼓舞而已。

translations.literal: Yet because the responsible officials had drilled for so long, the phrasing of musical lines and pitch standards had surged past their proper places and been lost; the music officers of the Bureau of Music, compared to the Music Master lineage, merely recorded clangorous sounds and drum-and-dance beating, nothing more.
translations.idiomatic: Over time, however, the officials charged with practice had drilled so long that melodic phrasing and pitch standards had drifted out of alignment. The Bureau of Music officers, like successors to the ancient Music Master, recorded little more than clashing tones and the beat of drums and dance.

sentences.zh: 自世祖時，已屢飭典樂官演習樂舞聲容儀節，嘗諭大學士等曰：「各處祭祀，太常寺所奏樂俱未和諧。

translations.literal: From the Shizu reign onward, [the court] had repeatedly ordered the directors of ritual music to drill in music, dance, sound, bearing, and ceremonial deportment, and once instructed the grand secretaries and others, saying: "At sacrifices throughout the realm, the music performed by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices is all out of harmony.
translations.idiomatic: Already under the Shizu Emperor the court had repeatedly ordered directors of ritual music to rehearse music, dance, sound, bearing, and ceremonial form. He once told the grand secretaries and others, "At sacrifices everywhere, the music performed by the Court of Imperial Sacrifices is still not harmonious.

sentences.zh: 樂乃祭祀之大典，必聲容儀節盡合歌章，始臻美善。

translations.literal: Music is the great ceremony of sacrifice; only when sound, bearing, and ceremonial deportment fully accord with the hymn texts does it reach true excellence.
translations.idiomatic: Music is a cardinal element of sacrifice. Only when sound, bearing, and ritual deportment fully match the hymn texts does the rite attain its proper beauty.

sentences.zh: 其召太常寺官嚴飭之。」

translations.literal: Summon the officials of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and strictly admonish them."
translations.idiomatic: Summon the Court of Imperial Sacrifices officials and discipline them strictly."

sentences.zh: 至十一年，聖祖亦諭禮臣：「慎重禋祀，勤加習練，勿仍前怠，褻越明典。」

translations.literal: By the eleventh year the Sage Ancestor also instructed the ritual officials: "Treat the solemn sacrifices with care, drill diligently, do not persist in former negligence, and do not profane the enlightened statutes."
translations.idiomatic: By the eleventh year the Sage Ancestor likewise admonished the ritual officials: "Honor the great sacrifices, practice diligently, do not lapse into past negligence, and do not violate the enlightened regulations."

sentences.zh: 二十一年，三籓削平，天下無事，左副都御史余國柱首請釐正郊廟、朝賀、宴享樂章，上曰：「享祀樂章，一代製作所繫，禮部、翰林院其集議以聞。」

translations.literal: In the twenty-first year, after the Three Feudatories were pacified and the realm was at peace, the left vice censor-in-chief Yu Guozhu was first to request rectification of the hymn texts for suburban sacrifice, ancestral temple, court congratulation, and banquet music. The emperor said: "Sacrificial hymn texts are bound up with a dynasty's creative work; let the Ministry of Rites and the Hanlin Academy assemble for deliberation and report."
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-first year, with the Three Feudatories subdued and the empire at peace, Left Vice Censor-in-Chief Yu Guozhu was the first to ask that hymn texts for suburban rites, ancestral temples, court congratulations, and banquets be corrected. The emperor replied, "Sacrificial hymns concern a dynasty's own cultural creation. Let the Ministry of Rites and Hanlin Academy deliberate together and report to me."

sentences.zh: 尋奏：「自古廟樂，原以頌述祖宗功德，本朝郊壇廟祀樂章，曲名曰『平』，遵奉已久。

translations.literal: Shortly afterward they memorialized: "Since antiquity temple music has served to praise and recount the achievements and virtue of the ancestors. In our dynasty the hymn texts for suburban altars and temple sacrifices, with tune names of 'ping,' have long been observed.
translations.idiomatic: Soon after they submitted a memorial: "Temple music has always existed to praise the achievements and virtue of the ancestors. In our dynasty the hymns for suburban altars and temple sacrifices, whose tune titles use ping, have been followed for a long time.

sentences.zh: 太祖、太宗、世祖同於太廟致祭，宜如舊。

translations.literal: The Taizu, Taizong, and Shizu are jointly sacrificed to in the Imperial Ancestral Temple; this should remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: Taizu, Taizong, and Shizu are worshipped together in the Imperial Ancestral Temple and should remain unchanged.

sentences.zh: 惟朝會、宴享等樂曲調，風雅未備，宜敕所司酌古准今，求聲律之原，定雅奏之節。」

translations.literal: Only the melodies for court assemblies, banquets, and the like lack full elegance; the responsible offices should be ordered to weigh antiquity against the present, seek the origins of pitch and mode, and fix the measures of refined performance."
translations.idiomatic: Only the melodies for court assemblies and banquets still lack full refinement. The responsible offices should be ordered to balance past models with present needs, recover the foundations of pitch and mode, and establish standards for elegant performance."

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: The request was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved.

sentences.zh: 因命大學士陳廷敬重撰燕樂諸章，然猶襲明故，雖務典蔚，有似徒歌，五聲二變，踵訛奪倫，黃鍾為萬事根本，臣工無能言之者。

translations.literal: Thereupon Grand Secretary Chen Tingjing was ordered to redraft the banquet-music hymns, yet they still followed Ming precedents; though striving for classical dignity, they resembled mere unaccompanied song. The five tones and two alterations perpetuated errors and usurped proper order, and though the yellow bell is the root of all affairs, no minister could speak to it.
translations.idiomatic: The court then ordered Grand Secretary Chen Tingjing to rewrite the banquet hymns, but the work still followed Ming precedents. Though written in a lofty classical style, the result resembled plain chanting. The five tones and two alterations continued to perpetuate errors and disorder, and although the yellow bell is the foundation of all things, no official could explain it.

sentences.zh: 帝方謙讓，亦未暇革也。

translations.literal: The emperor was then modest and yielding, and had no leisure to reform it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was still modest by temperament and had no time to undertake reform.

sentences.zh: 二十三年，東巡謁闕裡，躬祭孔林，陳鹵簿，奏導迎大樂樂章、樂舞，先期命太常寺遣司樂官前往肄習，與太學先師廟同。

translations.literal: In the twenty-third year, on the eastern tour to pay homage at Qufu, he personally sacrificed at the Kong Forest, deployed the honor guard, and performed the guiding and welcoming great music hymns and dances; beforehand he ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to send music officers ahead to drill, the same as at the Temple of the First Teacher in the Imperial Academy.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-third year, on his eastern tour to Qufu he personally sacrificed at the Kong Forest, deployed the honor guard, and performed the guiding and welcoming great music with its hymns and dances. In advance he ordered the Court of Imperial Sacrifices to send music officers to rehearse there, as at the Temple of the First Teacher in the Imperial Academy.

sentences.zh: 二十九年，以喀爾喀新附，特行會閱禮，陳鹵簿，奏鐃歌大樂，於是帝感禮樂崩隤，始有志製作之事。

translations.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, because the Khalkha had newly submitted, a special grand review ceremony was held, the honor guard was deployed, and the nao-song great music was performed; thereupon the emperor felt that ritual and music had collapsed, and first resolved to undertake creative work.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-ninth year, with the Khalkha newly submitted, the court held a special grand military review, deployed the honor guard, and performed the nao-song great music. The emperor then felt keenly that ritual and music had fallen into ruin and first resolved to undertake a program of restoration.

sentences.zh: 三十一年，御乾清宮，召大學士九卿前，指五聲八風圖示之曰：「古人謂十二律定，而後被之八音，則八音和，奏之天地，則八風和，諸福之物，可致之祥，無不畢至，言樂律所關者大也。

translations.literal: In the thirty-first year, at the Palace of Heavenly Purity he summoned the grand secretaries and the nine chief ministers before him, pointed to the diagram of the five tones and eight winds, and showed them, saying: "The ancients said that once the twelve pitch pipes are fixed and then applied to the eight kinds of sound, the eight sounds harmonize; when performed to Heaven and Earth, the eight winds harmonize, and the things of blessing and attainable auspice all arrive without exception—thus showing how great a matter pitch and mode concern.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-first year, at the Palace of Heavenly Purity he summoned the grand secretaries and nine chief ministers, pointed to the diagram of the five tones and eight winds, and said, "The ancients held that once the twelve pitch pipes are established and applied to the eight kinds of sound, those sounds harmonize; performed to Heaven and Earth, the eight winds harmonize, and every blessing and attainable auspice arrives without fail. That shows how vast the stakes of music and pitch truly are.

sentences.zh: 而十二律之所從出，其義不可知。

translations.literal: Yet the meaning of how the twelve pitch pipes arise cannot be known.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the principle by which the twelve pitch pipes arise remains unknowable.

sentences.zh: 律呂新書所言算數，專用徑一圍三之法，此法若合，則所算皆合；

translations.literal: The calculations in the New Book on Pitch Pipes rely exclusively on the method of diameter one and circumference three; if this method is correct, then all calculations are correct;
translations.idiomatic: The calculations in the New Book on Pitch Pipes rely entirely on the method of taking the diameter as one and the circumference as three. If that method is correct, every calculation follows;

sentences.zh: 若舛，則無所不舛矣。

translations.literal: if it is wrong, then nothing is not wrong.
translations.idiomatic: if it is wrong, nothing downstream can be right.

sentences.zh: 朕觀徑一圍三之法，必不能合，蓋徑一尺，則圍當三尺一寸四分一釐有奇，若積累至於百丈，所差當十四丈有奇，等而上之，舛錯可勝言耶？」

translations.literal: I observe that the method of diameter one and circumference three certainly cannot accord: for a diameter of one foot, the circumference should be three feet, one inch, four fen, one li and a fraction; if accumulated to a hundred zhang, the discrepancy would be more than fourteen zhang; extrapolating upward, can the errors even be fully described?"
translations.idiomatic: I see that the diameter-one, circumference-three method cannot possibly hold. For a diameter of one foot the circumference should be three feet, one inch, four fen, one li and a fraction more. Accumulated to a hundred zhang, the error would exceed fourteen zhang. Extrapolated further, the mistakes become beyond reckoning."

sentences.zh: 因取方圓諸圖謂群臣曰：「所言徑一圍三，但可算六角之數，若圍圓必有奇零。

translations.literal: He then took out diagrams of square and circle and said to the ministers: "What is called diameter one and circumference three can only calculate hexagonal figures; if the circumference is truly round, there must be a remainder.
translations.idiomatic: He then produced diagrams of squares and circles and told the ministers, "The so-called diameter-one, circumference-three ratio can only calculate hexagonal approximations. A true circle must leave a remainder.

sentences.zh: 朕觀八線表中半徑句股之法極精微，凡圓者可以方算，開方之術，即從此出。

translations.literal: I observe that the method of half-radius right triangles in the eight-line tables is extremely refined: whatever is round can be calculated by square methods, and the technique of extracting roots proceeds from this.
translations.idiomatic: The half-radius right-triangle method in the eight-line tables is extraordinarily precise. Every circle can be treated through square geometry, and root extraction proceeds from that foundation.

sentences.zh: 若黃鍾之管九寸，空圍九分，積八百一十分，是為律本，此舊說也。

translations.literal: As for the yellow bell pipe of nine inches, inner circumference nine fen, volume eight hundred and ten fen—that is taken as the pitch foundation; this is the old doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: The old doctrine holds that the yellow bell pipe is nine inches long, with an inner circumference of nine fen and a volume of eight hundred and ten fen, and that this constitutes the foundation of pitch.

sentences.zh: 其分寸若以尺言，則古今尺制不同，當以天地之度數為准。

translations.literal: If its inches and fen are spoken of in terms of the foot-rule, then ancient and modern foot measures differ; one should take the degrees of Heaven and Earth as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: If one measures those inches and fen by the foot-rule, ancient and modern scales differ. The standard must be the celestial and terrestrial measures themselves.

sentences.zh: 惟隔八相生之說，聲音高下，循環相生，復還本音，必須隔八，乃一定之理也。」

translations.literal: Only the doctrine of generation by skipping eight: pitch high and low, generating one another in cycle and returning to the original tone—one must skip eight; this is a fixed principle."
translations.idiomatic: As for generation by skipping eight tones: pitches rise and fall, beget one another in cycle, and return to the original note. The interval of eight is a fixed law."

sentences.zh: 隨命樂人取笛和瑟次第審音，至第八聲，仍還本音。

translations.literal: He then ordered musicians to take the flute and zither and examine the tones in sequence; at the eighth tone it still returned to the original pitch.
translations.idiomatic: He then ordered musicians to test the flute and zither tone by tone. At the eighth tone the pitch returned to the original note.

sentences.zh: 上曰：「此非隔八相生之義耶？」

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Is this not the meaning of generation by skipping eight?"
translations.idiomatic: The emperor asked, "Is this not exactly the principle of generation by skipping eight?"

sentences.zh: 群臣皆曰：「誠如聖訓，非臣等聞見所及。」

translations.literal: All the ministers said: "It is truly as Your sagely instruction states; this lies beyond what we have heard or seen."
translations.idiomatic: All the ministers replied, "It is exactly as Your Majesty teaches. This lies beyond our own hearing and understanding."

sentences.zh: 三十四年，定大閱鳴角擊鼓聲金之制。

translations.literal: In the thirty-fourth year, the regulations for sounding horns, beating drums, and clashing metal at the grand review were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-fourth year the court fixed the regulations for horns, drums, and gongs at the grand military review.

sentences.zh: 四十九年正月，孝惠章皇后七十萬壽，又諭禮部曰：「瑪克式舞，乃滿洲筵宴大禮，典至隆重，故事皆王大臣行之。

translations.literal: In the first month of the forty-ninth year, on the seventieth birthday of Empress Xiaohuizhang, he again instructed the Ministry of Rites: "The maikeshi dance is the great Manchu banquet ceremony, a rite of utmost solemnity; by precedent it was always performed by princes and great ministers.
translations.idiomatic: In the first month of the forty-ninth year, on Empress Xiaohuizhang's seventieth birthday, he again told the Ministry of Rites, "The maikeshi dance is the great Manchu banquet ceremony, a rite of the highest solemnity. By precedent princes and senior ministers always performed it.

sentences.zh: 今歲皇太后七旬大慶，朕亦五十有七，欲親舞稱觴。」

translations.literal: This year, on the great celebration of the empress dowager's seventh decade, I too am fifty-seven, and wish personally to dance and raise the cup in toast."
translations.idiomatic: This year, at the grand celebration of the empress dowager's seventieth year, I too am fifty-seven and wish to dance in person and raise the toast cup."

sentences.zh: 是日皇太后宮進宴奏樂，上前舞蹈奉爵，極懽乃罷。

translations.literal: On that day a banquet was presented at the empress dowager's palace with music performed; the emperor advanced, danced, and presented the wine cup, and only when joy reached its height did it end.
translations.idiomatic: That day a banquet with music was held at the empress dowager's palace. The emperor advanced, danced, and presented the wine cup, and the celebration ended only when merriment had reached its height.

sentences.zh: 帝既妙揅鍾律，時李光地為文淵閣大學士，以耆碩被顧問，會進所纂大司樂釋義及樂律論辨，因上言曰：「禮樂不可斯臾去身，亦不可以一日不行於天下。

translations.literal: The emperor had already mastered pitch and bell with subtle skill. At that time Li Guangdi was grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion and, as a venerable elder, was consulted; he happened to present his compiled Explanations of the Grand Director of Music and Discussions on Musical Pitch, and thereupon memorialized, saying: "Ritual and music cannot for a moment be removed from the person, nor can they fail to be practiced in the realm for a single day.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor had already attained subtle mastery of bells and pitch. Li Guangdi, then grand secretary of the Wenyuan Pavilion, was consulted as a venerable elder and presented his compiled Explanations of the Grand Director of Music and Discussions on Musical Pitch. He memorialized, "Ritual and music cannot be separated from the person even for a moment, nor can they cease to operate throughout the realm for even a day.

sentences.zh: 自漢以來，禮樂崩壞，不合於三代之意者二千餘年，而樂尤甚。

translations.literal: From the Han onward, ritual and music have collapsed; for more than two thousand years they have not accorded with the intent of the Three Dynasties, and music has suffered especially.
translations.idiomatic: Since the Han, ritual and music have been in ruin. For more than two thousand years they have failed to match the spirit of the Three Dynasties, and music has suffered most of all.

sentences.zh: 蓋自諸經所載節奏、篇章、器數、律呂之昭然者，而紛紛之說，終不能以相一，又況乎精微之旨，與天地同其和者哉！

translations.literal: Even for what is clearly set forth in the classics—rhythm, hymn texts, numbers of instruments, pitch pipes—conflicting doctrines in the end cannot be unified into one, how much less the subtle principle that shares harmony with Heaven and Earth!
translations.idiomatic: Even where the classics plainly record rhythm, hymn texts, instrument counts, and pitch pipes, competing doctrines still cannot be reconciled. How much less can anyone grasp the subtle principle that shares harmony with Heaven and Earth!

sentences.zh: 今四海靡靡，風聲頹敝，等威無辨，而奢僭不可止；

translations.literal: Now within the four seas all is dissolute, custom and reputation decayed, ranks and insignia undistinguished, yet extravagance and usurpation cannot be stopped;
translations.idiomatic: Today the four seas are adrift, customs decayed, ranks and insignia blurred, yet extravagance and presumption cannot be checked;

sentences.zh: 聯屬無法，而斗爭不可禁。

translations.literal: connections lack regulation, yet strife cannot be forbidden.
translations.idiomatic: social bonds lack proper form, yet conflict cannot be restrained.

sentences.zh: 記曰：『無本不立，無文不行。』

translations.literal: The Record says: 'Without root nothing is established; without pattern nothing is carried out.'
translations.idiomatic: The Record says, "Without root nothing stands; without pattern nothing proceeds."

sentences.zh: 神而明之者，本也；

translations.literal: What is made spirit-like and luminous is the root;
translations.idiomatic: What is made luminous in spirit is the root;

sentences.zh: 舉而措之者，文也。

translations.literal: what is lifted up and set in place is the pattern.
translations.idiomatic: what is raised up and put into practice is the pattern.

sentences.zh: 謂宜搜召名儒，以至淹洽古今之士，上監於夏、商，近稽自漢、唐以降，考定斟酌，成一代大典，以淑天下而范萬世。」

translations.literal: It is proposed that renowned Confucians be sought and summoned, even to scholars thoroughly versed in antiquity and the present, looking upward to Xia and Shang and examining closely from Han and Tang downward, weighing and fixing [standards] to complete a great code for the age, thereby beautifying the realm and providing a model for ten thousand generations."
translations.idiomatic: I propose summoning eminent Confucian scholars and men thoroughly versed in past and present, looking back to Xia and Shang and examining Han and Tang down to our day, to weigh and fix standards and complete a great code for the age that will refine the realm and set a model for ten thousand generations."

sentences.zh: 大學士張玉書亦言：「樂律算數之學，失傳已久，承訛襲舛，莫摘其非；

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Zhang Yushu also said: "The learning of musical pitch and mathematical calculation has long been lost in transmission; errors are inherited and mistakes perpetuated, and none can pluck out what is wrong;
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Zhang Yushu also said, "The study of musical pitch and mathematical calculation has long been lost. Errors are inherited and mistakes repeated, and no one can identify what is wrong;

sentences.zh: 奧義微機，莫探其蘊。

translations.literal: profound meanings and subtle mechanisms—none can probe their depths.
translations.idiomatic: profound meanings and subtle mechanisms remain unexplored.

sentences.zh: 臣等躬聆訓誨，猶且一時省寤，而覆算迷濛；

translations.literal: We who personally received your instruction still awaken only for a moment, while repeated calculation remains obscure;
translations.idiomatic: We who have personally heard Your instruction still grasp it only for a moment, while repeated calculation leaves us in confusion;

sentences.zh: 中外臣民，何由共喻？

translations.literal: how can officials and commoners within and without understand together?
translations.idiomatic: how can officials and people throughout the realm share in that understanding?

sentences.zh: 宜特賜裁定，編次成書，頒示四方，共相傳習。

translations.literal: Your Majesty should specially grant authoritative determination, compile and arrange it into a book, promulgate it to the four quarters, and have all study and transmit it together.
translations.idiomatic: Your Majesty should grant authoritative judgment, compile the results into books, promulgate them throughout the realm, and have all study and transmit them together.

sentences.zh: 正歷來積算之差訛，垂萬世和聲之善法，學術政事，均有裨益。」

translations.literal: Correct the accumulated errors of calendrical calculation through the ages, hand down good methods of harmonious sound for ten thousand generations—both learning and governance would benefit."
translations.idiomatic: Correct the accumulated errors of calendrical calculation, establish sound methods of harmony for ten thousand generations, and benefit both scholarship and government alike."

sentences.zh: 帝重違臣下請，五十二年，遂詔修律呂諸書，於蒙養齋立館，求海內暢曉樂律者，光地薦景州魏廷珍、寧國梅□成、交河王蘭生任編纂。

translations.literal: The emperor, reluctant to go against his ministers' request, in the fifty-second year then decreed the compilation of books on pitch pipes and related subjects, established an office at the Mengyang Studio, and sought those throughout the realm thoroughly versed in musical pitch; Guangdi recommended Jingzhou's Wei Tingzhen, Ningguo's Mei □ Cheng [name partially corrupted in source], and Jiaohe's Wang Lansheng to undertake compilation.
translations.idiomatic: Unwilling to refuse his ministers' plea, in the fifty-second year the emperor decreed the compilation of works on pitch pipes, established an office at the Mengyang Studio, and sought experts in music and pitch throughout the realm. Guangdi recommended Wei Tingzhen of Jingzhou, Mei □ Cheng of Ningguo [one character missing in the source text], and Wang Lansheng of Jiaohe as compilers.

sentences.zh: 蘭生故光地所拔士，樂律有神契，硃子琴律圖說，字多訛謬，蘭生以意是正，瞭然可曉。

translations.literal: Lansheng was a scholar formerly raised up by Guangdi; in musical pitch he had a divine attunement. Zhu Xi's Illustrated Explanation of Qin Pitch had many erroneous and mistaken characters; Lansheng corrected them by reasoned judgment so that they became clear and intelligible.
translations.idiomatic: Lansheng was a scholar Guangdi had earlier promoted and possessed an almost intuitive grasp of pitch. Zhu Xi's Illustrated Explanation of Qin Pitch contained many textual errors; Lansheng corrected them by reasoned judgment until the text was clear and intelligible.

sentences.zh: 及被詔入直，所與編校者皆淹雅士，而蘭生學獨深，亦時時折中於帝，遇有疑義，親臨決焉。

translations.literal: When he received the edict to enter regular attendance, those with whom he compiled and collated were all broadly cultivated scholars, yet Lansheng's learning alone was deepest; he also frequently mediated by the emperor's judgment, and whenever doubts arose the emperor personally decided them.
translations.idiomatic: When he was summoned to regular attendance at court, his fellow compilers were all broadly cultivated scholars, yet Lansheng's learning stood deepest. He frequently mediated by the emperor's judgment, and whenever doubts arose the emperor decided them in person.

sentences.zh: 其法首明黃鍾為十二律呂根源，以縱黍橫黍定古今尺度，今尺八寸一分，當古尺十寸，橫黍百粒，當縱黍八十一粒。

translations.literal: Their method first made clear that the yellow bell is the root of the twelve pitch pipes; vertical millet grains and horizontal millet grains were used to fix ancient and modern measures: the present foot of eight inches and one fen equals the ancient foot of ten inches; one hundred horizontal grains equal eighty-one vertical grains.
translations.idiomatic: Their method first established the yellow bell as the root of the twelve pitch pipes and used vertical and horizontal millet grains to fix ancient and modern measures. The present foot of eight inches and one fen equals the ancient foot of ten inches, and one hundred horizontal grains equal eighty-one vertical grains.

sentences.zh: 漢志：「黃鍾之長，以子穀秬黍中者，一黍之廣度之，九十分黃鍾之長，一為一分。」

translations.literal: The Han Treatise says: "The length of the yellow bell: taking the middle grain of the black millet, measure by the breadth of one grain; ninety parts make the length of the yellow bell, and one part is one fen."
translations.idiomatic: The Han Treatise states, "The length of the yellow bell: using the middle grain of black millet, measure by the breadth of one grain. Ninety such parts make the length of the yellow bell, and one part is one fen."

sentences.zh: 廣者橫也，九十分為黃鍾之長，則黃鍾為九十橫黍所累明矣。

translations.literal: 'Breadth' means horizontal; if ninety parts make the length of the yellow bell, then it is clear that the yellow bell is accumulated from ninety horizontal grains.
translations.idiomatic: "Breadth" means horizontal. If ninety parts make the length of the yellow bell, then the yellow bell is plainly built up from ninety horizontal grains.

sentences.zh: 即以橫黍之度比縱黍，為古尺之比今尺，以古尺為一率，今尺為二率，黃鍾古尺九寸為三率，推得四率七寸二分九釐，即黃鍾今尺之度。

translations.literal: Taking the measure of horizontal grains compared with vertical grains as the ratio of the ancient foot to the present foot, with the ancient foot as the first term, the present foot as the second term, and the yellow bell of nine ancient inches as the third term, the fourth term is obtained as seven inches, two fen, and nine li of the present foot—that is, the measure of the yellow bell in the present foot.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing the measure of horizontal grains with vertical grains yields the ratio of ancient to present feet. With the ancient foot as the first term, the present foot as the second, and the yellow bell of nine ancient inches as the third, the fourth term comes to seven inches, two fen, and nine li in the present foot—the length of the yellow bell on the modern scale.

sentences.zh: 律呂新書：黃鍾九寸，空圍九分，積八百一十分，再置古尺，積八百一十分，以九十分歸之，得面冪九方分，用比例相求，麵線相等，面積不同。

translations.literal: The New Book on Pitch Pipes: the yellow bell is nine inches, inner circumference nine fen, volume eight hundred and ten fen; setting the ancient foot again, volume eight hundred and ten fen, dividing by ninety parts, the face power is nine square fen; using proportional calculation, face and line are equal but face area differs.
translations.idiomatic: The New Book on Pitch Pipes gives the yellow bell as nine inches long, with an inner circumference of nine fen and a volume of eight hundred and ten fen. Restating this on the ancient foot and dividing by ninety parts yields a face value of nine square fen. By proportional calculation the face and line are equal, yet the face area differs.

sentences.zh: 定數圓面積一十萬為一率，方面積一十二萬七千三百二十四為二率，今面冪九方分為三率，推得四率一十一分四十五釐九十豪，開平方得三分三釐八豪五絲一忽，為黃鍾古尺徑數。

translations.literal: Fixing the circular face area of one hundred thousand as the first term and the square face area of one hundred twenty-seven thousand three hundred twenty-four as the second term, with the present face power of nine square fen as the third term, the fourth term is obtained as eleven fen, forty-five li, and ninety hao; extracting the square root gives three fen, three li, eight hao, five si, and one hu as the diameter of the yellow bell on the ancient foot.
translations.idiomatic: Taking a fixed circular face area of one hundred thousand as the first term and a square face area of one hundred twenty-seven thousand three hundred twenty-four as the second, with the present face value of nine square fen as the third, the fourth term is eleven fen, forty-five li, and ninety hao. Extracting the square root yields three fen, three li, eight hao, five si, and one hu as the diameter of the yellow bell on the ancient foot.

sentences.zh: 求周，得十分六釐三豪四絲六忽。

translations.literal: Seeking the circumference, one obtains ten fen, six li, three hao, four si, and six hu.
translations.idiomatic: The circumference comes to ten fen, six li, three hao, four si, and six hu.

sentences.zh: 即以古尺之積比今尺之積，古尺一百分，自乘再乘得一百萬分為一率，今尺八十一分，自乘再乘得五十三萬一千四十一分為二率，黃鍾積八百一十分為三率，推得四率四百三十分四百六十七釐二百十一豪，即黃鍾今尺之積。

translations.literal: Taking the volume of the ancient foot compared with the volume of the present foot: the ancient foot of one hundred parts, multiplied by itself and again, gives one million parts as the first term; the present foot of eighty-one parts, multiplied by itself and again, gives five hundred thirty-one thousand forty-one parts as the second term; the yellow bell volume of eight hundred ten parts as the third term; the fourth term is obtained as four hundred thirty parts, four hundred sixty-seven li, and two hundred eleven hao—that is, the volume of the yellow bell on the present foot.
translations.idiomatic: Comparing the volume of the ancient foot with that of the present foot: one hundred parts of the ancient foot, cubed, gives one million parts as the first term; eighty-one parts of the present foot, cubed, gives five hundred thirty-one thousand forty-one parts as the second; the yellow bell volume of eight hundred ten parts is the third. The fourth term is four hundred thirty parts, four hundred sixty-seven li, and two hundred eleven hao—the volume of the yellow bell on the present foot.

sentences.zh: 以今尺長七寸二分九釐歸之，得面冪五分九十釐四十九豪，求徑得二分七釐四豪一絲九忽，而黃鍾管之縱長體積面徑定矣。

translations.literal: Dividing by the present-foot length of seven inches, two fen, and nine li, the face power is five fen, ninety li, and forty-nine hao; seeking the diameter gives two fen, seven li, four hao, one si, and nine hu—and thus the yellow bell pipe's length, volume, face, and diameter were fixed.
translations.idiomatic: Dividing by the present-foot length of seven inches, two fen, and nine li yields a face value of five fen, ninety li, and forty-nine hao. The diameter is two fen, seven li, four hao, one si, and nine hu. Thus the yellow bell pipe's length, volume, face area, and diameter were all fixed.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾既定，於是制律呂同徑之法，以積實容黍為數，三分損益以覈之，黃鍾三分損一，下生林鍾，林鍾三分益一，上生太簇，太簇三分損一，下生南呂，南呂三分益一，上生姑洗，姑洗三分損一，下生應鍾，應鍾三分益一，上生蕤賓，蕤賓三分益一，上生大呂，大呂三分損一，下生夷則，夷則三分益一，上生夾鍾，夾鍾三分損一，下生無射，無射三分益一，上生仲呂。

translations.literal: Once the yellow bell was fixed, they then devised the method of uniform diameter for the pitch pipes, taking filled volume and grain capacity as the number, verifying by the three-part diminishment and augmentation: yellow bell diminished by one-third generates downward the forest bell; forest bell augmented by one-third generates upward the great cluster; great cluster diminished by one-third generates downward the southern lü; southern lü augmented by one-third generates upward the maiden wash; maiden wash diminished by one-third generates downward the responding bell; responding bell augmented by one-third generates upward the luxuriant guest; luxuriant guest augmented by one-third generates upward the great lü; great lü diminished by one-third generates downward the barren lü; barren lü augmented by one-third generates upward the squeezed bell; squeezed bell diminished by one-third generates downward the untiring shoot; untiring shoot augmented by one-third generates upward the second lü.
translations.idiomatic: Once the yellow bell was fixed, they established the method of uniform diameter for the pitch pipes, using filled volume and grain capacity as the measure and verifying by three-part diminishment and augmentation.
