The yellow bell diminished by one-third generates the forest bell below; the forest bell augmented by one-third generates the great cluster above; the great cluster diminished generates the southern lü below; the southern lü augmented generates the maiden wash above; the maiden wash diminished generates the responding bell below; the responding bell augmented generates the luxuriant guest above; the luxuriant guest augmented generates the great lü above; the great lü diminished generates the barren lü below; the barren lü augmented generates the squeezed bell above; the squeezed bell diminished generates the untiring shoot below; the untiring shoot augmented generates the second lü above.

sentences.zh: 又倍之，自蕤賓以下至應鍾，半之，自黃鍾以下至仲呂，皆六。

translations.literal: They were then doubled; from the luxuriant guest downward to the responding bell, and halved from the yellow bell downward to the second lü—all six each.
translations.idiomatic: They were then doubled from the luxuriant guest down to the responding bell and halved from the yellow bell down to the second lü—six pipes in each group.

sentences.zh: 不用京房變律之說，定宮聲在黃鍾、大呂之間。

translations.literal: They did not use Jing Fang's doctrine of altered pitch pipes, and fixed the palace tone between the yellow bell and the great lü.
translations.idiomatic: They rejected Jing Fang's doctrine of altered pitch pipes and fixed the palace tone between the yellow bell and the great lü.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾為宮，次太簇以商應，次姑洗以角應，次蕤賓以變徵應，次夷則以徵應，次無射以羽應，次半黃鍾以變宮應，所謂陽律五聲二變也。

translations.literal: The yellow bell serves as palace; next the great cluster responds as merchant; next the maiden wash responds as horn; next the luxuriant guest responds as altered zhi; next the barren lü responds as zhi; next the untiring shoot responds as feather; next the half yellow bell responds as altered palace—this is what is called the yang pitch pipes with five tones and two alterations.
translations.idiomatic: With the yellow bell as palace, the great cluster answers as merchant, the maiden wash as horn, the luxuriant guest as altered zhi, the barren lü as zhi, the untiring shoot as feather, and the half yellow bell as altered palace—this is the yang pitch series of five tones and two alterations.

sentences.zh: 至半太簇為清宮，仍應黃鍾焉。

translations.literal: Down to the half great cluster as clear palace, it still responds to the yellow bell.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the half great cluster as clear palace, which still corresponds to the yellow bell.

sentences.zh: 大呂為宮，次夾鍾以商應，次仲呂以角應，次林鍾以變徵應，次南呂以徵應，次應鍾以羽應，次半大呂以變宮應，所謂陰呂五聲二變也。

translations.literal: The great lü serves as palace; next the squeezed bell responds as merchant; next the second lü responds as horn; next the forest bell responds as altered zhi; next the southern lü responds as zhi; next the responding bell responds as feather; next the half great lü responds as altered palace—this is what is called the yin pitch pipes with five tones and two alterations.
translations.idiomatic: With the great lü as palace, the squeezed bell answers as merchant, the second lü as horn, the forest bell as altered zhi, the southern lü as zhi, the responding bell as feather, and the half great lü as altered palace—this is the yin pitch series of five tones and two alterations.

sentences.zh: 至半夾鍾為清宮，仍應大呂焉。

translations.literal: Down to the half squeezed bell as clear palace, it still responds to the great lü.
translations.idiomatic: Down to the half squeezed bell as clear palace, which still corresponds to the great lü.

sentences.zh: 旋相為宮，折中取聲，類而不雜。

translations.literal: Rotating to take each as palace, selecting tones from the middle fold, they are categorized without confusion.
translations.idiomatic: Rotating through the series as palace and selecting tones from the middle register, the categories remain distinct without confusion.

sentences.zh: 驗之簫笛，工為宮，則凡應商，六應角，五應變徵，乙應徵，上應羽，尺應變宮。

translations.literal: Verified on flute and pipe: when gong is palace, then fan responds as merchant, liu as horn, wu as altered zhi, yi as zhi, shang as feather, and chi as altered palace.
translations.idiomatic: Tested on flute and pipe: when gong is palace, fan answers as merchant, liu as horn, wu as altered zhi, yi as zhi, shang as feather, and chi as altered palace.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾為低工，大呂為高工，而分清濁。

translations.literal: The yellow bell is low gong, the great lü high gong, distinguishing clear and muddy.
translations.idiomatic: The yellow bell is low gong and the great lü high gong, distinguishing clear from muddy pitch.

sentences.zh: 太簇為低凡，夾鍾為高凡，而分清濁。

translations.literal: The great cluster is low fan, the squeezed bell high fan, distinguishing clear and muddy.
translations.idiomatic: The great cluster is low fan and the squeezed bell high fan, distinguishing clear from muddy pitch.

sentences.zh: 姑洗為低六，仲呂為高六，而分清濁。

translations.literal: The maiden wash is low liu, the second lü high liu, distinguishing clear and muddy.
translations.idiomatic: The maiden wash is low liu and the second lü high liu, distinguishing clear from muddy pitch.

sentences.zh: 蕤賓為低五，林鍾為高五，而分清濁。

translations.literal: The luxuriant guest is low wu, the forest bell high wu, distinguishing clear and muddy.
translations.idiomatic: The luxuriant guest is low wu and the forest bell high wu, distinguishing clear from muddy pitch.

sentences.zh: 夷則為低乙，南呂為高乙，而分清濁。

translations.literal: The barren lü is low yi, the southern lü high yi, distinguishing clear and muddy.
translations.idiomatic: The barren lü is low yi and the southern lü high yi, distinguishing clear from muddy pitch.

sentences.zh: 無射為低上，應鍾為高上，而分清濁。

translations.literal: The untiring shoot is low shang, the responding bell high shang, distinguishing clear and muddy.
translations.idiomatic: The untiring shoot is low shang and the responding bell high shang, distinguishing clear from muddy pitch.

sentences.zh: 倍之，則倍無射、倍應鍾為宮聲之右變宮尺字，而分清濁。

translations.literal: When doubled, then doubled untiring shoot and doubled responding bell serve as the right altered palace chi of the palace tone, distinguishing clear and muddy.
translations.idiomatic: When doubled, the doubled untiring shoot and doubled responding bell become the right altered-palace chi of the palace tone, again distinguishing clear from muddy pitch.

sentences.zh: 倍夷則、倍南呂為變宮之右下羽上字，而分清濁。

translations.literal: Doubled barren lü and doubled southern lü serve as the right lower feather shang of altered palace, distinguishing clear and muddy.
translations.idiomatic: The doubled barren lü and doubled southern lü form the right lower-feather shang of altered palace, distinguishing clear from muddy pitch.

sentences.zh: 倍蕤賓、倍林鍾為下羽之右下徵乙字，而分清濁。

translations.literal: Doubled luxuriant guest and doubled forest bell serve as the right lower zhi yi of lower feather, distinguishing clear and muddy.
translations.idiomatic: The doubled luxuriant guest and doubled forest bell form the right lower-zhi yi of lower feather, distinguishing clear from muddy pitch.

sentences.zh: 半之，則半黃鍾、半大呂為羽聲之左變宮尺字，而分清濁。

translations.literal: When halved, then half yellow bell and half great lü serve as the left altered palace chi of the feather tone, distinguishing clear and muddy.
translations.idiomatic: When halved, the half yellow bell and half great lü become the left altered-palace chi of the feather tone, distinguishing clear from muddy pitch.

sentences.zh: 半太簇、半夾鍾為變宮之左少宮工字，而分清濁。

translations.literal: Half great cluster and half squeezed bell serve as the left lesser palace gong of altered palace, distinguishing clear and muddy.
translations.idiomatic: The half great cluster and half squeezed bell form the left lesser-palace gong of altered palace, distinguishing clear from muddy pitch.

sentences.zh: 半姑洗、半仲呂為少宮之左少商凡字，而分清濁。

translations.literal: Half maiden wash and half second lü serve as the left lesser merchant fan of lesser palace, distinguishing clear and muddy.
translations.idiomatic: The half maiden wash and half second lü form the left lesser-merchant fan of lesser palace, distinguishing clear from muddy pitch.

sentences.zh: 古樂所以起下徵而終清商也。

translations.literal: Thus ancient music begins from lower zhi and ends in clear merchant.
translations.idiomatic: This is why ancient music begins from the lower zhi and ends in clear merchant.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾一徑，別其長短，為十二律呂，復助以倍半，而得五聲二變之全，由是制以樂器，以黃鍾之積為本，加分減分，皆用黃鍾之長與徑相比，大加至八倍，則長與徑亦加一倍，小減至八分之一，則長與徑亦減其半。

translations.literal: One diameter of the yellow bell, distinguishing long and short, makes the twelve pitch pipes; aided further by doubling and halving, the full complement of five tones and two alterations is obtained. Thereby instruments were fashioned: taking the volume of the yellow bell as foundation, whether adding or subtracting parts, all used the length and diameter of the yellow bell in comparison; at the greatest increase to eightfold, length and diameter also increase onefold; at the least reduction to one-eighth, length and diameter are also reduced by half.
translations.idiomatic: From a single yellow bell diameter, varying length and shortness yields the twelve pitch pipes; doubling and halving then complete the five tones and two alterations. Instruments were fashioned accordingly, using the yellow bell volume as the foundation. Whether adding or subtracting parts, all proportions were measured against the yellow bell's length and diameter. At eightfold increase, length and diameter also double; at one-eighth reduction, length and diameter are halved.

sentences.zh: 正律呂管十二，倍管六，半管六。

translations.literal: Standard pitch pipes twelve, doubled pipes six, halved pipes six.
translations.idiomatic: There were twelve standard pitch pipes, six doubled pipes, and six halved pipes.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾同形管五十六，亦倍管六，半管六。

translations.literal: Yellow bell uniform-form pipes fifty-six, likewise doubled pipes six, halved pipes six.
translations.idiomatic: There were fifty-six yellow bell uniform-form pipes, likewise with six doubled and six halved pipes.

sentences.zh: 同形管又生同徑管十一，凡一千三百六十八管。

translations.literal: From uniform-form pipes were further generated eleven uniform-diameter pipes; in all one thousand three hundred sixty-eight pipes.
translations.idiomatic: The uniform-form pipes further generated eleven uniform-diameter types, for a total of one thousand three hundred sixty-eight pipes.

sentences.zh: 依數立制，以考其度，以審其音。

translations.literal: According to number they established the system, to examine their measures and verify their tones.
translations.idiomatic: Standards were established by numerical rule to test their dimensions and verify their pitches.

sentences.zh: 八倍黃鍾之管，聲應正黃鍾之律濁宮低工。

translations.literal: The pipe of eightfold yellow bell: its sound corresponds to the proper yellow bell pitch, muddy palace, low gong.
translations.idiomatic: The eightfold yellow bell pipe produces a tone corresponding to the proper yellow bell pitch: muddy palace, low gong.

sentences.zh: 七倍黃鍾之管，應大呂之呂清宮高工。

translations.literal: The pipe of sevenfold yellow bell corresponds to the great lü pitch, clear palace, high gong.
translations.idiomatic: The sevenfold yellow bell pipe corresponds to the great lü pitch: clear palace, high gong.

sentences.zh: 六倍黃鍾之管，應太簇之律濁商低凡。

translations.literal: The pipe of sixfold yellow bell corresponds to the great cluster pitch, muddy merchant, low fan.
translations.idiomatic: The sixfold yellow bell pipe corresponds to the great cluster pitch: muddy merchant, low fan.

sentences.zh: 五倍黃鍾之管，應夾鍾之呂清商高凡。

translations.literal: The pipe of fivefold yellow bell corresponds to the squeezed bell pitch, clear merchant, high fan.
translations.idiomatic: The fivefold yellow bell pipe corresponds to the squeezed bell pitch: clear merchant, high fan.

sentences.zh: 四倍黃鍾之管，應姑洗之律濁角低六。

translations.literal: The pipe of fourfold yellow bell corresponds to the maiden wash pitch, muddy horn, low liu.
translations.idiomatic: The fourfold yellow bell pipe corresponds to the maiden wash pitch: muddy horn, low liu.

sentences.zh: 三倍半黃鍾之管，應仲呂之呂清角高六。

translations.literal: The pipe of three-and-a-half-fold yellow bell corresponds to the second lü pitch, clear horn, high liu.
translations.idiomatic: The three-and-a-half-fold yellow bell pipe corresponds to the second lü pitch: clear horn, high liu.

sentences.zh: 三倍黃鍾之管，應蕤賓之律濁變徵低五。

translations.literal: The pipe of threefold yellow bell corresponds to the luxuriant guest pitch, muddy altered zhi, low wu.
translations.idiomatic: The threefold yellow bell pipe corresponds to the luxuriant guest pitch: muddy altered zhi, low wu.

sentences.zh: 三倍宜應仲呂，今高半音而應蕤賓，蓋管體漸小，聲音易別。

translations.literal: At threefold it ought to correspond to the second lü, but now, a half-tone higher, it corresponds to the luxuriant guest—presumably because as the pipe body gradually diminishes, the sound is more easily distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: At threefold length it should correspond to the second lü, yet it sounds a half-tone higher and matches the luxuriant guest instead—presumably because as the pipe grows smaller, its tone becomes easier to distinguish.

sentences.zh: 必於三倍之積，復加正黃鍾之半積，始應仲呂之呂清角高六。

translations.literal: Only upon threefold volume, adding again half the volume of proper yellow bell, does it correspond to the second lü pitch, clear horn, high liu.
translations.idiomatic: Only at threefold volume, with half the proper yellow bell volume added again, does the tone match the second lü pitch: clear horn, high liu.

sentences.zh: 半積之理，由此生也。

translations.literal: The principle of half volume arises from this.
translations.idiomatic: The principle of half volume arises from this.

sentences.zh: 二倍半黃鍾之管，應林鍾之呂清變徵高五。

translations.literal: The pipe of two-and-a-half-fold yellow bell corresponds to the forest bell pitch, clear altered zhi, high wu.
translations.idiomatic: The two-and-a-half-fold yellow bell pipe corresponds to the forest bell pitch: clear altered zhi, high wu.

sentences.zh: 二倍加四分之一黃鍾之管，應夷則之律濁徵低乙。

translations.literal: The pipe of twofold plus one-quarter yellow bell corresponds to the barren lü pitch, muddy zhi, low yi.
translations.idiomatic: The twofold yellow bell pipe plus one-quarter corresponds to the barren lü pitch: muddy zhi, low yi.

sentences.zh: 二倍黃鍾之管，不應夷則，而二倍半二倍之間始應之。

translations.literal: The twofold yellow bell pipe does not correspond to the barren lü; only between twofold-and-a-half and twofold does it begin to correspond.
translations.idiomatic: The twofold yellow bell pipe does not match the barren lü; correspondence begins only between two-and-a-half-fold and twofold length.

sentences.zh: 必以半積復半之，為四分之一，加於二倍之內，其分乃合。

translations.literal: One must take half the volume and halve it again to make one-quarter, add it within the twofold, and only then do the parts align.
translations.idiomatic: Half the volume must be halved again to yield one-quarter, added within the twofold measure, before the parts align.

sentences.zh: 四分之一之理，由此生焉。

translations.literal: The principle of one-quarter arises from this.
translations.idiomatic: The principle of one-quarter parts arises from this.

sentences.zh: 二倍黃鍾之管，應南呂之呂清徵高乙。

translations.literal: The twofold yellow bell pipe corresponds to the southern lü pitch, clear zhi, high yi.
translations.idiomatic: The twofold yellow bell pipe corresponds to the southern lü pitch: clear zhi, high yi.

sentences.zh: 正加四分之三黃鍾之管，應無射之律濁羽低上。

translations.literal: The pipe of proper yellow bell plus three-quarters yellow bell corresponds to the untiring shoot pitch, muddy feather, low shang.
translations.idiomatic: The proper yellow bell pipe plus three-quarters corresponds to the untiring shoot pitch: muddy feather, low shang.

sentences.zh: 正加四分之二黃鍾之管，應應鍾之呂清羽高上。

translations.literal: The pipe of proper plus two-quarters yellow bell corresponds to the responding bell pitch, clear feather, high shang.
translations.idiomatic: The proper yellow bell pipe plus two-quarters corresponds to the responding bell pitch: clear feather, high shang.

sentences.zh: 正加四分之一黃鍾之管，應半黃鍾之律濁變宮低尺。

translations.literal: The pipe of proper plus one-quarter yellow bell corresponds to the half yellow bell pitch, muddy altered palace, low chi.
translations.idiomatic: The proper yellow bell pipe plus one-quarter corresponds to the half yellow bell pitch: muddy altered palace, low chi.

sentences.zh: 正加八分之一黃鍾之管，應半大呂之呂清變宮高尺。

translations.literal: The pipe of proper plus one-eighth yellow bell corresponds to the half great lü pitch, clear altered palace, high chi.
translations.idiomatic: The proper yellow bell pipe plus one-eighth corresponds to the half great lü pitch: clear altered palace, high chi.

sentences.zh: 此管與正黃鍾最近，欲取合清宮之分，則以四分之一復半之，為八分之一，加於正黃鍾之分，其聲始應。

translations.literal: This pipe is nearest to proper yellow bell; to obtain the part matching clear palace, one takes one-quarter, halves it again to make one-eighth, adds it to the portion of proper yellow bell, and only then does the sound correspond.
translations.idiomatic: This pipe lies closest to proper yellow bell. To obtain the interval matching clear palace, one quarters it, halves again to one-eighth, adds that to the proper yellow bell portion, and only then does the tone correspond.

sentences.zh: 八分之一之理，由此生焉。

translations.literal: The principle of one-eighth arises from this.
translations.idiomatic: The principle of one-eighth parts arises from this.

sentences.zh: 繼此則正黃鍾管聲應半太簇之律，濁宮低工乃與八倍黃鍾之管相和同聲矣。

translations.literal: Continuing from this, the proper yellow bell pipe's sound corresponds to the half great cluster pitch, muddy palace, low gong—and thus matches the eightfold yellow bell pipe in unison.
translations.idiomatic: Next, the proper yellow bell pipe corresponds to the half great cluster pitch, muddy palace, low gong, and thus sounds in unison with the eightfold yellow bell pipe.

sentences.zh: 遞減之，黃鍾正積八分之七之管，應大呂之呂。

translations.literal: By progressive diminution: the pipe of seven-eighths of yellow bell proper volume corresponds to the great lü pitch.
translations.idiomatic: By successive reduction, the pipe of seven-eighths of the yellow bell proper volume corresponds to the great lü pitch.

sentences.zh: 八分之六之管，應太簇之律。

translations.literal: The pipe of six-eighths corresponds to the great cluster pitch.
translations.idiomatic: The six-eighths pipe corresponds to the great cluster pitch.

sentences.zh: 八分之五之管，應夾鍾之呂。

translations.literal: The pipe of five-eighths corresponds to the squeezed bell pitch.
translations.idiomatic: The five-eighths pipe corresponds to the squeezed bell pitch.

sentences.zh: 八分之四之管，應姑洗之律。

translations.literal: The pipe of four-eighths corresponds to the maiden wash pitch.
translations.idiomatic: The four-eighths pipe corresponds to the maiden wash pitch.

sentences.zh: 八分之三分有半之管，應仲呂之呂。

translations.literal: The pipe of three and a half eighths corresponds to the second lü pitch.
translations.idiomatic: The three-and-a-half-eighths pipe corresponds to the second lü pitch.

sentences.zh: 八分之三之管，應蕤賓之律。

translations.literal: The pipe of three-eighths corresponds to the luxuriant guest pitch.
translations.idiomatic: The three-eighths pipe corresponds to the luxuriant guest pitch.

sentences.zh: 八分之二分有半之管，應林鍾之呂。

translations.literal: The pipe of two and a half eighths corresponds to the forest bell pitch.
translations.idiomatic: The two-and-a-half-eighths pipe corresponds to the forest bell pitch.

sentences.zh: 八分之二又加一分之四分之一之管，應夷則之律。

translations.literal: The pipe of two-eighths plus one-quarter of one-eighth corresponds to the barren lü pitch.
translations.idiomatic: The two-eighths pipe plus one-quarter of one-eighth corresponds to the barren lü pitch.

sentences.zh: 此一分之四分之一，乃正黃鍾三十二分之一，至此三十二分之理生焉。

translations.literal: This one-quarter of one-eighth is one thirty-second of proper yellow bell; thus the principle of thirty-second parts arises here.
translations.idiomatic: This quarter-of-an-eighth is one thirty-second of proper yellow bell; here the principle of thirty-second parts arises.

sentences.zh: 八分之二之管，應南呂之呂。

translations.literal: The pipe of two-eighths corresponds to the southern lü pitch.
translations.idiomatic: The two-eighths pipe corresponds to the southern lü pitch.

sentences.zh: 八分之一又加一分之四分之三之管，應無射之律。

translations.literal: The pipe of one-eighth plus three-quarters of one-eighth corresponds to the untiring shoot pitch.
translations.idiomatic: The one-eighth pipe plus three-quarters of one-eighth corresponds to the untiring shoot pitch.

sentences.zh: 八分之一又加一分之四分之二之管，應應鍾之呂。

translations.literal: The pipe of one-eighth plus two-quarters of one-eighth corresponds to the responding bell pitch.
translations.idiomatic: The one-eighth pipe plus two-quarters of one-eighth corresponds to the responding bell pitch.

sentences.zh: 八分之一又加一分之四分之一之管，應半黃鍾之律。

translations.literal: The pipe of one-eighth plus one-quarter of one-eighth corresponds to the half yellow bell pitch.
translations.idiomatic: The one-eighth pipe plus one-quarter of one-eighth corresponds to the half yellow bell pitch.

sentences.zh: 八分之一又加一分之八分之一之管，應半大呂之呂。

translations.literal: The pipe of one-eighth plus one-eighth of one-eighth corresponds to the half great lü pitch.
translations.idiomatic: The one-eighth pipe plus one-eighth of one-eighth corresponds to the half great lü pitch.

sentences.zh: 此一分之八分之一，乃正黃鍾六十四分之一，至此六十四分之理生焉。

translations.literal: This one-eighth of one-eighth is one sixty-fourth of proper yellow bell; thus the principle of sixty-fourth parts arises here.
translations.idiomatic: This eighth-of-an-eighth is one sixty-fourth of proper yellow bell; here the principle of sixty-fourth parts arises.

sentences.zh: 而八分之一之管，又應正黃鍾，而為正黃鍾長與徑之半。

translations.literal: And the one-eighth pipe again corresponds to proper yellow bell, being half the length and diameter of proper yellow bell.
translations.idiomatic: The one-eighth pipe again matches proper yellow bell, with length and diameter each half those of proper yellow bell.

sentences.zh: 自八倍黃鍾至黃鍾八分之一，皆具同徑之十二律呂，皆成一調之五聲二變。

translations.literal: From eightfold yellow bell down to one-eighth yellow bell, all possess the twelve pitch pipes of uniform diameter, each completing the five tones and two alterations of one mode.
translations.idiomatic: From eightfold yellow bell down to one-eighth yellow bell, each pipe of uniform diameter carries the full twelve pitch pipes, each yielding the five tones and two alterations of a single mode.

sentences.zh: 推而演之，加黃鍾之積至六十四倍，則同形管長徑皆四倍於正黃鍾，減黃鍾之積至六十四分之一，則同形管長徑皆得正黃鍾四分之一。

translations.literal: Extending the calculation: increasing yellow bell volume to sixty-fourfold, the uniform-form pipe's length and diameter are both four times those of proper yellow bell; diminishing yellow bell volume to one sixty-fourth, the uniform-form pipe's length and diameter both equal one-quarter of proper yellow bell.
translations.idiomatic: Carrying the method forward: at sixty-fourfold yellow bell volume, the uniform-form pipe's length and diameter are each four times those of proper yellow bell; at one sixty-fourth volume, the uniform-form pipe's length and diameter are each one-quarter of proper yellow bell.

sentences.zh: 六十四倍積同形管應正黃鍾，五十六倍積同形管與六十四分之七同形管應大呂，四十八倍積同形管與六十四分之六同形管應太簇，四十倍積同形管與六十四分之五同形管應夾鍾，三十二倍積同形管與六十四分之四同形管應姑洗，二十八倍積同形管與六十四分之三加半同形管應仲呂，二十四倍積同形管與六十四分之三同形管應蕤賓，二十倍積同形管與六十四分之二加半同形管應林鍾，十八倍積同形管與六十四分之二加一分四之一同形管應夷則，十六倍積同形管與六十四分之二同形管應南呂，十四倍積同形管與六十四分之一加一分四之三同形管應無射，十二倍積同形管與六十四分之一加一分四之二同形管應應鍾，十倍積同形管與六十四分之一加一分四之一同形管應半黃鍾，九倍積同形管與六十四分之一加一分八之一同形管應半大呂，六十四分之一同形管仍應正黃鍾，於是十二律呂之同徑異形者，合長短倍半以成旋宮之用。

translations.literal: The sixty-fourfold-volume uniform-form pipe corresponds to proper yellow bell; the fifty-sixfold-volume uniform-form pipe and the seven sixty-fourths uniform-form pipe correspond to the great lü; the forty-eightfold and six sixty-fourths correspond to the great cluster; the fortyfold and five sixty-fourths to the squeezed bell; the thirty-twofold and four sixty-fourths to the maiden wash; the twenty-eightfold and three-and-a-half sixty-fourths to the second lü; the twenty-fourfold and three sixty-fourths to the luxuriant guest; the twentyfold and two-and-a-half sixty-fourths to the forest bell; the eighteenfold and two sixty-fourths plus one-quarter of one sixty-fourth to the barren lü; the sixteenfold and two sixty-fourths to the southern lü; the fourteenfold and one sixty-fourth plus three-quarters of one sixty-fourth to the untiring shoot; the twelvefold and one sixty-fourth plus two-quarters of one sixty-fourth to the responding bell; the tenfold and one sixty-fourth plus one-quarter of one sixty-fourth to the half yellow bell; the ninefold and one sixty-fourth plus one-eighth of one sixty-fourth to the half great lü; the one sixty-fourth uniform-form pipe still corresponds to proper yellow bell—thus the twelve pitch pipes of uniform diameter but differing form, combining length, shortness, doubling, and halving, serve for circulating the modes.
translations.idiomatic: The sixty-fourfold-volume uniform-form pipe matches proper yellow bell; the fifty-sixfold pipe and the seven-sixty-fourths pipe match the great lü; forty-eightfold and six-sixty-fourths match the great cluster; fortyfold and five-sixty-fourths the squeezed bell; thirty-twofold and four-sixty-fourths the maiden wash; twenty-eightfold and three-and-a-half sixty-fourths the second lü; twenty-fourfold and three-sixty-fourths the luxuriant guest; twentyfold and two-and-a-half sixty-fourths the forest bell; eighteenfold and two-sixty-fourths plus one sixty-fourth of a sixty-fourth the barren lü; sixteenfold and two-sixty-fourths the southern lü; fourteenfold and one-sixty-fourth plus three-quarters of a sixty-fourth the untiring shoot; twelvefold and one-sixty-fourth plus two-quarters of a sixty-fourth the responding bell; tenfold and one-sixty-fourth plus one-quarter of a sixty-fourth the half yellow bell; ninefold and one-sixty-fourth plus one-eighth of a sixty-fourth the half great lü; the one-sixty-fourth pipe still matches proper yellow bell. Thus the twelve pitch pipes of uniform diameter but differing shape, combining long and short with doubling and halving, complete the method of circulating modes.

sentences.zh: 而黃鍾之同形異徑者，因加減實積，亦成旋宮之用。

translations.literal: As for yellow bell pipes of uniform form but differing diameter, by adding and subtracting solid volume they too serve for circulating the modes.
translations.idiomatic: Yellow bell pipes of uniform shape but differing diameter, by adding and subtracting solid volume, likewise serve to circulate the modes.

sentences.zh: 制器求聲，齊於此矣。

translations.literal: Fashioning instruments and seeking sound are brought into accord here.
translations.idiomatic: Instrument-making and tone-seeking are brought into full accord here.

sentences.zh: 雖然，五聲二變管律與弦度又各不同，漢、唐以後，皆宗司馬、淮南之說，以三分損益之術，誤為管音五聲二變之次，復執管子弦音五聲度分，而牽合於十二律呂之中。

translations.literal: Nevertheless, the five tones and two alterations of pipe pitch and string measure each differ; after Han and Tang all followed the doctrines of Sima [Qian] and the Huainan [masters], taking the three-part diminishment-and-augmentation method and mistakenly applying it as the sequence of five tones and two alterations in pipe sound, then clinging to Guanzi's string-tone five-tone degree-parts and forcing them into the twelve pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Yet pipe pitch and string measure differ in their five tones and two alterations. After Han and Tang, scholars followed Sima Qian and the Huainan masters, misapplied three-part diminishment and augmentation as the order of pipe tones, then forced Guanzi's string-degree divisions into the twelve pitch pipes.

sentences.zh: 試截竹為管吹之，黃鍾半律，不與黃鍾合，而合黃鍾者為太簇之半律，則倍半相應之說，在弦音而非管音也。

translations.literal: Try cutting bamboo into a pipe and blowing it: the half yellow bell pitch does not match yellow bell, while what matches yellow bell is the half great cluster pitch—thus the doctrine that doubling and halving correspond applies to string sound, not pipe sound.
translations.idiomatic: Cut bamboo into a pipe and blow: the half yellow bell pitch does not unite with yellow bell, but the half great cluster pitch does—proving that octave correspondence belongs to strings, not pipes.

sentences.zh: 又黃鍾為宮，其徵聲不應於林鍾而應於夷則，則三分損益宮下生徵之說，在弦度而非管律也。

translations.literal: Again, with yellow bell as palace, its zhi tone does not correspond to the forest bell but to the barren lü—thus the doctrine that palace generates zhi downward by three-part diminishment applies to string measure, not pipe pitch.
translations.idiomatic: With yellow bell as palace, the zhi tone answers not the forest bell but the barren lü—so the rule that palace generates zhi by three-part diminishment applies to string measure, not pipe pitch.

sentences.zh: 以弦度取聲，全弦與半弦之音相應，而半律較全律則下一音。

translations.literal: Taking sound by string measure, the full string and half string correspond in tone, while a half pitch compared with a full pitch is one tone lower.
translations.idiomatic: On strings, the full string and half string sound in correspondence, yet a half pitch stands one tone below its full pitch.

sentences.zh: 蓋弦之體，實藉人力鼓動而生聲，全弦長，故得音緩，半弦短，故得音急，長短緩急之間，全半相應之理寓焉。

translations.literal: For the string's body truly relies on human force to stir it and produce sound: the full string is long, so the tone is slow; the half string is short, so the tone is quick—in the relation of long and short, slow and quick, the principle of full-and-half correspondence resides.
translations.idiomatic: A string sounds only when human force sets it vibrating: the long full string yields a slow tone, the short half string a quick one—and in that contrast of length and speed lies the principle of full-and-half correspondence.

sentences.zh: 管之體虛，假人氣入之以生聲，故管之徑同者，其全半不相應，求其相應，必徑減半始得，所以正黃鍾與黃鍾八分之一之管相應同聲也。

translations.literal: The pipe's body is hollow; sound is produced by human breath entering it. Thus pipes of the same diameter do not correspond at full and half length; to obtain correspondence the diameter must be halved—hence the proper yellow bell pipe and the one-eighth yellow bell pipe correspond in the same tone.
translations.idiomatic: A pipe is hollow and sounds when breath enters it. Pipes of equal diameter do not correspond at full and half length; correspondence requires halving the diameter—hence proper yellow bell and the one-eighth yellow bell pipe sound as one.

sentences.zh: 因全半之不同，於是管律弦度首音至八音，其間所生五聲二變之度分亦異。

translations.literal: Because full and half differ, the degree-parts of the five tones and two alterations generated between the first and eighth tones of pipe pitch and string measure also differ.
translations.idiomatic: Since full and half lengths differ, the degree-parts of the five tones and two alterations between the first and eighth tones differ for pipe pitch and string measure alike.

sentences.zh: 管律黃鍾之全為宮聲首音，則太簇之半為少宮八音，其間太簇之全為商聲二音，姑洗為角聲三音，蕤賓為變徵四音，夷則為徵聲五音，無射為羽聲六音，黃鍾之半為變宮七音。

translations.literal: In pipe pitch, the full yellow bell is the palace-tone first tone; the half great cluster is the lesser palace eighth tone; between them the full great cluster is the merchant second tone, maiden wash the horn third, luxuriant guest the altered zhi fourth, barren lü the zhi fifth, untiring shoot the feather sixth, and half yellow bell the altered palace seventh.
translations.idiomatic: In pipe pitch, full yellow bell is the first palace tone; half great cluster is the eighth lesser-palace tone; between them full great cluster is merchant, maiden wash horn, luxuriant guest altered zhi, barren lü zhi, untiring shoot feather, and half yellow bell altered palace.

sentences.zh: 自首音至第八音，得七全分。

translations.literal: From the first tone to the eighth, seven full parts are obtained.
translations.idiomatic: From the first tone through the eighth, seven full parts are obtained.

sentences.zh: 若弦度假借黃鍾全分為宮聲首音，則黃鍾之半為少宮八音，其間太簇之分為商聲二音，姑洗之分為角聲三音，蕤賓之分為變徵四音，而林鍾之分乃為徵聲五音，南呂之分為羽聲六音，應鍾之分為變宮七音。

translations.literal: If on string measure one borrows the full yellow bell part as the palace-tone first tone, then half yellow bell is the lesser palace eighth tone; between them the great cluster part is merchant second, maiden wash part horn third, luxuriant guest part altered zhi fourth, while the forest bell part is zhi fifth, southern lü part feather sixth, and responding bell part altered palace seventh.
translations.idiomatic: On strings, borrowing the full yellow bell part as the first palace tone makes half yellow bell the eighth lesser-palace tone; the great cluster part is merchant, maiden wash horn, luxuriant guest altered zhi, forest bell zhi, southern lü feather, and responding bell altered palace.

sentences.zh: 各弦之分，宮至商，商至角，角至變徵，徵至羽，羽至變宮，皆得全分，而變徵至徵，變宮至少宮，祗得半分。

translations.literal: Among the parts of each string, palace to merchant, merchant to horn, horn to altered zhi, zhi to feather, and feather to altered palace each yield a full part, while altered zhi to zhi and altered palace to lesser palace yield only half a part.
translations.idiomatic: On each string, palace to merchant, merchant to horn, horn to altered zhi, zhi to feather, and feather to altered palace each span a full part; altered zhi to zhi and altered palace to lesser palace span only half a part.

sentences.zh: 自首音至八音，合為六全分，故弦音不可以十二律呂之度取分。

translations.literal: From the first tone to the eighth, the total is six full parts; therefore string sound cannot take its parts from the degrees of the twelve pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: From first to eighth tone the total is six full parts—so string tones cannot be measured by the twelve pitch-pipe degrees.

sentences.zh: 如以倍無射變宮尺字定弦，則得下徵之分。

translations.literal: If one sets the string by the doubled untiring shoot altered-palace chi note, one obtains the lower zhi part.
translations.idiomatic: Setting the string by the doubled untiring shoot altered-palace chi yields the lower-zhi division.

sentences.zh: 倍無射變宮尺字，即今笛與頭管之合字也。

translations.literal: The doubled untiring shoot altered-palace chi is precisely the unison note of today's flute and lead pipe.
translations.idiomatic: The doubled untiring shoot altered-palace chi is the unison note used on the modern flute and lead pipe.

sentences.zh: 凡品樂居首一弦，必得下徵之分，而五音之位始正。

translations.literal: Whenever graded music places the first string foremost, it must obtain the lower-zhi part before the positions of the five tones are correct.
translations.idiomatic: In graded music the leading string must carry the lower-zhi division before the five tones fall into their proper places.

sentences.zh: 故世以頭管合字定琴之一弦為黃鍾之宮者，蓋一弦不得不定以合字，正為取下徵之分也。

translations.literal: Hence the world sets the qin's first string by the lead pipe's unison note as yellow bell palace—because the first string cannot but be fixed to the unison note, precisely to obtain the lower-zhi part.
translations.idiomatic: Hence musicians fix the qin's first string to the lead pipe's unison note as yellow bell palace: the first string must be set to that unison precisely to obtain the lower-zhi division.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾宮聲工字定弦，得下羽之分；

translations.literal: Setting the string by yellow bell palace-tone gong yields the lower-feather part;
translations.idiomatic: Fixing the string to yellow bell palace gong yields the lower-feather division;

sentences.zh: 太簇商聲凡字定弦，得變宮之分；

translations.literal: Setting by great cluster merchant-tone fan yields the altered-palace part;
translations.idiomatic: Fixing to great cluster merchant fan yields the altered-palace division;

sentences.zh: 姑洗角聲六字定弦，得宮弦之分；

translations.literal: Setting by maiden wash horn-tone liu yields the palace-string part;
translations.idiomatic: Fixing to maiden wash horn liu yields the palace-string division;

sentences.zh: 蕤賓變徵五字定弦，得商弦之分；

translations.literal: Setting by luxuriant guest altered-zhi wu yields the merchant-string part;
translations.idiomatic: Fixing to luxuriant guest altered zhi wu yields the merchant-string division;

sentences.zh: 夷則徵聲乙字定弦，得角弦之分；

translations.literal: Setting by barren lü zhi-tone yi yields the horn-string part;
translations.idiomatic: Fixing to barren lü zhi yi yields the horn-string division;

sentences.zh: 無射羽聲上字定弦，得變徵之分；

translations.literal: Setting by untiring shoot feather-tone shang yields the altered-zhi part;
translations.idiomatic: Fixing to untiring shoot feather shang yields the altered-zhi division;

sentences.zh: 而半黃鍾變宮尺字定弦，仍得徵弦之分焉。

translations.literal: Yet setting by half yellow bell altered-palace chi still yields the zhi-string part.
translations.idiomatic: Yet fixing to half yellow bell altered palace chi still yields the zhi-string division.

sentences.zh: 今借黃鍾之分為宮弦全分，其首音仍定以黃鍾之律，則二音限於太簇之分，而聲亦應太簇之律，三音則變為夾鍾之分，而聲始應姑洗之律。

translations.literal: Now if one borrows the yellow bell part as the palace string's full part, with the first tone still fixed to the yellow bell pitch, then the second tone is confined to the great cluster part and the sound also answers the great cluster pitch; the third tone shifts to the squeezed bell part while the sound only then answers the maiden wash pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Borrowing the yellow bell part as the palace string's full measure, with the first tone still on yellow bell pitch, confines the second tone to the great cluster part—sound and measure both on great cluster—while the third shifts to the squeezed bell part before the sound answers maiden wash.

sentences.zh: 如仍取姑洗之分，則聲必變而應於仲呂之呂，四音復變為仲呂之分，而聲應蕤賓之律。

translations.literal: If one still takes the maiden wash part, the sound must shift to answer the second lü pitch; the fourth tone again shifts to the second lü part while the sound answers the luxuriant guest pitch.
translations.idiomatic: If one keeps the maiden wash part, the sound shifts to the second lü pitch; the fourth tone moves to the second lü part while the sound answers luxuriant guest.

sentences.zh: 如仍取蕤賓之分，則聲必變而應於林鍾之呂，五音則為林鍾之分而應夷則之律，六音則為南呂之分而應無射之律，七音又變為無射之分而聲始應半黃鍾之律。

translations.literal: If one still takes the luxuriant guest part, the sound must shift to answer the forest bell pitch; the fifth tone becomes the forest bell part and answers the barren lü pitch, the sixth becomes the southern lü part and answers the untiring shoot pitch, and the seventh again shifts to the untiring shoot part before the sound answers the half yellow bell pitch.
translations.idiomatic: If one keeps the luxuriant guest part, the sound shifts to forest bell; the fifth becomes forest bell part answering barren lü, the sixth southern lü part answering untiring shoot, and the seventh shifts to untiring shoot before answering half yellow bell.

sentences.zh: 如仍取應鍾之分，則聲必變而應於半大呂之呂。

translations.literal: If one still takes the responding bell part, the sound must shift to answer the half great lü pitch.
translations.idiomatic: If one keeps the responding bell part, the sound shifts to the half great lü pitch.

sentences.zh: 此宮弦之分因全弦首音定黃鍾之律，而變為羽弦之分者也。

translations.literal: This is a case in which the palace-string part, because the full string's first tone is fixed to the yellow bell pitch, shifts into the feather-string part.
translations.idiomatic: Here the palace-string division, with the full string's first tone fixed to yellow bell pitch, shifts into the feather-string division.

sentences.zh: 或以黃鍾之分為宮弦全分，而本弦七音欲各限以宮弦內七音之分，則首音必定以姑洗之律。

translations.literal: Or if one takes the yellow bell part as the palace string's full part, yet wishes each of the string's seven tones to be confined to the seven parts within the palace string, then the first tone must be fixed to the maiden wash pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Or, taking the yellow bell part as the palace string's full measure while confining all seven tones to the palace string's seven internal parts, the first tone must be fixed to maiden wash pitch.

sentences.zh: 以次分之，此宮弦之分因全弦首音定姑洗之律，而得宮弦之分者也。

translations.literal: Dividing the parts in sequence—this palace-string part, because the full string's first tone is fixed to the maiden wash pitch, thereby obtains the palace-string part.
translations.idiomatic: Dividing sequentially: with the first tone on maiden wash pitch, the palace-string division is obtained.

sentences.zh: 又或以笛與頭管合字為今所定倍無射之律為宮弦全分，首音依次分之，得下徵弦之分，此宮弦之分因全弦首音定以笛之合字而變為徵弦之分者也。

translations.literal: Or again, taking the flute and lead pipe's unison note as the pitch now fixed for doubled untiring shoot as the palace string's full part and dividing the first tone in sequence yields the lower-zhi string part—this palace-string part, because the full string's first tone is fixed to the flute's unison note, shifts into the zhi-string part.
translations.idiomatic: Or taking the flute and lead pipe unison as today's doubled untiring shoot pitch for the palace string's full measure and dividing from the first tone yields the lower-zhi string division—here the palace string, with its first tone on the flute's unison, shifts into the zhi-string division.

sentences.zh: 依律呂而定弦音，則弦度之分隨之潛移，依弦度之分命為七音之次，則聲音宮調不與律呂相協。

translations.literal: Fix string sound by pitch pipes and the string's degree-parts shift invisibly; name the seven tones by the string's degree-parts and the mode no longer accords with the pitch pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Fix strings by pitch pipes and their degree-parts drift; name the seven tones by string parts and the mode no longer matches the pipes.

sentences.zh: 此由管律、弦度全、半生聲取分之不同，於是絲樂弦音之旋宮轉調，與竹樂管音亦異。

translations.literal: Because pipe pitch and string measure differ in how full, half, and sounding length yield their parts, the circulating modes and shifted keys of silk-string music and bamboo pipe music also differ.
translations.idiomatic: Since pipe pitch and string measure differ in deriving parts from full, half, and sounding length, silk strings and bamboo pipes diverge in circulating modes and transposition.

sentences.zh: 清濁二均各七調，中與管樂有同者，有可同者，有不可同者。

translations.literal: The clear and muddy two registers each have seven modes; in relation to pipe music some match, some can match, and some cannot match.
translations.idiomatic: Clear and muddy registers each hold seven modes; against pipe music some align fully, some partially, and some not at all.

sentences.zh: 同者惟宮調一調，五聲二變皆正應。

translations.literal: What matches is only the palace mode, in which all five tones and two alterations respond correctly.
translations.idiomatic: Only the palace mode matches completely, with all five tones and two alterations in true correspondence.

sentences.zh: 可同者，商調、徵調五聲正、應二變借用；

translations.literal: What can match: in merchant and zhi modes the five proper tones match and the two alterations are borrowed;
translations.idiomatic: Merchant and zhi modes can partially match: the five proper tones align and the two alterations are borrowed;

sentences.zh: 不可同者，角調、變徵調、羽調、變宮調五聲之內清濁相淆。

translations.literal: What cannot match: in horn, altered-zhi, feather, and altered-palace modes, clear and muddy are confused within the five tones.
translations.idiomatic: Horn, altered-zhi, feather, and altered-palace modes cannot match, for clear and muddy tones mingle within the five tones.

sentences.zh: 如但以弦音奏之，而不和以管音，祗有四調，餘三調皆轉入弦音宮調。

translations.literal: If one plays only string sound without harmonizing pipe sound, there are only four modes; the remaining three all shift into the string palace mode.
translations.idiomatic: Played on strings alone, without pipe harmony, only four modes remain; the other three collapse into the string palace mode.

sentences.zh: 故周禮大司樂三宮，漢志三統，皆以三調為準。

translations.literal: Hence the Grand Music Master of three palaces in the Rites of Zhou and the three sequences in the Han Treatise all take three modes as the standard.
translations.idiomatic: Hence the Zhou Rites' Grand Music Master of three palaces and the Han Treatise's three sequences both treat three modes as the standard.

sentences.zh: 所謂三統，其一天統，黃鍾為宮，乃黃鍾宮聲位羽起調，姑洗角聲立宮，主調是為宮調也。

translations.literal: The so-called three sequences: the first, the Heaven sequence—with yellow bell as palace, namely the palace-tone position starting from feather, maiden wash horn-tone establishing palace—is the palace mode.
translations.idiomatic: Of the three sequences, the Heaven sequence takes yellow bell as palace—the palace tone with feather as starting degree and maiden wash horn establishing the mode—forming the palace mode.

sentences.zh: 其一人統，太簇為宮，乃太簇商聲位羽起調，蕤賓變徵立宮，主調是為商調也。

translations.literal: The second, the Human sequence—with great cluster as palace, namely the merchant-tone position starting from feather, luxuriant guest altered zhi establishing palace—is the merchant mode.
translations.idiomatic: The Human sequence takes great cluster as palace—the merchant tone with feather as starting degree and luxuriant guest altered zhi establishing the mode—forming the merchant mode.

sentences.zh: 其一地統，林鍾為宮，乃弦音徵分位羽，實管音夷則徵聲位羽起調，半黃鍾變宮立宮，主調是為徵調也。

translations.literal: The third, the Earth sequence—with forest bell as palace, namely the string zhi part in the feather position, while in pipe sound the barren lü zhi-tone position starts from feather and half yellow bell altered palace establishes palace—is the zhi mode.
translations.idiomatic: The Earth sequence takes forest bell as palace—in strings the zhi degree stands in the feather place, while in pipes barren lü zhi starts from feather and half yellow bell altered palace establishes the mode—forming the zhi mode.

sentences.zh: 隋志鄭譯云：考尋律呂，七聲之內，三聲乖應。

translations.literal: Zheng Yi in the Sui Treatise said: examining the pitch pipes, within the seven tones three tones fail to correspond.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Yi in the Sui Treatise wrote: "Examining the pitch pipes, three of the seven tones fail to correspond."

sentences.zh: 當時考較聲律，或以管音考核弦音，或以弦音考核管音，故得四調相和，三調乖應，即二變調與角調也。

translations.literal: At that time, in comparing sound and pitch, some tested string sound against pipe sound, some pipe against string—thus four modes harmonized while three failed to correspond, namely the two altered modes and the horn mode.
translations.idiomatic: When sound and pitch were compared—sometimes pipe testing string, sometimes the reverse—four modes harmonized and three failed, namely the two altered modes and the horn mode.

sentences.zh: 變徵調與羽調五正聲內祗一聲乖應，然羽調猶能自立一調，變徵調則轉入宮調聲字。

translations.literal: In the altered-zhi mode and feather mode, among the five proper tones only one fails to correspond; yet the feather mode can still stand as its own mode, while the altered-zhi mode shifts into palace-tone syllables.
translations.idiomatic: Altered-zhi and feather modes each have one mismatched tone among the five proper tones; yet feather can still stand alone, while altered-zhi collapses into palace syllables.

sentences.zh: 至角調變宮調，五聲之內二三聲乖應，與宮調聲字雷同，皆不能成一調也。

translations.literal: As for horn mode and altered-palace mode, two or three of the five tones fail to correspond and their syllables duplicate those of palace mode—they cannot constitute modes of their own.
translations.idiomatic: Horn and altered-palace modes have two or three mismatched tones and duplicate palace syllables—they cannot form independent modes.

sentences.zh: 唐志載四宮二十八調，率以弦音之分定為十二律呂之度，故有正宮大食、高大食之名。

translations.literal: The Tang Treatise records four palaces and twenty-eight modes, all largely fixing the degrees of the twelve pitch pipes by string degree-parts—hence names such as Proper Palace, Great Shí, and Lofty Great Shí.
translations.idiomatic: The Tang Treatise records four palaces and twenty-eight modes, largely deriving the twelve pitch-pipe degrees from string parts—hence names like Proper Palace, Great Shí, and Lofty Great Shí.

sentences.zh: 今即弦音、管音之和不和，以辨陽律、陰呂之分用、合用，乃知唐書之二十八調獨取弦音，不在管律。

translations.literal: Now, judging harmony and disharmony between string and pipe sound, and distinguishing use, combination, and non-combination of yang pitch pipes and yin pitch pipes, one knows that the Tang History's twenty-eight modes drew solely on string sound, not on pipe pitch.
translations.idiomatic: Judging string and pipe harmony and the separate or combined use of yang pipes and yin pipes shows that the Tang History's twenty-eight modes drew on strings alone, not pipe pitch.

sentences.zh: 而古人所用三統，實取管音、弦音之相和者用之也。

translations.literal: Yet the three sequences used by the ancients in fact employed what harmonized between pipe sound and string sound.
translations.idiomatic: Yet the ancients' three sequences in fact used only what harmonized between pipe and string.

sentences.zh: 是以弦音諸樂，其要有四：一，定弦音應某律呂之聲字，即得某弦之度分。

translations.literal: Thus for string music the essentials are four: first, fix which pitch pipe's tone-syllable the string sound answers, and thereby obtain that string's degree-part.
translations.idiomatic: String music rests on four essentials: first, fix which pitch pipe's syllable the string answers to obtain that string's degree-part.

sentences.zh: 一，弦音轉調不能依次遞遷，故以宮調為準，有幾弦不移，而他弦或緊一音，或慢半音，遂成一調，而各弦七聲之分因之而變。

translations.literal: Second, string transposition cannot proceed by successive steps, so the palace mode serves as standard: several strings remain unchanged while others are tightened one tone or loosened half a tone, thereby forming a mode—and the seven-tone parts of each string shift accordingly.
translations.idiomatic: Second, transposition cannot march stepwise, so the palace mode is standard: some strings stay fixed while others tighten a whole tone or loosen a half tone to form a mode, shifting each string's seven-tone parts.

sentences.zh: 一，弦音諸調雖無二變，而定弦取音，必審二變之聲，必計二變之分，始能得其條貫，不然，宮調無所取準。

translations.literal: Third, although string modes lack the two alterations, in setting strings and taking tones one must scrutinize the two altered tones and calculate their parts before the thread can be grasped—otherwise the palace mode has no standard.
translations.idiomatic: Third, though string modes omit the two alterations, tuning requires judging altered tones and their parts; without this the palace mode lacks a standard.

sentences.zh: 一，弦音宮調，惟宮與商徵得與律呂相和為用，餘四調陰陽乖應，或淆入宮調聲字，不得自成一調。

translations.literal: Fourth, in the string palace mode only palace, merchant, and zhi can harmonize with the pitch pipes for use; the remaining four modes have yin-yang mismatch, or their syllables blur into palace mode, and cannot stand as modes of their own.
translations.idiomatic: Fourth, in string palace mode only palace, merchant, and zhi harmonize with the pipes; the other four modes mismatch yin and yang or collapse into palace syllables and cannot stand alone.

sentences.zh: 即此四者，條分縷析，則弦音旋宮轉調之法備矣。

translations.literal: With these four points analyzed strand by strand, the method of circulating modes and transposing keys in string sound is complete.
translations.idiomatic: These four points, analyzed in detail, complete the method of circulating modes and transposition for strings.

sentences.zh: 樂之學既微，自古言者又歧說繁滋，莫衷一是。

translations.literal: The study of music having grown faint, and those who spoke of it from antiquity having proliferated conflicting doctrines, no single view could prevail.
translations.idiomatic: Music studies had faded, and ancient authorities multiplied conflicting doctrines until no single view prevailed.

sentences.zh: 子長、孟堅時已異同，隋、唐登歌，雜蘇祗婆龜茲樂，以律呂文之，神瞽弗世，等於詩亡。

translations.literal: Even in the times of Sima Qian and Ban Gu they already differed; Sui and Tang court hymns mixed in Zhemo Tupo's Kucha music, glossing it with pitch-pipe terminology—when divine hearing no longer passed down the age, it was as though the Odes had perished.
translations.idiomatic: Sima Qian and Ban Gu already disagreed; Sui and Tang court hymns mixed in Zhemo Tupo's Kucha music under pitch-pipe terminology—once divine hearing ceased to pass down, music was as lost as the Odes.

sentences.zh: 宋人李照、和峴、范鎮、蔡元定之徒，稍有志於復古，然但資肊驗，或且飾以陰陽郛廓之說，明鄭世子載堉始以勾股譚律度。

translations.literal: Song men such as Li Zhao, He Xian, Fan Zhen, and Cai Yuanding still aspired to restore antiquity, yet relied only on piecemeal verification, or even adorned their work with yin-yang and cosmological doctrine; only in Ming did Prince Zhu Zai of the Zheng clan begin to treat pitch and measure with right triangles and the gougu method.
translations.idiomatic: Song scholars Li Zhao, He Xian, Fan Zhen, and Cai Yuanding still sought antiquity but relied on piecemeal tests, sometimes draped in yin-yang cosmology; only in Ming did Prince Zhu Zai of Zheng apply gougu geometry to pitch and measure.

sentences.zh: 帝本長疇人術，加之以密率，基之以實測，管音弦分千載之襲繆，至是乃定。

translations.literal: The emperor himself was long versed in calendrical arts; adding precise ratios and grounding them in actual measurement, the thousand-year errors of pipe sound and string division were at last fixed.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor was himself versed in calendrical arts; adding precise ratios and real measurement, he at last corrected the millennial errors of pipe pitch and string division.

sentences.zh: 明年書成，分三編：曰正律審音，發明黃鍾起數，及縱長、體積、面冪、周徑律呂損益之理，管弦律度旋宮之法；

translations.literal: The next year the work was completed and divided into three compilations: Zhènglǜ Shěnyīn, expounding the yellow bell's starting number and the principles of length, volume, face power, circumference, diameter, pitch-pipe diminishment and augmentation, and the methods of pipe-and-string pitch, measure, and circulating modes;
translations.idiomatic: The following year it was finished in three parts: Zhènglǜ Shěnyīn, on the yellow bell's starting number, length, volume, face area, circumference, diameter, pipe diminishment and augmentation, and pipe-string circulation;

sentences.zh: 曰和聲定樂，明八音制器之要，詳考古今之同異；

translations.literal: Héshēng Dìngyuè, clarifying the essentials of fashioning the eight kinds of sound and detailing ancient and modern similarities and differences;
translations.idiomatic: Héshēng Dìngyuè, on the eight sounds, instrument-making, and ancient versus modern practice;

sentences.zh: 曰協均度曲，取波爾都哈兒國人徐日昇及意大裡亞國人德裡格所講聲律節度，證以經史所載律呂宮調諸法，分配陰陽二均字譜，賜名曰律呂正義。

translations.literal: Xiéjūn Dùqǔ, taking the pitch and rhythm taught by the Portuguese Thomas Pereira and the Italian Teodorico Pedrini, verified against pitch-pipe and mode methods recorded in the classics, assigning yin-yang registers and syllable notation, and bestowing the title Lǚlǜ Zhèngyì.
translations.idiomatic: Xiéjūn Dùqǔ, drawing on Thomas Pereira of Portugal and Teodorico Pedrini of Italy, checked against classical pipe and mode methods, assigned yin-yang registers and notation, and received the title Lǚlǜ Zhèngyì.

sentences.zh: 蘭生、廷珍等皆賜及第，進官有差。

translations.literal: Lansheng, Tingzhen, and the others were all granted jinshi degrees and promoted in rank by varying degrees.
translations.idiomatic: Lansheng, Tingzhen, and the rest received jinshi degrees and promotions of varying rank.

sentences.zh: 既又諭改訂中和樂章聲調，曰：「殿陛所奏中和樂章，皆沿明代，句有長短，體制類詞，曾因不雅，命大學士陳廷敬等改撰，章法皆以四字為句，而樂人未嫻聲調，仍以長短句湊拍歌之。

translations.literal: Thereupon he also ordered the revision of the tonal patterns of the Zhonghe Yuezhang, saying: "The Zhonghe Yuezhang performed before the throne all follow the Ming dynasty; the lines vary in length and the form resembles lyric poetry. Because they were inelegant, the Grand Academician Chen Tingjing and others were ordered to rewrite them—all stanzas in four-character lines—but the musicians were not skilled in tonal patterns and still fitted the lines to long-and-short phrases for singing.
translations.idiomatic: He also ordered revision of the Zhonghe Yuezhang tones, saying: "The Zhonghe Yuezhang performed at court still follow Ming forms: lines of uneven length in a lyric style. Deeming them inelegant, I had Grand Academician Chen Tingjing rewrite them in four-character lines, yet the musicians, unskilled in tonal patterns, still sang them to long-and-short phrasing.

sentences.zh: 今考舊調已得，宮商節奏甚為和平，必使歌章字句亦隨韻逗，則章明而宮聲諧，其著南書房翰林同大學士詳定以聞。」

translations.literal: Now that the old melodies have been recovered and the palace and merchant rhythms are quite harmonious, the sung text must follow the rhyme pauses in its lines—then the text will be clear and the palace tone harmonious. Have the Hanlin Academicians of the Southern Studio together with the Grand Academicians examine and fix this in detail and report.
translations.idiomatic: The old melodies are now recovered and palace and merchant rhythms are harmonious; the sung text must follow the rhyme pauses so text and tone align. Let the Southern Studio Hanlin and Grand Academicians examine this in detail and report."

sentences.zh: 是年十一月冬至，躬祀圜丘，遂用新定樂律。

translations.literal: That year, on the winter solstice in the eleventh month, he personally sacrificed at the Circular Mound and thereupon employed the newly fixed pitch standards.
translations.idiomatic: That winter solstice in the eleventh month, the emperor personally sacrificed at the Circular Mound and adopted the newly fixed pitch standards.

sentences.zh: 五十四年，改造圜丘壇，金鐘玉磬，各十有六。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fourth year, the Circular Mound altar was rebuilt; gold bells and jade chimes, sixteen of each.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fourth year they rebuilt the Circular Mound altar, with sixteen gold bells and sixteen jade chimes.

sentences.zh: 五十五年，頒中和韶樂於直省文廟。

translations.literal: In the fifty-fifth year, the Zhonghe Shaoyue was issued to Confucian temples in the directly administered provinces.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-fifth year the Zhonghe Shaoyue was distributed to Confucian temples in the metropolitan provinces.

sentences.zh: 初，樂章既改用「平」，而直省仍沿用「和」，至是從禮部請，始頒行焉。

translations.literal: Initially, though hymn titles had been changed to "Ping," the provinces still used "He"; only now, following the Board of Rites' request, were they first promulgated.
translations.idiomatic: Hymn titles had already been changed to "Ping," but the provinces still used "He"; only now, at the Board of Rites' request, were the new titles promulgated.

sentences.zh: 世宗雍正二年，定耕耤三十六禾詞，耕耤筵宴樂制，進筵，丹陛樂奏雨暘時若之章，進酒，管弦樂奏五穀豐登之章，進饌，清樂奏家給人足之章，其辭皆大學士蔣廷錫撰。

translations.literal: In the second year of the Yongzheng reign, the thirty-six grain hymns for the Ploughing and Weeding ceremony were fixed, as were banquet music rules: at presentation of the feast, Dangdi music performed the "Yuyang Shiruo" chapter; at presentation of wine, orchestra music performed "Wugu Fengdeng"; at presentation of food, qing music performed "Jiaji Renzu"—all texts by Grand Academician Jiang Tingxi.
translations.idiomatic: In Yongzheng 2 they fixed the thirty-six grain hymns and ploughing banquet music: Dangdi music for the feast course ("Yǔyáng Shírùo"), orchestra music for wine ("Wǔgǔ Fēngdēng"), qing music for food ("Jiājì Rénzú")—all composed by Grand Academician Jiang Tingxi.

sentences.zh: 後又定祭時應宮、祭風伯廟、教坊司作樂，祭雷師、雲師廟，和聲署作樂，官民婚嫁，品官鼓樂人不得過十二，生、監、軍、民不得過八人，著為令。

translations.literal: Later were also fixed: music for the Time-Appropriate Palace sacrifice, the Wind Earl Temple (music by the Court Entertainment Office), the Thunder Master and Cloud Master temples (music by the Harmony Office); for official and common weddings, ranked officials' drum musicians might not exceed twelve, students, licentiates, soldiers, and commoners not eight—promulgated as statute.
translations.idiomatic: They also fixed music for the Time-Appropriate Palace and Wind Earl Temple (Court Entertainment Office), and for the Thunder Master and Cloud Master temples (Harmony Office). For weddings, ranked officials were limited to twelve drum musicians and students, licentiates, soldiers, and commoners to eight—enacted as law.

sentences.zh: 高宗即位，銳意製作，莊親王允祿自聖祖時監修律算三書，至是仍典樂事。

translations.literal: When the Gaozong emperor acceded, he was keen on creative reform; Prince Zhuang Yunlu, who since the Kangxi era had supervised compilation of the three books on pitch and measure, at this time still directed music affairs.
translations.idiomatic: On Gaozong's accession he pursued institutional reform; Prince Zhuang Yunlu, who since Kangxi had overseen the three books on pitch and measure, still directed music.

sentences.zh: 乾隆六年，殿陛奏中和韶樂，帝覺音律節奏與樂章不協，因命和親王弘晝同允祿奏試，允祿因言：「明代舊制，樂章以五、六、七字為句，而音律之節奏隨之，樂章音律俱八句，故長短相協。

translations.literal: In the sixth year of Qianlong, the Zhonghe Shaoyue was performed before the throne; the emperor felt pitch rhythm and hymn text were out of accord, and ordered Prince He Hongzhou together with Yunlu to perform trials. Yunlu then said: "Under the Ming old system, hymn lines were five, six, or seven characters, and pitch rhythm followed; hymn and pitch alike had eight lines, so length matched.
translations.idiomatic: In Qianlong 6 the Zhonghe Shaoyue was played at court; the emperor found pitch rhythm and hymn text misaligned and ordered Prince He Hongzhou and Yunlu to test them. Yunlu said: "Under Ming practice, hymn lines ran five, six, or seven characters and pitch rhythm followed; both hymn and pitch had eight lines, so lengths matched.

sentences.zh: 今殿陛樂若定以四字為句，則與壇廟無殊，惟樂章更定，大典攸關，謂宜會同大學士、禮部將樂章十二成詳議，令翰林改擬進覽。」

translations.literal: If court music is now fixed at four characters per line, it will differ in no way from altar and temple music; yet hymn revision bears on great rites. It is fitting to convene Grand Academicians and the Board of Rites for detailed deliberation on the twelve suites, and have the Hanlin revise and submit for imperial review."
translations.idiomatic: If court music is fixed at four characters per line, it will be no different from altar and temple music; yet revising the hymns touches great rites. Grand Academicians and the Board of Rites should deliberate the twelve suites in detail, and the Hanlin should revise and submit for review."

sentences.zh: 尋大學士鄂爾泰等議：「樂章十二成內，惟淑平、順平二成每章八句，其十成樂章每章各十句，句四字，而按之音律，則每章八句，每句六、七、八字，以十句四字樂章，和以八句六、七、八字之音律，長短抑揚，宜不盡協。

translations.literal: Soon Grand Academician Ortai and others deliberated: "Among the twelve suites, only Shuping and Shunping have eight lines per stanza; the other ten have ten four-character lines per stanza, yet when matched to pitch rhythm each stanza has eight lines of six, seven, or eight characters. To set ten four-character hymn lines to eight lines of six-, seven-, or eight-character pitch rhythm—length and cadence cannot fully agree.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Academician Ortai and others replied: "Of the twelve suites, only Shúpíng and Shùnpíng have eight lines per stanza; the other ten have ten four-character lines, yet pitch rhythm gives eight lines of six, seven, or eight characters. Ten four-character hymn lines set to eight longer rhythmic lines cannot fully align in length and cadence.

sentences.zh: 應將樂章字句，按音律之節奏以調和之，章酌從八句，句無拘四言。」

translations.literal: The hymn lines should be harmonized to pitch rhythm; stanzas should generally follow eight lines, with lines not confined to four characters."
translations.idiomatic: Hymn lines should be adjusted to pitch rhythm; stanzas should generally use eight lines, without confining lines to four characters."

sentences.zh: 奏可。

translations.literal: The memorial was approved.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was approved.

sentences.zh: 舊中和樂編鐘內倍夷則四鐘在黃鍾正律之前，帝疑其舛，兼詢編鐘倍律及設而不作之故於臣工，時張照以刑部侍郎副允祿管部，名知樂，奏言：「編鐘之制，以十六鐘為一架，陽律八為一懸，在上；

translations.literal: In the old Zhonghe music, among the arranged bells the four bells of doubled Yize stood before the standard Huangzhong pitch; the emperor suspected error and also inquired of his ministers on doubled bells and bells set but not struck. At the time Zhang Zhao, Vice Minister of Justice assisting Yunlu in managing the ministry and famed for musical knowledge, memorialized: "The arranged-bell system takes sixteen bells as one frame: eight yang pitches as one suspension above;
translations.idiomatic: In the old Zhonghe music, four doubled-Yíze bells stood before standard Huángzhōng in the bell frame; the emperor suspected error and asked ministers why some doubled bells were set but not struck. Zhang Zhao, Vice Minister of Justice assisting Yunlu and famed for music, memorialized: "The bell frame has sixteen bells: eight yang pitches as the upper suspension;

sentences.zh: 陰律八為一懸，在下。

translations.literal: eight yin pitches as one suspension below.
translations.idiomatic: eight yin pitches as the lower suspension.

sentences.zh: 陽自陽，陰自陰。

translations.literal: Yang with yang, yin with yin.
translations.idiomatic: Yang with yang, yin with yin.

sentences.zh: 律呂之法，必有倍、半，然後高低清濁具備，以成旋宮之用。

translations.literal: In the method of pitch pipes, there must be doubled and halved tones before high and low, clear and muddy, are complete, to accomplish circulating-mode use.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch pipes require doubled and halved tones before the full range of high and low, clear and muddy, is available for circulating modes.

sentences.zh: 故陽律有倍蕤賓、倍夷則、倍無射在黃鍾之前，有半黃鍾、半太簇、半姑洗在無射之後。

translations.literal: Thus among yang pitches are doubled Ruibin, doubled Yize, and doubled Wushe before Huangzhong, and half Huangzhong, half Taicu, and half Guxian after Wushe.
translations.idiomatic: Yang pitches therefore include doubled Ruíbīn, doubled Yíze, and doubled Wúshè before Huángzhōng, and half Huángzhōng, half Tàicù, and half Gǔxiàn after Wúshè.

sentences.zh: 陰律則有倍林鍾、倍南呂、倍應鍾在大呂之前，有半大呂、半夾鍾、半仲呂在應鍾之後。

translations.literal: Among yin pitches are doubled Linzhong, doubled Nanlu, and doubled Yingzhong before Dalu, and half Dalu, half Jiazhong, and half Zhonglu after Yingzhong.
translations.idiomatic: Yin pitches include doubled Línzhōng, doubled Nánlǜ, and doubled Yīngzhōng before Dàlǜ, and half Dàlǜ, half Jiázhōng, and half Zhònglǜ after Yīngzhōng.

sentences.zh: 倍蕤賓以還，則聲過低而啞，半仲呂以還，則聲過高而促，故不用。

translations.literal: From doubled Ruibin downward the sound is too low and muffled; from half Zhonglu upward it is too high and hurried—hence they are not used.
translations.idiomatic: From doubled Ruíbīn down the sound is too low and muffled; from half Zhònglǜ up it is too high and hurried—so they are not used.

sentences.zh: 編鐘無倍蕤賓、倍林鍾，亦無六半律，以編鐘具八，其音中和，已足於用。

translations.literal: The arranged bells have no doubled Ruibin or Linzhong, nor the six half pitches; with eight bells complete, their sound is harmonious and sufficient for use.
translations.idiomatic: The bell frame omits doubled Ruíbīn and Línzhōng and the six half pitches; eight bells suffice, their tone harmonious for use.

sentences.zh: 低不至倍蕤賓、倍林鍾，高不至六半律，其序以從低至高，濁至清，排列為次。

translations.literal: Low does not reach doubled Ruibin or Linzhong; high does not reach the six half pitches; the order runs from low to high, muddy to clear, arranged in sequence.
translations.idiomatic: The range stops before doubled Ruíbīn and Línzhōng and above the six half pitches, ordered from low to high, muddy to clear.

sentences.zh: 倍夷則、倍無射當在黃鍾之前，倍南呂、倍應鍾當在大呂之前，與簫管之長短，琴弦之鉅細為一例。

translations.literal: Doubled Yize and Wushe should stand before Huangzhong; doubled Nanlu and Yingzhong before Dalu—the same principle as long and short panpipes and thick and thin strings.
translations.idiomatic: Doubled Yíze and Wúshè belong before Huángzhōng; doubled Nánlǜ and Yīngzhōng before Dàlǜ—as with panpipe length and string thickness.

sentences.zh: 排簫倍夷則、倍無射二管在黃鍾之前，倍南呂、倍應鍾二管在大呂之前。

translations.literal: In the panpipe array, the two pipes of doubled Yize and Wushe stand before Huangzhong; the two of doubled Nanlu and Yingzhong before Dalu.
translations.idiomatic: In the panpipe array, doubled Yíze and Wúshè pipes stand before Huángzhōng; doubled Nánlǜ and Yīngzhōng before Dàlǜ.

sentences.zh: ★A9之倍徵、倍羽二弦在宮弦之前，若琴弦簫管易位，則音不可諧，是以編鐘之次第同於弦管。」

translations.literal: On the qin, the doubled-zhi and doubled-yu two strings stand before the palace string; if strings, panpipes, and pipes swap places, the sound cannot harmonize—hence the bell sequence matches strings and pipes."
translations.idiomatic: On the qin, the doubled-zhī and doubled-yǔ strings stand before the palace string; if strings, panpipes, and pipes are rearranged, tone cannot harmonize—so bell order follows strings and pipes."

sentences.zh: 又奏：「編鐘一架，上八下八，上陽律，下陰呂。

translations.literal: He further memorialized: "One bell frame: eight above, eight below; yang pitches above, yin pipes below.
translations.idiomatic: He added: "One frame: eight bells above, eight below; yang pitches above, yin pipes below.

sentences.zh: 考擊之節，南郊、廟祀及臨朝大典，皆用黃鍾為宮，北郊、月壇，則用大呂為宮。

translations.literal: In performance, for the Southern Suburb, temple sacrifices, and court great ceremonies Huangzhong is palace; for the Northern Suburb and Moon Altar, Dalu is palace.
translations.idiomatic: In performance, the Southern Suburb, temple rites, and great court ceremonies use Huángzhōng as palace; the Northern Suburb and Moon Altar use Dàlǜ.

sentences.zh: 用黃鍾為宮，則擊上鐘，用大呂為宮，則擊下鐘。

translations.literal: When Huangzhong is palace, the upper bells are struck; when Dalu is palace, the lower bells.
translations.idiomatic: With Huángzhōng as palace the upper bells are struck; with Dàlǜ as palace, the lower.

sentences.zh: 臨朝以下鐘易置於上而擊之，非下八鐘不擊也。

translations.literal: At court audiences the lower bells are simply moved above for striking—it is not that the lower eight are never struck.
translations.idiomatic: At court audiences the lower bells are moved above for striking; the lower eight are not left unused.

sentences.zh: 又八鐘原祗七音，姑洗為宮，黃鍾起調為工字，倍夷則、無射為變徵，太簇為變宮，三鐘不入調，是以不擊。

translations.literal: Moreover, the eight bells originally yield only seven tones: Guxian as palace, Huangzhong starting the mode as the gong syllable; doubled Yize and Wushe as altered-zhi; Taicu as altered-palace—three bells fall outside the mode and are not struck.
translations.idiomatic: The eight bells originally yield only seven tones: Gǔxiàn as palace, Huángzhōng opening the mode as the gōng syllable; doubled Yíze and Wúshè as altered-zhī; Tàicù as altered-palace—three bells lie outside the mode and are not struck.

sentences.zh: 工字調外，則惟二鐘不擊。

translations.literal: Outside the gong-mode, only two bells are not struck.
translations.idiomatic: Outside the gōng mode, only two bells go unstruck.

sentences.zh: 如以太簇為宮，倍無射起調為尺字，則倍夷則、無射、太簇三鐘皆擊，而黃鍾為變宮，夷則為變徵，二鐘又當不擊矣。

translations.literal: If Taicu is palace and doubled Wushe opens the mode as the chi syllable, then doubled Yize, Wushe, and Taicu are all struck, while Huangzhong becomes altered-palace and Yize altered-zhi—two bells again should not be struck.
translations.idiomatic: If Tàicù is palace and doubled Wúshè opens the chǐ syllable, doubled Yíze, Wúshè, and Tàicù are struck, while Huángzhōng becomes altered-palace and Yíze altered-zhī—two bells again go unstruck.

sentences.zh: 因相沿俱以黃鍾調為黃鍾宮，儒生不知音律，謂黃鍾為聲氣之元，萬物之母，郊廟、朝廷用之吉，否則凶。

translations.literal: Because all along Huangzhong mode was taken as Huangzhong palace, Confucian scholars ignorant of pitch law say Huangzhong is the origin of sound and breath, mother of the myriad things—auspicious for suburban altars and court, otherwise inauspicious.
translations.idiomatic: Custom had long treated Huángzhōng mode as Huángzhōng palace; scholars ignorant of pitch law called Huángzhōng the origin of sound and breath, mother of all things—auspicious at suburban altars and court, otherwise ill-omened.

sentences.zh: 不知黃鍾為宮，其第一聲便是下羽，除變宮、變徵不入調，商、角、徵、羽必須迭用。

translations.literal: They do not know that with Huangzhong as palace, the first tone is lower yu; except altered-palace and altered-zhi, which fall outside the mode, merchant, horn, zhi, and yu must be used in turn.
translations.idiomatic: They did not see that with Huángzhōng as palace the first tone is lower yǔ; except altered-palace and altered-zhī, shāng, jué, zhī, and yǔ must alternate.

sentences.zh: 若聲聲皆是黃鍾，晏子所謂琴瑟專一，誰能聽之。

translations.literal: If every sound were Huangzhong, it would be what Yanzi called lute and zither all one note—who could listen?
translations.idiomatic: If every note were Huángzhōng, it would be Yanzi's "lute and zither all one note—who could listen?"

sentences.zh: 況大武之樂，即是無射為宮，載之國語。

translations.literal: Moreover, the music of the Great Martial used Wushe as palace, as recorded in the Guoyu.
translations.idiomatic: The Great Martial music used Wúshè as palace, as the Guoyu records.

sentences.zh: 無射乃陽律之窮，而武王用之，則十二月各以其律為宮，無所不可，亦明矣。」

translations.literal: Wushe is the exhaustion of yang pitch, yet King Wu used it—so each of the twelve months may take its pitch as palace; nothing is forbidden, which is clear."
translations.idiomatic: Wúshè is the limit of yang pitch, yet King Wu used it—so any month may take its pitch as palace; that much is clear."

sentences.zh: 上是之，命如故。

translations.literal: The emperor approved and ordered matters to remain as before.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor approved and left the arrangement unchanged.

sentences.zh: 當是時，清興百餘年矣，古學萌芽，儒者毛奇齡、李□恭、胡彥升、江永輩多著書言樂事，考證益邃密。

translations.literal: At that time the Qing dynasty had flourished more than a century; ancient learning was sprouting; scholars Mao Qiling, Li Chong, Hu Yansheng, Jiang Yong, and others wrote extensively on music, and textual verification grew ever more rigorous.
translations.idiomatic: By then the Qing had flourished over a century; ancient learning was reviving; Mao Qiling, Li Chong, Hu Yansheng, Jiang Yong, and others wrote extensively on music, and scholarship grew ever more rigorous.

sentences.zh: 帝亦慕簫韶九成之盛，剬詩緝頌，勇於改為，欲以文致太平。

translations.literal: The emperor also admired the splendor of the ninefold Xiaoshao, carved poems and compiled eulogies, and was bold in reform, wishing to bring peace through culture.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor also admired the splendor of the ninefold Xiāosháo, composed poems and compiled eulogies, and pursued reform boldly, seeking peace through culture.

sentences.zh: 聖祖時雖編定樂書，大抵稽於音律，而樂章句逗無譜，不與音相應。

translations.literal: In the Kangxi era, though music books were compiled, they largely investigated pitch law, while hymn phrasing had no notation and did not answer to the tones.
translations.idiomatic: Kangxi had compiled music books focused chiefly on pitch law, but hymn phrasing lacked notation and did not match the tones.

sentences.zh: 有協律高萬霖者，耆年審音，改定宮譜，然祗壇廟之樂。

translations.literal: There was Gao Wanlin, a harmonizer of pitch, aged and skilled in sound, who revised palace notation—yet only for altar and temple music.
translations.idiomatic: Gao Wanlin, an aged harmonizer skilled in sound, revised palace notation—but only for altar and temple music.

sentences.zh: 朝會清歌，仍踵前繆。

translations.literal: Court clear songs still followed former errors.
translations.idiomatic: Court clear songs still followed old errors.

sentences.zh: 照遂請續纂律呂書，謂「前代墜典，宜見刊正」，許之。

translations.literal: Zhao then requested continued compilation of pitch books, saying "fallen institutions of former ages should be published and corrected"—which was granted.
translations.idiomatic: Zhang Zhao then asked to continue compiling pitch books, saying "fallen institutions of former ages should be published and corrected"—and was permitted.

sentences.zh: 開館纂修，仍命允祿監其事。

translations.literal: A compilation office was opened, with Yunlu again ordered to supervise.
translations.idiomatic: A compilation office was opened, again under Yunlu's supervision.

sentences.zh: 未幾，館臣上議：「壇廟樂章字譜，天壇、太廟、朝日壇俱黃鍾為宮，地壇、夕月壇大呂為宮，近於南齊祗用黃鍾之說，而兼清濁二均。

translations.literal: Before long the compilers memorialized: "For altar and temple hymn notation, the Temple of Heaven, Imperial Ancestral Temple, and Sun Altar all use Huangzhong as palace; the Earth Altar and Moon Altar use Dalu as palace—close to the Southern Qi doctrine of using only Huangzhong, yet combining clear and muddy registers.
translations.idiomatic: Soon the compilers proposed: "Altar and temple hymn notation assigns Huángzhōng as palace for the Temple of Heaven, Imperial Ancestral Temple, and Sun Altar, and Dàlǜ for the Earth and Moon altars—near the Southern Qi idea of Huangzhong alone, yet mixing clear and muddy registers.

sentences.zh: 及於大呂，雖義有可取，但編鐘器內必有設而不作者，同於隋以前啞鐘之誚。

translations.literal: As for Dalu, though the rationale has merit, within the bell frame there must be bells set but not struck—the same reproach as the mute bells before Sui.
translations.idiomatic: Dàlǜ is defensible in theory, but the frame must include bells set but not struck—the same reproach as pre-Sui mute bells.

sentences.zh: 我皇上製作定世，繼述休明，允宜博考詳稽，以襄盛典。

translations.literal: Our emperor's creative ordering fixes the age and continues enlightened rule; it is fitting to investigate broadly and in detail to assist the great ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor's creative ordering fixes the age; a broad, careful inquiry should assist the great ceremony.

sentences.zh: 夫言禮樂必宗成周，顧周代遙邈，文不足徵，所可考者，莫如周禮。

translations.literal: In speaking of ritual and music one must take the Zhou as authority; yet the Zhou is remote and texts insufficient for proof—what can be examined is nothing better than the Zhouli.
translations.idiomatic: Ritual and music must look to the Zhou, but the Zhou is remote and texts scarce—the Zhouli is the best evidence available.

sentences.zh: 而周禮所載圜鐘為宮祭天、函鐘為宮祭地、黃鍾為宮祭宗廟之說，圜鐘、函鐘不知何律。

translations.literal: The Zhouli records that the Yuanzhong is palace for Heaven sacrifice, the Hanzhong for Earth, and Huangzhong for the ancestral temple—but what pitches Yuanzhong and Hanzhong are is unknown.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhouli says Yuánzhōng is palace for Heaven, Hánzhōng for Earth, and Huángzhōng for the ancestral temple—but which pitches Yuánzhōng and Hánzhōng denote is unknown.

sentences.zh: 鄭康成以圜鐘為夾鍾，函鐘為林鍾，祭地用林鍾，義則善矣。

translations.literal: Zheng Xuan took Yuanzhong as Jiazhong and Hanzhong as Linzhong; using Linzhong for Earth sacrifice is reasonable in principle.
translations.idiomatic: Zheng Xuan identified Yuánzhōng with Jiázhōng and Hánzhōng with Línzhōng; Línzhōng for Earth sacrifice is reasonable in principle.

sentences.zh: 然林鍾何以又稱函鐘，則亦無所據也。

translations.literal: Yet why Linzhong is also called Hanzhong has no basis.
translations.idiomatic: Yet why Línzhōng is also called Hánzhōng has no textual basis.

sentences.zh: 惟准六樂次第論之，有函鐘而無林鍾，則知函鐘即林鍾，然六樂又有夾鍾無圜鐘，其以圜鐘為夾鍾，謂夾鍾生於房、心之間，房、心大辰，天帝之明堂，則用甘公、石申戰代星家之言，以解七百年前周公之制度，誠非篤詁。

translations.literal: Only by the sequence of the Six Music can one argue: there is Hanzhong but no Linzhong, so Hanzhong is Linzhong; yet the Six Music also has Jiazhong and no Yuanzhong. To take Yuanzhong as Jiazhong because Jiazhong is born between Fang and Xin, Fang and Xin being great asterisms and the Bright Hall of the Heavenly Emperor, is to explain a system of the Duke of Zhou seven hundred years earlier with Gan Gong and Shi Shen's Warring States star lore—hardly sound exegesis.
translations.idiomatic: By the Six Music sequence there is Hánzhōng but no Línzhōng, so Hánzhōng must be Línzhōng; yet the Six Music has Jiázhōng and no Yuánzhōng. Calling Yuánzhōng Jiázhōng because Jiázhōng lies between Fáng and Xīn—the Bright Hall of the Heavenly Emperor—imports Warring States star lore to explain Duke of Zhou ritual seven centuries earlier—hardly sound exegesis.

sentences.zh: 李光地謂祭天以黃鍾為宮，祭宗廟以圜鐘為宮，圜黃互錯，諸儒相承而不知改。

translations.literal: Li Guangdi held that Heaven sacrifice uses Huangzhong as palace and the ancestral temple Yuanzhong—Yuan and Huang crossed, transmitted by the ru without correction.
translations.idiomatic: Li Guangdi held Heaven sacrifice used Huángzhōng as palace and the ancestral temple Yuánzhōng—yuán and huáng transposed, handed down uncorrected.

sentences.zh: 揆以春禘之文，則夾鍾之月也，雖若近理，然亦出於肊見。

translations.literal: Measured against the spring di text, it is the month of Jiazhong—seemingly reasonable, yet still a private surmise.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against the spring dì text it is the month of Jiázhōng—plausible, yet still private surmise.

sentences.zh: 周禮本言祭天以圜鐘為宮，其下即雲黃鍾為角，一章之樂，斷無黃鍾既為宮，而又為角之理。

translations.literal: The Zhouli itself says Heaven sacrifice takes Yuanzhong as palace, and immediately below says Huangzhong is horn—in one suite's music there is no reason Huangzhong should be both palace and horn.
