translations.idiomatic: The Zhouli says Heaven sacrifice takes Yuánzhōng as palace and immediately adds Huángzhōng as jué—in one suite Huángzhōng cannot be both palace and jué.

sentences.zh: 六樂次第，清濁各一均，黃鍾與大呂配祀天神，太簇與應鍾配祭地祗，姑洗與南呂配祀四望，蕤賓與函鐘配祭山川，夷則與仲呂配享姜嫄，無射與夾鍾配享先祖，以律之次第分神之尊卑。

translations.literal: In the Six Music sequence, clear and muddy each have one register: Huangzhong with Dalu for heavenly spirits; Taicu with Yingzhong for earthly spirits; Guxian with Nanlu for the Four Peaks; Ruibin with Hanzhong for mountains and rivers; Yize with Zhonglu for Jiang Yuan; Wushe with Jiazhong for remote ancestors—ranking spirits by pitch order.
translations.idiomatic: The Six Music sequence pairs clear and muddy registers: Huángzhōng with Dàlǜ for heavenly spirits; Tàicù with Yīngzhōng for earthly spirits; Gǔxiàn with Nánlǜ for the Four Peaks; Ruíbīn with Hánzhōng for mountains and rivers; Yíze with Zhònglǜ for Jiāng Yuán; Wúshè with Jiázhōng for remote ancestors—ranking spirits by pitch order.

sentences.zh: 顧律呂同用，而清濁之間，有同均者，有不同均者，見諸實用，難於施行。

translations.literal: Yet when pitch pipes are used together, among clear and muddy some share a register and some do not—in practice this is hard to execute.
translations.idiomatic: In practice, mixing registers that share or differ among clear and muddy pitches is hard to execute.

sentences.zh: 是以歷代皆欲仰法周制，而苦無所憑。

translations.literal: Hence every dynasty wished to follow the Zhou yet found nothing to rely on.
translations.idiomatic: Hence every dynasty wished to follow the Zhou yet lacked a workable model.

sentences.zh: 惟唐貞觀時祖孝孫定為祭圜丘以黃鍾為宮，方澤以林鍾為宮，宗廟以太簇為宮，朝賀宴饗則隨月用呂為宮，最為通論。

translations.literal: Only in the Zhenguan era of Tang did Zu Xiaosun fix: Circular Mound sacrifice with Huangzhong as palace, Square Pond with Linzhong, ancestral temple with Taicu, court congratulations and banquets taking the month's pitch as palace—the most comprehensive doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: Only in Tang Zhenguan did Zu Xiaosun fix Huángzhōng for the Circular Mound, Línzhōng for the Square Pond, Tàicù for the ancestral temple, and the month's pitch for court congratulations and banquets—the most comprehensive doctrine.

sentences.zh: 蓋黃鍾子位，天之統也。

translations.literal: For Huangzhong is the zi position, the unity of Heaven.
translations.idiomatic: Huángzhōng is the zǐ position, Heaven's unity.

sentences.zh: 乾位在亥，亥前為子，十二辰之始。

translations.literal: The Qian position lies at hai; before hai is zi—the start of the twelve branches.
translations.idiomatic: Qián lies at hài; before hài is zǐ—the start of the twelve branches.

sentences.zh: 黃鍾下生林鍾，林鐘未位，地之統也。

translations.literal: Huangzhong generates Linzhong downward; Linzhong is the wei position, the unity of Earth.
translations.idiomatic: Huángzhōng generates Línzhōng downward; Línzhōng is the wèi position, Earth's unity.

sentences.zh: 坤位在申，陽順陰逆，申前為未。

translations.literal: The Kun position lies at shen; yang proceeds and yin reverses—before shen is wei.
translations.idiomatic: Kūn lies at shēn; yang advances and yin reverses—before shēn is wèi.

sentences.zh: 自子至午七律，而天之道備，自未至丑七律，而地之道備。

translations.literal: From zi to wu are seven pitches, and the Way of Heaven is complete; from wei to chou are seven pitches, and the Way of Earth is complete.
translations.idiomatic: Seven pitches from zǐ to wǔ complete Heaven's Way; seven from wèi to chǒu complete Earth's Way.

sentences.zh: 故黃鍾屬天，林鍾屬地，林鍾上生太簇，太簇寅位，人之統也。

translations.literal: Hence Huangzhong belongs to Heaven, Linzhong to Earth; Linzhong generates Taicu upward—Taicu is the yin position, the unity of Man.
translations.idiomatic: Huángzhōng belongs to Heaven, Línzhōng to Earth; Línzhōng generates Tàicù upward—Tàicù is the yín position, humanity's unity.

sentences.zh: 故以祀宗廟，先儒所謂萬物本乎天，人本乎祖之義也。

translations.literal: Hence it is used for the ancestral temple—the meaning the early ru called "the myriad things root in Heaven, man roots in the ancestors."
translations.idiomatic: Hence it serves the ancestral temple—the early ru's "myriad things root in Heaven, man roots in the ancestors."

sentences.zh: 光地亦稱祖孝孫特有遠識，而歷代用樂，此最近古。

translations.literal: Guangdi also praised Zu Xiaosun for far-sightedness, and among dynastic music this is nearest antiquity.
translations.idiomatic: Guangdi also praised Zu Xiaosun's far-sightedness; among dynastic practice this is nearest antiquity.

sentences.zh: 臣等愚見，謂宜遵聖祖律呂正義所定旋宮轉調之法，將地壇樂章改林鍾為宮，太廟樂章改太簇為宮，社稷壇亦地也，亦宜改用林鍾為宮。

translations.literal: Your servants' humble view is that one should follow the circulating-mode method fixed in the Kangxi Lülü Zhengyi: change Earth Altar hymns to Linzhong as palace, Imperial Temple hymns to Taicu as palace; the Altars of Soil and Grain are also Earth and should likewise use Linzhong as palace.
translations.idiomatic: We humbly advise following the Kangxi Lǚlǜ Zhèngyì circulating-mode method: Earth Altar hymns should use Línzhōng as palace, Imperial Temple hymns Tàicù; the Altars of Soil and Grain, being Earth, should likewise use Línzhōng.

sentences.zh: 月生於西，酉，西方正位也。

translations.literal: The moon is born in the west; you is the due west position.
translations.idiomatic: The moon rises in the west; yǒu is the due-west position.

sentences.zh: 又秋分夕月，建酉之月也。

translations.literal: Moreover, the autumn equinox evening moon sacrifice falls in the month established at you.
translations.idiomatic: The autumn-equinox evening moon rite falls in the month established at yǒu.

sentences.zh: 夕月壇宜改用南呂為宮，朝日壇若以日東月西、日卯月酉論，應用夾鍾為宮，但夾鍾陰而日陽，衷以人心屬日之義，宜改用太簇為宮。

translations.literal: The Moon Altar should use Nanlu as palace; for the Sun Altar, if one argues sun east and moon west, sun mao and moon you, Jiazhong should apply—but Jiazhong is yin while the sun is yang; weighing the human heart's attachment to the sun, Taicu is fitting as palace.
translations.idiomatic: The Moon Altar should use Nánlǜ as palace; for the Sun Altar, sun-east and moon-west would suggest Jiázhōng—but Jiázhōng is yin and the sun yang; honoring the heart's attachment to the sun, Tàicù is fitting.

sentences.zh: 其朝會宴享，並應依唐祖孝孫之說，各以其月之律為宮。

translations.literal: Court congratulations and banquets should all follow Tang Zu Xiaosun, each month taking its pitch as palace.
translations.idiomatic: Court congratulations and banquets should follow Tang Zu Xiaosun, each month taking its own pitch as palace.

sentences.zh: 先農壇，農事也，宜以姑洗為宮。

translations.literal: The First-Farmer Altar concerns agriculture and should use Guxian as palace.
translations.idiomatic: The First-Farmer Altar concerns agriculture and should use Gǔxiàn as palace.

sentences.zh: 歷代帝王廟、孔子廟祭以春秋，春夾鍾、秋南呂為宮，太歲壇宜以歲始之律太簇為宮。」

translations.literal: Temples to dynastic emperors and Confucius sacrifice in spring and autumn—Jiazhong in spring, Nanlu in autumn; the Grand Year Altar should use Taicu, the pitch of year's beginning, as palace."
translations.idiomatic: Dynastic emperor and Confucius temples sacrifice in spring and autumn—Jiázhōng in spring, Nánlǜ in autumn; the Grand Year Altar should use Tàicù, the year's opening pitch, as palace."

sentences.zh: 奏上，而皇太后、皇后升座、還宮樂章律呂未定，因命禮臣集議。

translations.literal: The memorial was submitted; yet the palace and return hymns for the Empress Dowager and Empress had not been fixed in pitch—so ritual officials were ordered to deliberate.
translations.idiomatic: The memorial was submitted, but palace and return hymns for the Empress Dowager and Empress still lacked fixed pitch—so ritual officials were ordered to deliberate.

sentences.zh: 允祿議曰：「皇太后、皇后樂章應用律呂，博考前典，並無明文。

translations.literal: Yunlu deliberated: "Empress Dowager and Empress hymns should use pitch pipes; broad investigation of antiquity yields no explicit text.
translations.idiomatic: Yunlu argued: "Empress Dowager and Empress hymns should use pitch pipes, but antiquity offers no explicit rule.

sentences.zh: 惟十二律呂皆生於黃鍾，故黃鍾為聲氣之元，但既專用於南郊以尊上帝，自不便擬用。

translations.literal: Only all twelve pitches are born from Huangzhong, so Huangzhong is the origin of sound and breath—but since it is reserved for the Southern Suburb to honor the Supreme Lord, it is inconvenient to adopt.
translations.idiomatic: All twelve pitches spring from Huángzhōng, the origin of sound and breath—but Huángzhōng is reserved for the Southern Suburb to honor the Supreme Lord and cannot be reused.

sentences.zh: 且律協於乾，呂協於坤，坤元允宜用呂。

translations.literal: Moreover, pitch harmonizes with Qian and pipe with Kun; Kun's origin properly should use pipes.
translations.idiomatic: Pitch harmonizes with Qián and pipe with Kūn; Kūn's origin properly calls for yin pipes.

sentences.zh: 大呂為黃鍾之呂，擬皇太后樂以大呂為宮。

translations.literal: Dalu is Huangzhong's pipe; we propose Empress Dowager music with Dalu as palace.
translations.idiomatic: Dàlǜ is Huángzhōng's pipe; we propose Dàlǜ as palace for the Empress Dowager's music.

sentences.zh: 禮記：天子日也，日月東西相從而不已，天道也。

translations.literal: The Liji: "The Son of Heaven is the sun; sun and moon follow east and west without ceasing—this is the Way of Heaven."
translations.idiomatic: The Liji says: "The Son of Heaven is the sun; sun and moon follow east and west unceasingly—this is Heaven's Way."

sentences.zh: 酉為月之正位，援後月之義，擬皇后樂以南呂為宮。」

translations.literal: You is the moon's due position; invoking the later moon's meaning, we propose Nanlu as palace for the Empress's music."
translations.idiomatic: Yǒu is the moon's due position; invoking the later moon, we propose Nánlǜ as palace for the Empress."

sentences.zh: 履親王允祹議曰：「館臣擬皇太后樂以大呂為宮，皇后樂以南呂為宮，臣愚以為大呂、南呂並是陰呂，皇上曾有『凡慶賀大典，皇太后宮應用陽律』之旨，舊制一切大典，俱以黃鍾為宮，請仍循舊制。

translations.literal: Prince Yunxiang deliberated: "The compilers propose Dalu for the Empress Dowager and Nanlu for the Empress; your servant thinks Dalu and Nanlu are both yin pipes. The emperor once said, 'For all congratulatory great ceremonies, the Empress Dowager's palace should use yang pitch.' The old system used Huangzhong as palace for all great ceremonies; I ask to follow the old system.
translations.idiomatic: Prince Yunxiang argued: "The compilers propose Dàlǜ for the Empress Dowager and Nánlǜ for the Empress; both are yin pipes. Your Majesty once said, 'For all congratulatory great ceremonies, the Empress Dowager's palace should use yang pitch.' The old system used Huángzhōng for every great ceremony; I ask to keep it.

sentences.zh: 皇上冬至、元旦、萬壽三大節，皇太后、皇后三大節，並以黃鍾為宮。」

translations.literal: For the emperor's three great festivals at winter solstice, New Year, and Longevity, and the Empress Dowager and Empress's three great festivals, all should use Huangzhong as palace."
translations.idiomatic: For Your Majesty's winter solstice, New Year, and Longevity festivals and the Empress Dowager and Empress's three festivals, all should use Huángzhōng as palace."

sentences.zh: 帝以「大呂者，黃鍾之呂也。

translations.literal: The emperor said: "Dalu is Huangzhong's pipe.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor said: "Dàlǜ is Huángzhōng's pipe.

sentences.zh: 既用黃鍾尊上帝，林鍾尊后土，太簇尊宗廟，而議皇太后樂用大呂，大呂之序，乃在南呂後，皇后樂已用南呂，是先於皇太后也。

translations.literal: Huangzhong already honors the Supreme Lord, Linzhong honors Queen Earth, Taicu honors the ancestral temple—yet to propose Dalu for the Empress Dowager: in pitch order Dalu comes after Nanlu, while the Empress already uses Nanlu—she would precede the Empress Dowager.
translations.idiomatic: Huángzhōng honors the Supreme Lord, Línzhōng Queen Earth, Tàicù the ancestral temple—yet Dalu for the Empress Dowager would place her after Nánlǜ in pitch order while the Empress already uses Nánlǜ, putting the Empress before the Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 又方澤壇用蕤賓之呂，林鍾為宮，而社稷亦宜有別」。

translations.literal: Moreover, the Square Pond uses Ruibin's pipe with Linzhong as palace, and the Altars of Soil and Grain should also differ."
translations.idiomatic: Moreover, the Square Pond uses Ruíbīn's pipe with Línzhōng as palace; the Altars of Soil and Grain should also differ."

sentences.zh: 因命重議。

translations.literal: He therefore ordered renewed deliberation.
translations.idiomatic: He ordered the matter reconsidered.

sentences.zh: 於是館臣請定皇太后樂用南呂為宮，社稷壇祭以春秋二仲月上戊，宜以夾鍾南呂為宮。

translations.literal: Thereupon the compilers asked to fix the Empress Dowager's music with Nanlu as palace; for the Altars of Soil and Grain, sacrifices on the wu days of the second month of spring and autumn should use Jiazhong and Nanlu as palace.
translations.idiomatic: The compilers then proposed Nánlǜ as palace for the Empress Dowager; for the Altars of Soil and Grain, wǔ days in the second month of spring and autumn should use Jiázhōng and Nánlǜ.

sentences.zh: 從之。

translations.literal: This was approved.
translations.idiomatic: Approved.

sentences.zh: 七年，允祿等又奏：「太皇太后升座、還宮用中和韶樂，行禮用丹陛樂，與皇帝同，而皇太后、皇后俱用丹陛樂。

translations.literal: In the seventh year, Yunlu and others again memorialized: "For the Grand Empress Dowager's mounting the throne and return to palace, Zhonghe Shaoyue is used; for the rites, Dangdi music—as with the emperor—while the Empress Dowager and Empress both use Dangdi music.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year Yunlu memorialized: "The Grand Empress Dowager uses Zhonghe Shaoyue for mounting the throne and return, Dangdi music for the rite—as the emperor does—while the Empress Dowager and Empress both use Dangdi music.

sentences.zh: 考諸掌儀司，自來升座、還宮並用中和韶樂，緣陳廷敬撰擬樂章之時，以皇太后、皇后不敢同於太皇太后，便以丹陛名之。

translations.literal: Checking the Directorate of Ceremonies, mounting the throne and return have always used Zhonghe Shaoyue; when Chen Tingjing drafted hymns, because the Empress Dowager and Empress dared not equal the Grand Empress Dowager, they were named Dangdi instead.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Ceremonies records that mounting and return always used Zhonghe Shaoyue; Chen Tingjing named them Dangdi because the Empress Dowager and Empress dared not equal the Grand Empress Dowager.

sentences.zh: 請仍復舊，各為樂章。」

translations.literal: We ask to restore the old practice, each with its own hymns."
translations.idiomatic: We ask to restore the old practice, each with separate hymns."

sentences.zh: 尋定皇太后御慈寧宮升座中和韶樂奏豫平；

translations.literal: Soon it was fixed: when the Empress Dowager presided at Cining Palace, mounting the throne used Zhonghe Shaoyue performing Yuping;
translations.idiomatic: They fixed: when the Empress Dowager presided at Cíníng Palace, mounting the throne used Zhonghe Shaoyue performing Yùpíng;

sentences.zh: 皇帝率諸王群臣行禮丹陛大樂奏益平，還宮中和韶樂奏履平，皇后率皇貴妃、貴妃、妃、嬪及公主、福晉、命婦至宮行禮並同。

translations.literal: when the emperor led princes and ministers in the rite, Dangdi great music performed Yiping; on return to palace, Zhonghe Shaoyue performed Lüping—the same when the Empress led imperial consorts, princesses, fujin, and titled ladies to the palace for the rite.
translations.idiomatic: when the emperor led princes and ministers, Dangdi great music performed Yìpíng; on return, Zhonghe Shaoyue performed Lǚpíng—the same when the Empress led consorts, princesses, fujin, and titled ladies.

sentences.zh: 皇帝三大節臨軒、還宮、御內殿升座中和韶樂奏元平，皇后率皇貴妃、貴妃、妃、嬪行禮丹陛大樂奏雍平，降座中和韶樂奏和平，皇后三大節升座中和韶樂奏淑平，行禮丹陛大樂奏正平，降座中和韶樂奏順平。

translations.literal: For the emperor's three great festivals at the audience hall, return to palace, and mounting the throne in the inner hall, Zhonghe Shaoyue performed Yuanping; when the Empress led imperial consorts in the rite, Dangdi great music performed Yongping; on descending the throne, Zhonghe Shaoyue performed Heping. For the Empress's three great festivals, mounting used Shuping, the rite Zhengping, descending Shunping.
translations.idiomatic: For the emperor's three festivals at court, return, and inner-hall mounting, Zhonghe Shaoyue played Yuánpíng; the Empress's rite used Dangdi great music with Yōngpíng; descent used Hépíng. For the Empress's three festivals: mounting Shúpíng, rite Zhèngpíng, descent Shùnpíng.

sentences.zh: 皇帝筵宴、進茶、賜茶丹陛清樂奏海宇昇平日，進酒、賜酒奏玉殿雲開，進饌、賜食中和清樂奏萬象清寧。

translations.literal: At the emperor's banquet, presentation and bestowal of tea: Dangdi qing music performed "Haiyu Shengping Ri"; wine: "Yudian Yunkai"; food: Zhonghe qing music performed "Wanxiang Qingning."
translations.idiomatic: At imperial banquets: tea used Dangdi qing music ("Hǎiyǔ Shēngpíng Rì"); wine ("Yùdiàn Yúnkāi"); food Zhonghe qing music ("Wànxiàng Qīngníng").

sentences.zh: 皇太后三大節升座、還宮行禮與慶賀同，筵宴進茶、進酒、進饌所奏歌詞與皇帝同。

translations.literal: For the Empress Dowager's three great festivals, mounting, return, and rites matched congratulations; banquet tea, wine, and food used the same lyrics as the emperor.
translations.idiomatic: For the Empress Dowager's three festivals, mounting, return, and rites matched congratulations; banquet tea, wine, and food used the emperor's lyrics.

sentences.zh: 時山東道監察御史徐以升奏言：「古有雩祭之典，所以為百穀祈膏雨也。

translations.literal: At that time Shandong Circuit Investigating Censor Xu Yisheng memorialized: "Antiquity had the yu sacrifice rite to pray rich rain for the hundred grains.
translations.idiomatic: Shandong Circuit censor Xu Yisheng memorialized: "Antiquity had the yú sacrifice to pray rich rain for the hundred grains.

sentences.zh: 其制，則為壇於南郊之旁。

translations.literal: Its form was to set an altar beside the Southern Suburb.
translations.idiomatic: Its form was an altar beside the Southern Suburb.

sentences.zh: 我朝禮制具備，惟雩祭未有壇壝，乞敕下禮臣博求典故，詳考制度，仿古龍見而雩之禮，擇地立壇。」

translations.literal: Our dynasty's ritual system is complete, yet the yu sacrifice has no altar mound; I beg that ritual officials be ordered to search antiquity broadly, examine the system in detail, imitate the ancient rite of yu when the dragon appears, and choose a site to establish an altar."
translations.idiomatic: Our ritual system is complete, yet the yú sacrifice has no altar; I beg ritual officials to search antiquity, examine the system, imitate the ancient yú when the dragon appears, and choose a site for an altar."

sentences.zh: 帝下其章，大學士鄂爾泰等議曰：「孟夏之月，蒼龍宿見東方，為百穀祈膏雨，故龍見而雩。

translations.literal: The emperor sent down the memorial; Grand Secretaries Ortai and others deliberated: "In the fourth month of summer the Azure Dragon constellation appears in the east to pray rich rain for the hundred grains; hence yu when the dragon appears.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor sent down the memorial; Grand Secretaries Ortai and others argued: "In early summer the Azure Dragon appears in the east to pray rich rain for the hundred grains—hence the yú when the dragon appears.

sentences.zh: 晉永和中，依郊壇制為雩壇，祈上帝百辟，旱則祈雨。

translations.literal: In the Jin Yonghe period, following suburban altar form they made a yu altar, praying to the Supreme Lord and the hundred lords; in drought they prayed for rain.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jin Yonghe reign they built a yú altar on the suburban model, praying to the Supreme Lord and the hundred powers; in drought they prayed for rain.

sentences.zh: 唐時雩祀於南郊，後行雩禮於圜丘。

translations.literal: In Tang times yu sacrifice was at the Southern Suburb; later they performed yu rites at the Round Mound.
translations.idiomatic: Tang held yú at the Southern Suburb; later they performed yú at the Round Mound.

sentences.zh: 歷代京師孟夏後旱雩之禮，皆七日一祈，唐制斟酌最善，臣等酌議宜仿其制。

translations.literal: Through the ages the capital's post-midsummer drought-yu rite was one prayer every seven days; Tang's weighing was best—your servants deliberate and propose imitating that system.
translations.idiomatic: Across dynasties the capital's midsummer drought yú was prayed every seven days; Tang's arrangement was best—we propose following it.

sentences.zh: 古大雩用舞童二佾，衣玄衣，各執羽翳，歌雲漢之詩。

translations.literal: Ancient great yu used two rows of dancing boys in dark robes, each holding feather fans, singing the "Cloudy Han" ode.
translations.idiomatic: The ancient great yú used two rows of boy dancers in dark robes, each with feather fans, singing the Yún Hàn ode.

sentences.zh: 今皇上仿雲漢體御制詩歌八章，聖念懇誠，宸章剴切，應用舞童十六人，玄衣，八列，執羽翳，終獻樂止，贊者讚：『舞童歌詩。』

translations.literal: Now His Majesty, imitating the Yun Han style, composed eight imperial stanzas—sacred thought earnest, imperial phrases incisive—there should be sixteen dancing boys in dark robes, eight ranks, holding feather fans; at the final offering music stops, the usher praises: 'Dancing boys sing the odes.'
translations.idiomatic: His Majesty composed eight stanzas in the Yún Hàn manner—earnest in purpose, incisive in diction—so sixteen boy dancers in dark robes, eight ranks deep with feather fans; at the final offering the music stops and the usher calls: 'Let the dancers sing the odes.'

sentences.zh: 歌畢，乃望燎。

translations.literal: When the song ends, then gaze toward the burning.
translations.idiomatic: When the singing ends, they gaze toward the pyre.

sentences.zh: 令掌儀司選聲音清亮者充之，羽翳依周禮皇舞之式，禮儀與孟夏常雩同。

translations.literal: Order the Directorate of Ceremonies to select those with clear, bright voices; feather fans follow the Zhou li imperial dance form—rites the same as the regular midsummer yu.
translations.idiomatic: The Directorate of Ceremonies was to choose singers with clear voices; feather fans followed the Zhou ritual imperial dance; the ceremony matched the regular midsummer yú.

sentences.zh: 上帝、社稷、宗廟、太歲壇俱舊有樂章，惟神祇壇闕，應敕律呂館撰進。」

translations.literal: The Supreme Lord, soil and grain, ancestral temple, and Grand Year altars all had old hymns; only the Spirits Altar lacked them—order the Pitch-Pipe Office to compose and submit."
translations.idiomatic: The Supreme Lord, soil and grain, ancestral temple, and Grand Year altars already had hymns; only the Spirits Altar lacked them—the Pitch-Pipe Office was ordered to compose and submit."

sentences.zh: 乃定雩祀天神從圜丘，以黃鍾為宮；

translations.literal: Thus they fixed yu sacrifice to heavenly spirits following the Round Mound, with Huangzhong as palace;
translations.idiomatic: They fixed yú rites to heaven following the Round Mound, with Huángzhōng as palace pitch;

sentences.zh: 地祇從方澤，以林鍾為宮。

translations.literal: earth spirits followed the Square Mound, with Linzhong as palace.
translations.idiomatic: earth spirits followed the Square Mound, with Línzhōng as palace.

sentences.zh: 樂用七成，迎神奏祈豐，奠帛奏華豐，初獻奏安豐，亞獻奏興豐，終獻奏儀豐，徹饌奏和豐，送神奏錫豐。

translations.literal: Music used seven pieces: welcoming spirits Qi Feng; presenting silk Hua Feng; first offering An Feng; second offering Xing Feng; final offering Yi Feng; clearing feast He Feng; sending spirits Xi Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Music comprised seven movements: welcoming spirits Qí Fēng; offering silk Huá Fēng; first offering Ān Fēng; second Xīng Fēng; final Yí Fēng; clearing feast Hé Fēng; dismissal Xī Fēng.

sentences.zh: 是年始專設樂部，凡太常寺、神樂觀所司祭祀之樂，和聲署、掌儀司所司朝會宴饗之樂，鑾儀衛所司鹵簿諸樂，均隸焉。

translations.literal: That year they first established a dedicated Music Office: all sacrificial music of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Divine Music Bureau, court-assembly and banquet music of the Harmonious Sound Office and Directorate of Ceremonies, and guard-of-honor music of the Imperial Procession Guard were all placed under it.
translations.idiomatic: That year a dedicated Music Office was created, absorbing sacrificial music from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and Divine Music Bureau, court and banquet music from the Harmonious Sound Office and Directorate of Ceremonies, and procession music from the Imperial Procession Guard.

sentences.zh: 以禮部內務府大臣及各部院大臣諳曉音律者總理之，設署正、署丞、侍從、待詔、供奉、供用官、鼓手、樂工，總曰署吏，而以所司樂器別其目。

translations.literal: Ministers of the Board of Rites, Imperial Household, and other boards and courts who understood pitch were to oversee it; they set bureau chiefs, vice chiefs, attendants, awaiting-edict officers, court musicians, supply officers, drummers, and music workers—collectively called office clerks—distinguished by the instruments they served.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers of the Board of Rites, Imperial Household, and other boards versed in pitch oversaw it; they appointed bureau chiefs, deputies, attendants, awaiting-edict officers, court musicians, supply officers, drummers, and players—office clerks all—sorted by instrument.

sentences.zh: 鐘曰司鐘，磬曰司磬，琴、瑟、笙、簫亦如之。

translations.literal: Bells were called bell masters, stone chimes chime masters; zithers, se, sheng, and xiao likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Bell players were bell masters, stone-chime players chime masters; zither, se, sheng, and xiao players likewise.

sentences.zh: 又禁道士充太常寺樂員。

translations.literal: Daoist priests were also forbidden to serve as Court of Imperial Sacrifices musicians.
translations.idiomatic: Daoist priests were also barred from serving as Court of Imperial Sacrifices musicians.

sentences.zh: 初，明樂舞生多選道童，世祖定都，沿而用之，羽流慢褻，識者慨焉，至是其弊始革。

translations.literal: Earlier, Ming music-and-dance students were mostly chosen from Daoist youths; when the Founding Emperor fixed the capital this continued, and the feathered clergy grew irreverent—men of insight lamented it; only now was that abuse reformed.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier Ming dance students were mostly Daoist youths; when the Founding Emperor fixed the capital the practice continued, and the feathered clergy grew irreverent—thoughtful men lamented it—until now that abuse was finally reformed.

sentences.zh: 既又從館臣言，定耕耤之樂。

translations.literal: Thereafter, following the Hanlin compilers' advice, they fixed music for the ploughing-and-sacred-field ceremony.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, on the Hanlin compilers' advice, they fixed music for the ploughing-and-sacred-field ceremony.

sentences.zh: 耕耤前期進種，導迎樂前導，至日，和聲署率屬鵠立采棚南，采棚之制，後二十三年裁。

translations.literal: Before the ploughing ceremony seed was advanced; conducting-welcome music led ahead; on the day the Harmonious Sound Office led its subordinates standing like geese south of the silk-picking shelter—the shelter form was abolished twenty-three years later.
translations.idiomatic: Before the ceremony seed was brought forward with conducting-welcome music leading; on the day the Harmonious Sound Office led its men standing in ranks south of the silk-picking shelter—the shelter itself was abolished twenty-three years later.

sentences.zh: 歌禾辭者十四人，司鑼、司鼓、司版、司笛、笙、簫者各六人，搴采旗者五十人。

translations.literal: Fourteen sang the grain ode; six each for gong, drum, clapper, flute, sheng, and xiao; fifty plucked silk flags.
translations.idiomatic: Fourteen sang the grain hymn; six each played gong, drum, clapper, flute, sheng, and xiao; fifty carried silk flags.

sentences.zh: 祭畢，行耕耤禮。

translations.literal: When the sacrifice ended, they performed the ploughing-and-sacred-field rite.
translations.idiomatic: After the sacrifice they performed the ploughing-and-sacred-field rite.

sentences.zh: 禮成，導迎樂作，駕蒞齋宮內門，樂止，中和韶樂作。

translations.literal: When the rite was complete, conducting-welcome music sounded; the imperial carriage reached the fasting palace inner gate—music stopped—Harmonious Central Shao music began.
translations.idiomatic: When the rite ended, conducting-welcome music sounded; the carriage reached the fasting palace inner gate—music stopped—then Harmonious Central Shao music.

sentences.zh: 皇帝御後殿，樂止，報終畝，中和韶樂作。

translations.literal: The emperor entered the rear hall—music stopped; when the final furrow was reported, Harmonious Central Shao music began.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered the rear hall—music stopped; when the final furrow was reported, Harmonious Central Shao music resumed.

sentences.zh: 皇帝御齋宮，升座，樂止，群臣慶賀行禮，丹陛大樂作。

translations.literal: The emperor entered the fasting palace and ascended the seat—music stopped; the hundred officials congratulated and performed rites—Cinnabar Steps Great Music began.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor entered the fasting palace and took his seat—music stopped; officials congratulated and bowed—Cinnabar Steps Great Music began.

sentences.zh: 進茶、賜茶中和韶樂作。

translations.literal: Presenting tea and bestowing tea: Harmonious Central Shao music.
translations.idiomatic: Tea service and imperial tea: Harmonious Central Shao music.

sentences.zh: 皇帝乘輦出宮，和聲署鹵簿大樂並作。

translations.literal: The emperor rode the palanquin out of the palace; the Harmonious Sound Office guard-of-honor great music sounded together.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor rode out; the Harmonious Sound Office guard-of-honor great music played together.

sentences.zh: 筵宴、進茶、賜茶改雨暘時若為喜春光。

translations.literal: For banquets and presenting or bestowing tea they changed Yu Yang Shi Ruo to Xi Chun Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Banquet and tea hymns changed from Yǔ Yáng Shí Ruò to Xǐ Chūn Guāng.

sentences.zh: 進酒、賜酒改五穀豐登為雲和迭奏。

translations.literal: Presenting and bestowing wine they changed Wu Gu Feng Deng to Yun He Die Zou.
translations.idiomatic: Wine service changed from Wǔ Gǔ Fēng Dēng to Yún Hé Dié Zòu.

sentences.zh: 進饌、賜饌改家給人足為風和日麗，升座、還宮樂章與三月常朝同。

translations.literal: Presenting and bestowing food they changed Jia Ji Ren Zu to Feng He Ri Li; ascending the seat and returning to the palace used the same hymns as the third-month regular audience.
translations.idiomatic: Food service changed from Jiā Jǐ Rén Zú to Fēng Hé Rì Lì; seat and return hymns matched the third-month regular audience.

sentences.zh: 群臣行禮丹陛樂章與元旦同。

translations.literal: When the hundred officials performed rites, Cinnabar Steps hymns were the same as New Year's Day.
translations.idiomatic: Officials' obeisance used the same Cinnabar Steps hymns as New Year's Day.

sentences.zh: 又定祀先蠶樂章器用方響十有六，雲鑼、瑟、杖鼓、拍版各二，琴四，簫、笛、笙各六，建鼓一。

translations.literal: They also fixed hymns and instruments for sacrifice to the First Silkworm: sixteen square sonorous stones; two each of cloud gongs, se, staff drums, and clappers; four zithers; six each of xiao, flute, and sheng; one established drum.
translations.idiomatic: They also fixed First Silkworm sacrifice music: sixteen square sonorous stones; two each of cloud gongs, se, staff drums, and clappers; four zithers; six each of xiao, flute, and sheng; one established drum.

sentences.zh: 皇后採桑歌器用金鼓、拍版二，簫、笛、笙六。

translations.literal: For the empress picking mulberry and singing, instruments were two gold drums and clappers, six each of xiao, flute, and sheng.
translations.idiomatic: For the empress's mulberry picking and song: two gold drums and clappers, six each of xiao, flute, and sheng.

sentences.zh: 遣官致祭樂章與群祀同。

translations.literal: When officials were dispatched to sacrifice, hymns were the same as group sacrifices.
translations.idiomatic: Dispatched-official sacrifices used the same hymns as group rites.

sentences.zh: 又定賜衍聖公宴樂章奏洙泗發源長。

translations.literal: They also fixed the banquet hymn for bestowing on the Duke Continuator of the Sage: Zhu Si Fa Yuan Chang was performed.
translations.idiomatic: They fixed the banquet for the Duke Continuator of the Sage to perform Zhū Sī Fā Yuán Cháng.

sentences.zh: 正一真人宴奏上清碧落。

translations.literal: The Zhengyi Perfect Man's banquet performed Shang Qing Bi Luo.
translations.idiomatic: The Zhengyi Perfect Man's banquet performed Shàng Qīng Bì Luò.

sentences.zh: 文進士宴奏啟天門。

translations.literal: The civil jinshi banquet performed Qi Tian Men.
translations.idiomatic: The civil jinshi banquet performed Qǐ Tiān Mén.

sentences.zh: 武進士奏和氣洽。

translations.literal: The military jinshi performed He Qi Qia.
translations.idiomatic: The military jinshi performed Hé Qì Qià.

sentences.zh: 鄉飲酒禮歌鹿鳴、四牡、皇皇者華三章，笙御制補南陔、白華、華黍三章，閒歌魚麗、南有嘉魚、南山有台三章，笙御制補由庚、崇丘、由儀三章，合樂周南關雎、葛覃、卷耳三章，召南鵲巢、采蘩、采蘋三章。

translations.literal: The district drinking ceremony sang Lu Ming, Si Mu, and Huang Huang Zhe Hua—three pieces; the sheng supplemented with imperial Nan Gai, Bai Hua, and Hua Shu—three; interlude songs Yu Li, Nan You Jia Yu, and Nan Shan You Tai—three; sheng imperial supplements You Geng, Chong Qiu, and You Yi—three; combined with Zhou Nan Guan Ju, Ge Tan, Juan Er—three, and Zhao Nan Que Chao, Cai Fan, Cai Pin—three.
translations.idiomatic: The district drinking rite sang Lù Míng, Sì Mǔ, and Huáng Huáng Zhě Huá; the sheng added imperial Nán Gāi, Bái Huá, and Huá Shǔ; interlude songs Yú Lì, Nán Yǒu Jiā Yú, and Nán Shān Yǒu Tái; sheng imperial supplements Yóu Gēng, Chóng Qiū, and Yóu Yí; combined with Zhōu Nán's Guān Jū, Gé Tán, and Juǎn Ěr and Zhāo Nán's Què Cháo, Cǎi Fán, and Cǎi Píng.

sentences.zh: 八年九月，高宗東巡狩至盛京，儀仗具，馬上鼓吹導引，翼日設丹陛大樂於兩樂亭，禮部設龍亭，置慶賀表，用導迎樂。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, ninth month, the High Ancestor on eastern tour reached Shengjing; guard of honor complete, mounted drum-and-pipe led the way; next day Cinnabar Steps great music was set at the two music pavilions; the Board of Rites set the dragon pavilion with congratulatory memorial, using conducting-welcome music.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year, ninth month, the emperor on eastern tour reached Shengjing with full guard; mounted drum-and-pipe led; the next day Cinnabar Steps great music was placed at the two music pavilions; the Board of Rites set the dragon pavilion with a congratulatory memorial and conducting-welcome music.

sentences.zh: 上御崇政殿，升座中和韶樂奏元平，諸王大臣行禮、宣表丹陛大樂奏慶平，朝鮮陪臣朝賀丹陛大樂奏治平，頒詔、賜茶中和韶樂奏和平。

translations.literal: His Majesty entered Chongzheng Hall and ascended—Harmonious Central Shao played Yuan Ping; princes and ministers performed rites and proclaimed the memorial—Cinnabar Steps great music played Qing Ping; Korean tributary envoys congratulated—Cinnabar Steps played Zhi Ping; issuing the edict and bestowing tea—Harmonious Central played He Ping.
translations.idiomatic: He entered Chongzheng Hall and ascended—Harmonious Central Shao played Yuán Píng; princes and ministers bowed and the memorial was read—Cinnabar Steps played Qìng Píng; Korean envoys congratulated—Zhi Píng; edict and tea—Hé Píng.

sentences.zh: 是日崇政殿筵宴所奏中和丹陛清樂與太和殿筵宴同。

translations.literal: That day the Chongzheng Hall banquet's Harmonious Central, Cinnabar Steps, and clear music were the same as the Hall of Supreme Harmony banquet.
translations.idiomatic: That day's Chongzheng banquet used the same Harmonious Central, Cinnabar Steps, and clear music as the Hall of Supreme Harmony.

sentences.zh: 改瑪克式舞為慶隆之舞，又增世德之舞。

translations.literal: They changed the Makshi-style dance to the Dance of Celebrated Grandeur and added the Dance of Worldly Virtue.
translations.idiomatic: They renamed the Makshi-style dance the Dance of Celebrated Grandeur and added the Dance of Worldly Virtue.

sentences.zh: 旋定樂舞內大小馬護為揚烈舞，舞人所騎竹馬為禺馬，馬護為面具。

translations.literal: Soon after they fixed within the music dances: great and small horse-guards became the Dance of Spreading Valor; bamboo horses the dancers rode were called "fool horses," horse-guards their masks.
translations.idiomatic: They then fixed the dance roster: great and small horse-guards became the Spreading Valor dance; bamboo horses the dancers rode were "fool horses," horse-guards their masks.

sentences.zh: 大臣起舞上壽為喜起舞。

translations.literal: When great ministers danced offering longevity it was called the Dance of Joyful Rising.
translations.idiomatic: Ministers dancing the longevity offering became the Joyful Rising dance.

sentences.zh: 歌章者曰司章，騎竹馬曰司舞，搊琵琶曰司琵琶，彈弦子曰司三弦，彈箏曰司箏，劃節曰司節，拍版曰司拍，拍掌曰司抃。

translations.literal: Singers of stanzas were called stanza masters; riders of bamboo horses dance masters; plucking pipa—pipa masters; plucking sanxian—sanxian masters; plucking zheng—zheng masters; marking beat—beat masters; clappers—clapper masters; hand-clapping—hand-clap masters.
translations.idiomatic: Stanza singers were stanza masters; bamboo-horse riders dance masters; pipa players pipa masters; sanxian players sanxian masters; zheng players zheng masters; beat markers beat masters; clapper players clapper masters; hand-clappers hand-clap masters.

sentences.zh: 九年，親幸翰林院，詔樂部設樂，升座奏隆平，掌院大學士率百官行禮奏慶平，進茶、賜茶奏文物京華盛，進御筵宴奏玉署延英、進酒、賜酒奏延閣雲濃，百官謝恩奏慶平，還官奏顯平。

translations.literal: In the ninth year he personally visited the Hanlin Academy; ordered the Music Office to set music—ascending the seat played Long Ping; the Hanlin chancellor leading the hundred officials performed rites to Qing Ping; presenting and bestowing tea played Wen Wu Jing Hua Sheng; entering the imperial banquet played Yu Shu Yan Ying, presenting and bestowing wine Yan Ge Yun Nong; the hundred officials thanked grace to Qing Ping; returning to court Xian Ping.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year he visited the Hanlin Academy; the Music Office set music—ascending played Lóng Píng; the chancellor leading officials bowed to Qìng Píng; tea played Wén Wù Jīng Huá Shèng; the imperial banquet Yù Shǔ Yán Yīng, wine Yán Gé Yún Nóng; officials' thanks Qìng Píng; return Xiǎn Píng.

sentences.zh: 是年裁太常寺司樂人六，增設天神地祇壇樂器，諭禮臣，除夕保和殿筵宴蒙古王等，先進蒙古樂曲，次慶隆舞，元旦太和殿筵宴王大臣，互易用之，著為令。

translations.literal: That year six Court of Imperial Sacrifices music officers were cut; instruments were added for the Heavenly and Earth Spirits altars; ritual officials were instructed: on New Year's Eve the Hall of Preserving Harmony banquet for Mongol princes should first present Mongol tunes, then the Celebrated Grandeur dance; on New Year's Day the Hall of Supreme Harmony banquet for princes and ministers should interchange them—fixed as statute.
translations.idiomatic: That year six Court of Imperial Sacrifices musicians were cut and instruments added for the Heavenly and Earth Spirits altars; ritual officials were told: on New Year's Eve the Hall of Preserving Harmony banquet for Mongol princes should lead with Mongol tunes, then Celebrated Grandeur; on New Year's Day at the Hall of Supreme Harmony the order was reversed—statute.

sentences.zh: 帝自御宇，樂制屢易，因革損益，悉出睿裁，群臣希旨，務為補苴，非有張乾龜、萬寶常之識也。

translations.literal: From the emperor's accession music systems changed often; reform, retention, reduction, and increase all issued from sagely decision; ministers curried favor and patched piecemeal—they did not have the discernment of Zhang Qian-gui or Wan Baochang.
translations.idiomatic: From his accession music changed repeatedly; every reform issued from the throne; ministers curried favor and patched piecemeal—none had the discernment of Zhang Qian-gui or Wan Baochang.

sentences.zh: 帝思隆巍煥，遂特詔釐定朝會宴饗諸樂章，自七年定郊廟祭祀諸樂章，至十一年始成。

translations.literal: The emperor, thinking to elevate splendor, specially ordered the fixing of court-assembly and banquet hymns—from the seventh year's fixing of suburban and temple hymns until the eleventh year it was complete.
translations.idiomatic: Wishing to elevate splendor, he ordered court and banquet hymns fixed—from suburban and temple hymns in the seventh year until completion in the eleventh.

sentences.zh: 朝會，皇帝元旦中和樂，升座元平，還宮和平。

translations.literal: Court assemblies: on the emperor's New Year, Harmonious Central music—ascending Yuan Ping, returning He Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Court assembly: New Year's Harmonious Central—ascending Yuán Píng, return Hé Píng.

sentences.zh: 冬至中和樂，升座遂平，還宮允平。

translations.literal: Winter solstice Harmonious Central—ascending Sui Ping, returning Yun Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Winter solstice—ascending Suí Píng, return Yǔn Píng.

sentences.zh: 萬壽中和樂，升座乾平，還宮泰平。

translations.literal: Longevity Harmonious Central—ascending Qian Ping, returning Tai Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Longevity—ascending Qián Píng, return Tài Píng.

sentences.zh: 上元中和樂，升座怡平，還宮昇平，常朝中和樂，升座隆平，還宮顯平。

translations.literal: Lantern Festival Harmonious Central—ascending Yi Ping, returning Sheng Ping; regular audience Harmonious Central—ascending Long Ping, returning Xian Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Lantern Festival—Yí Píng ascending, Shēng Píng return; regular audience—Lóng Píng ascending, Xiǎn Píng return.

sentences.zh: 內廷行禮丹陛樂雝平，諸王百官行禮丹陛樂慶平，外籓丹陛樂治平。

translations.literal: Inner court rites: Cinnabar Steps Yong Ping; princes and officials Cinnabar Steps Qing Ping; outer domains Zhi Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Inner court rites: Cinnabar Steps Yōng Píng; princes and officials Qìng Píng; tributaries Zhì Píng.

sentences.zh: 皇太后三大節中和樂，升座豫平，還宮履平，丹陛樂益平。

translations.literal: Empress Dowager's three great festivals: Harmonious Central—ascending Yu Ping, returning Lü Ping; Cinnabar Steps Yi Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Empress Dowager's three festivals: Harmonious Central—Yù Píng ascending, Lǚ Píng return; Cinnabar Steps Yì Píng.

sentences.zh: 皇后三大節中和樂，升座淑平，還宮順平，丹陛樂正平。

translations.literal: Empress's three great festivals: Harmonious Central—ascending Shu Ping, returning Shun Ping; Cinnabar Steps Zheng Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Empress's three festivals: Harmonious Central—Shū Píng ascending, Shùn Píng return; Cinnabar Steps Zhèng Píng.

sentences.zh: 郊廟圜丘迎神始平，奠玉帛景平，進俎咸平，初獻壽平，亞獻嘉平，終獻永平，徹饌熙平，送神清平，望燎太平。

translations.literal: Suburban Round Mound: welcoming spirits Shi Ping; presenting jade and silk Jing Ping; presenting offerings Xian Ping; first offering Shou Ping; second Jia Ping; final Yong Ping; clearing feast Xi Ping; sending spirits Qing Ping; gazing at burning Tai Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Round Mound: welcoming Shǐ Píng; jade and silk Jǐng Píng; offerings Xián Píng; first Shòu Píng; second Jiā Píng; final Yǒng Píng; clearing Xī Píng; dismissal Qīng Píng; pyre Tài Píng.

sentences.zh: 方澤迎神中平，奠玉帛廣平，進俎含平，初獻大平，亞獻安平，終獻時平，徹饌貞平，送神、望瘞寧平。

translations.literal: Square Mound: welcoming Zhong Ping; jade and silk Guang Ping; offerings Han Ping; first Da Ping; second An Ping; final Shi Ping; clearing Zhen Ping; sending spirits and burial mound Ning Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Square Mound: welcoming Zhōng Píng; jade and silk Guǎng Píng; offerings Hán Píng; first Dà Píng; second Ān Píng; final Shí Píng; clearing Zhēn Píng; dismissal and burial Níng Píng.

sentences.zh: 祈穀迎神祈平，奠玉帛綏平，進俎萬平，初獻寶平，亞獻穰平，終獻瑞平，徹饌渥平，送神滋平，望燎穀平。

translations.literal: Prayer for grain: welcoming Qi Ping; jade and silk Sui Ping; offerings Wan Ping; first Bao Ping; second Rang Ping; final Rui Ping; clearing Wo Ping; sending Zi Ping; pyre Gu Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Prayer for grain: welcoming Qí Píng; jade and silk Suí Píng; offerings Wàn Píng; first Bǎo Píng; second Rǎng Píng; final Ruì Píng; clearing Wò Píng; dismissal Zī Píng; pyre Gǔ Píng.

sentences.zh: 雩祭迎神靄平，奠玉帛雲平，進俎需平，初獻霖平，亞獻露平，終獻霑平，徹饌靈平，送神霮平，望燎霈平。

translations.literal: Yu sacrifice: welcoming Ai Ping; jade and silk Yun Ping; offerings Xu Ping; first Lin Ping; second Lu Ping; final Zhan Ping; clearing Ling Ping; sending Dian Ping; pyre Pei Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Yú sacrifice: welcoming Ǎi Píng; jade and silk Yún Píng; offerings Xū Píng; first Lín Píng; second Lù Píng; final Zhān Píng; clearing Líng Píng; dismissal Diàn Píng; pyre Pèi Píng.

sentences.zh: 太廟時饗，迎神貽平，奠帛、初獻敉平，亞獻敷平，終獻紹平，徹饌光平，送神、還宮、望燎乂平。

translations.literal: Ancestral temple seasonal offering: welcoming Yi Ping; presenting silk and first offering Shu Ping; second Fu Ping; final Shao Ping; clearing Guang Ping; sending spirits, return to palace, and pyre Yi Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Ancestral temple seasonal rite: welcoming Yí Píng; silk and first offering Shū Píng; second Fū Píng; final Shào Píng; clearing Guāng Píng; dismissal, return, and pyre Yì Píng.

sentences.zh: 祫祭迎神開平，奠帛、初獻肅平，亞獻協平，終獻裕平，徹饌諴平，送神、還宮、望燎成平。

translations.literal: Collective offering: welcoming Kai Ping; silk and first Su Ping; second Xie Ping; final Yu Ping; clearing Xian Ping; sending spirits, return, and pyre Cheng Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Collective rite: welcoming Kāi Píng; silk and first Sù Píng; second Xié Píng; final Yù Píng; clearing Xián Píng; dismissal, return, and pyre Chéng Píng.

sentences.zh: 社稷迎神登平，奠帛、初獻茂平，亞獻育平，終獻敦平，徹饌博平，送神樂平，望瘞徵平。

translations.literal: Soil and grain: welcoming Deng Ping; silk and first Mao Ping; second Yu Ping; final Dun Ping; clearing Bo Ping; sending Yue Ping; burial mound Zheng Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Soil and grain: welcoming Dēng Píng; silk and first Mào Píng; second Yù Píng; final Dūn Píng; clearing Bó Píng; dismissal Yuè Píng; burial Zhēng Píng.

sentences.zh: 社稷壇祈雨報祀迎神延豐，奠帛、初獻介豐，亞獻滋豐，終獻霈豐，徹饌綏豐，送神貽豐，望瘞博豐。

translations.literal: Soil-and-grain altar prayer for rain and thanksgiving: welcoming Yan Feng; silk and first Jie Feng; second Zi Feng; final Pei Feng; clearing Sui Feng; sending Yi Feng; burial Bo Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Soil-and-grain rain prayer and thanksgiving: welcoming Yán Fēng; silk and first Jiè Fēng; second Zī Fēng; final Pèi Fēng; clearing Suí Fēng; dismissal Yí Fēng; burial Bó Fēng.

sentences.zh: 朝日迎神寅曦，奠玉帛朝曦，初獻清曦，亞獻咸曦，終獻純曦，徹饌延曦，送神歸曦。

translations.literal: Morning sun: welcoming Yin Xi; jade and silk Zhao Xi; first Qing Xi; second Xian Xi; final Chun Xi; clearing Yan Xi; sending Gui Xi.
translations.idiomatic: Morning sun: welcoming Yín Xī; jade and silk Zhāo Xī; first Qīng Xī; second Xián Xī; final Chún Xī; clearing Yán Xī; dismissal Guī Xī.

sentences.zh: 夕月迎神迎光，奠帛、初獻升光，亞獻瑤光，終獻瑞光，徹饌涵光，送神保光。

translations.literal: Evening moon: welcoming Ying Guang; silk and first Sheng Guang; second Yao Guang; final Rui Guang; clearing Han Guang; sending Bao Guang.
translations.idiomatic: Evening moon: welcoming Yíng Guāng; silk and first Shēng Guāng; second Yáo Guāng; final Ruì Guāng; clearing Hán Guāng; dismissal Bǎo Guāng.

sentences.zh: 歷代帝王迎神肇平，奠帛、初獻興平，亞獻崇平，終獻恬平，徹饌淳平，送神、望燎匡平。

translations.literal: Dynastic emperors: welcoming Zhao Ping; silk and first Xing Ping; second Chong Ping; final Tian Ping; clearing Chun Ping; sending spirits and pyre Kuang Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Dynastic emperors: welcoming Zhào Píng; silk and first Xīng Píng; second Chóng Píng; final Tián Píng; clearing Chún Píng; dismissal and pyre Kuāng Píng.

sentences.zh: 先師迎神昭平，奠帛、初獻宣平，亞獻秩平，終獻敘平，徹饌懿平，送神德平。

translations.literal: First Teacher: welcoming Zhao Ping; silk and first Xuan Ping; second Zhi Ping; final Xu Ping; clearing Yi Ping; sending De Ping.
translations.idiomatic: First Teacher: welcoming Zhāo Píng; silk and first Xuān Píng; second Zhì Píng; final Xù Píng; clearing Yì Píng; dismissal Dé Píng.

sentences.zh: 先農迎神永豐，奠帛、初獻時豐，亞獻咸豐，終獻大豐，徹饌屢豐，送神報豐，望瘞慶豐。

translations.literal: First Farmer: welcoming Yong Feng; silk and first Shi Feng; second Xian Feng; final Da Feng; clearing Lü Feng; sending Bao Feng; burial Qing Feng.
translations.idiomatic: First Farmer: welcoming Yǒng Fēng; silk and first Shí Fēng; second Xián Fēng; final Dà Fēng; clearing Lǚ Fēng; dismissal Bào Fēng; burial Qìng Fēng.

sentences.zh: 先蠶迎神庥平，奠帛、初獻承平，亞獻均平，終獻齊平，徹饌柔平，送神洽平，天神地祇迎神祈豐，奠帛、初獻華豐，亞獻興豐，終獻儀豐，徹饌和豐，送神錫豐。

translations.literal: First Silkworm: welcoming Xiu Ping; silk and first Cheng Ping; second Jun Ping; final Qi Ping; clearing Rou Ping; sending Qia Ping; Heavenly and Earth Spirits—welcoming Qi Feng; silk and first Hua Feng; second Xing Feng; final Yi Feng; clearing He Feng; sending Xi Feng.
translations.idiomatic: First Silkworm: welcoming Xiū Píng; silk and first Chéng Píng; second Jūn Píng; final Qí Píng; clearing Róu Píng; dismissal Qià Píng; Heavenly and Earth Spirits—Qí Fēng welcoming; Huá Fēng first; Xīng Fēng second; Yí Fēng final; Hé Fēng clearing; Xī Fēng dismissal.

sentences.zh: 太歲迎神保平，奠帛、初獻定平，亞獻嘏平，終獻富平，徹饌盈平，送神豐平。

translations.literal: Grand Year: welcoming Bao Ping; silk and first Ding Ping; second Gu Ping; final Fu Ping; clearing Ying Ping; sending Feng Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Year: welcoming Bǎo Píng; silk and first Dìng Píng; second Gù Píng; final Fù Píng; clearing Yíng Píng; dismissal Fēng Píng.

sentences.zh: 太歲壇祈雨、報祀迎神需豐，奠帛、初獻宜豐，亞獻晉豐，終獻協豐，徹饌應豐，送神洽豐。

translations.literal: Grand Year altar prayer for rain and thanksgiving: welcoming Xu Feng; silk and first Yi Feng; second Jin Feng; final Xie Feng; clearing Ying Feng; sending Qia Feng.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Year rain prayer and thanksgiving: welcoming Xū Fēng; silk and first Yí Fēng; second Jìn Fēng; final Xié Fēng; clearing Yìng Fēng; dismissal Qià Fēng.

sentences.zh: 皇帝祭壇廟還宮導迎樂祐平，慶典導迎樂禧平。

translations.literal: When the emperor sacrificed at altars and temples and returned to the palace: conducting-welcome music You Ping; great celebrations Xi Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Return from altar and temple sacrifice: conducting-welcome Yòu Píng; great celebrations Xǐ Píng.

sentences.zh: 其詞皆命儒臣重撰，天子親裁之，分刌而節比，合則仍其故，不合則易其辭、更其調，視舊章增損有加，而律呂正義後編亦於是年書成。

translations.literal: The texts were all ordered rewritten by Confucian officials and personally trimmed by the Son of Heaven—split and matched by measure; where they fit, the old remained; where not, words and tunes were changed; compared with old statutes there was increase and decrease, and the Correct Meaning of Pitch Pipes sequel was also completed that year.
translations.idiomatic: Texts were rewritten by scholar-officials and trimmed by the throne—split and matched by measure; what fit stayed, what did not brought new words and tunes; gains and losses over old statutes were considerable, and the Correct Meaning of Pitch Pipes sequel was completed the same year.

sentences.zh: 曰祭祀樂，曰朝會樂，曰宴饗樂，曰導迎樂，曰行幸樂。

translations.literal: There were sacrificial music, court-assembly music, banquet music, conducting-welcome music, and imperial progress music.
translations.idiomatic: Categories included sacrificial, court-assembly, banquet, conducting-welcome, and imperial progress music.

sentences.zh: 更參稽前代因革損益之異，為樂器考、樂制考、樂章考、度量權衡考。

translations.literal: Further collating earlier dynasties' differences in reform and retention, they made studies of instruments, musical systems, hymns, and measures, weights, and balances.
translations.idiomatic: Collating earlier reforms, they compiled studies of instruments, musical systems, hymns, and measures, weights, and balances.

sentences.zh: 復推闡聖祖所以審音定樂制器協均者，為樂問三十五篇。

translations.literal: They further developed what the founding emperor used to examine tone, fix music, make instruments, and harmonize pitch—thirty-five chapters of Musical Questions.
translations.idiomatic: They further expounded how the founding emperor examined tone, fixed music, fashioned instruments, and harmonized pitch—thirty-five Musical Questions.

sentences.zh: 大抵詳於宮譜，而於律呂之原，管音弦度之分合，一遵聖祖，無所創也。

translations.literal: Generally detailed on palace notation, yet on the origin of pitch pipes and the division and joining of tube tone and string measure they wholly followed the founding emperor without innovation.
translations.idiomatic: Detailed on palace notation, yet on pitch-pipe origins and the joining of tube tone to string measure they wholly followed the founding emperor without innovation.

sentences.zh: 帝自製序以冠之。

translations.literal: The emperor himself composed a preface to crown it.
translations.idiomatic: The emperor composed a preface to crown the work.

sentences.zh: 十三年二月，東巡山左，祭岱嶽，大學士等上言：「泰山向不用樂，考周禮大司樂『奏蕤賓、歌函鐘、舞大夏以祭山川』。

translations.literal: In the second month of the thirteenth year, on eastern tour of Shandong he sacrificed at Mount Tai; Grand Secretaries memorialized: "Mount Tai has not used music; examining Zhou li, the Grand Director of Music 'plays Ruibin, sings Hantong, dances Great Xia to sacrifice to mountains and rivers.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirteenth year, second month, touring east into Shandong he sacrificed at Mount Tai; Grand Secretaries memorialized: "Mount Tai has never used music; the Zhou Grand Director of Music 'plays Ruíbīn, sings Hántóng, dances Great Xia for mountains and rivers.'

sentences.zh: 今特舉盛典，秩於岱宗，請遵古用樂，樂章飭部撰擬。」

translations.literal: Now this special grand ceremony ranks with Dai Zong—please follow antiquity and use music; let the ministry compose hymns.'
translations.idiomatic: This extraordinary ceremony ranks with Dai Zong—we beg to follow antiquity and use music; let the ministry compose hymns."

sentences.zh: 於是詔樂章六奏，用「豐」。

translations.literal: Thereupon an edict fixed six hymn performances, all using "Feng."
translations.idiomatic: An edict then fixed six hymn movements, all using "Fēng".

sentences.zh: 十月，張廣泗、訥親討金川久無功，上特命大學士傅恆為經略，出師，行授鉞禮。

translations.literal: In the tenth month Zhang Guangsi and Neqin campaigned against Jinchuan long without success; His Majesty specially appointed Grand Secretary Fu Heng as commissioner-general to take the field, performing the rite of bestowing the battle-axe.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month Zhang Guangsi and Neqin had campaigned against Jinchuan without success; the emperor appointed Grand Secretary Fu Heng commissioner-general and performed the rite of bestowing the battle-axe.

sentences.zh: 是日御太和殿，陳法駕鹵簿樂器如常儀。

translations.literal: That day at the Hall of Supreme Harmony the legal guard of honor and instruments followed usual rites.
translations.idiomatic: That day at the Hall of Supreme Harmony guard and instruments followed usual rites.

sentences.zh: 升座，中和韶樂奏隆平，經略跪受敕印行禮，丹陛大樂奏慶平，經略隨奉敕印大臣由東階下，樂止，上還宮中和韶樂奏顯平。

translations.literal: Ascending the seat, Harmonious Central Shao played Long Ping; the commissioner-general knelt to receive seal and edict and performed rites—Cinnabar Steps great music played Qing Ping; the commissioner-general followed the minister bearing seal and edict down the east steps—music stopped; returning to the palace Harmonious Central played Xian Ping.
translations.idiomatic: Ascending, Harmonious Central Shao played Lóng Píng; the commissioner-general knelt for seal and edict—Cinnabar Steps Qìng Píng; he followed the minister bearing them down the east steps—music stopped; return Xiǎn Píng.

sentences.zh: 禡日建八旗大纛於堂子內門外之南，軍士執螺角列竣，上輿出宮，樂陳而不作。

translations.literal: On the exorcism day eight-banner great banners were raised south of the inner gate outside the Hall of the Spirits; soldiers held conch horns in ranks; the emperor's carriage left the palace—music was set out but not played.
translations.idiomatic: On the exorcism day eight-banner great standards were raised south of the Hall of the Spirits inner gate; soldiers with conch horns stood in ranks; the carriage left the palace—music arrayed but silent.

sentences.zh: 至紅椿，聲螺角，上入自街門降輿，螺止。

translations.literal: Reaching Hongchun, conchs sounded; the emperor entered by the street gate and descended—conchs stopped.
translations.idiomatic: At Hongchun conchs sounded; he entered by the street gate and descended—conchs stopped.

sentences.zh: 行禮，復聲螺。

translations.literal: Performing rites, conchs sounded again.
translations.idiomatic: During the rites conchs sounded again.

sentences.zh: 纛前行禮畢，出至紅椿，螺止，導迎樂作。

translations.literal: When rites before the banners were complete and they went out to Hongchun, conchs stopped and conducting-welcome music began.
translations.idiomatic: When rites before the banners ended and they reached Hongchun, conchs stopped and conducting-welcome music began.

sentences.zh: 駕至東長安門外，御武帳，升座，賜經略酒，從征官皆櫜鞬，辭，啟行。

translations.literal: The carriage reached outside the East Chang'an Gate; at the military tent he ascended the seat and bestowed wine on the commissioner-general; officers on campaign all with quivers and bows declined and set out.
translations.idiomatic: The carriage reached outside the East Chang'an Gate; at the military tent he ascended and bestowed wine on the commissioner-general; campaign officers with quivers and bows took leave and marched.

sentences.zh: 還宮，導迎樂作。

translations.literal: Returning to the palace, conducting-welcome music played.
translations.idiomatic: Returning to the palace, conducting-welcome music played.

sentences.zh: 明年凱旋，賜宴豐澤園，駕御帳殿，進茶、賜茶奏景運乾坤泰，掌儀捧臺盞卮壺奏聖德誕敷，進饌奏日耀中天。

translations.literal: The next year on triumphant return a banquet was given at Fengze Garden; the emperor entered the tent hall; presenting and bestowing tea played Jing Yun Qian Kun Tai; the Directorate of Ceremonies bore platters, cups, and ewers to Sheng De Dan Fu; presenting food played Ri Yao Zhong Tian.
translations.idiomatic: The next year, on triumphant return, a banquet at Fengze Garden; entering the tent hall, tea played Jǐng Yùn Qiān Kūn Tài; the Directorate bore platters and cups to Shèng Dé Dàn Fū; food Rì Yào Zhōng Tiān.

sentences.zh: 其後兆惠平定西域，阿桂再克金川，凱旋皆用此禮，改景運乾坤泰為聖武光昭世，聖德誕敷為禹甸遐通，日耀中天為聖治遐昌。

translations.literal: Thereafter when Zhao Hui pacified the Western Regions and Agui again conquered Jinchuan, triumphant return all used this rite—changing Jing Yun Qian Kun Tai to Sheng Wu Guang Zhao Shi, Sheng De Dan Fu to Yu Dian Xia Tong, Ri Yao Zhong Tian to Sheng Zhi Xia Chang.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhao Hui pacified the Western Regions and Agui reconquered Jinchuan, triumph used the same rite—Jǐng Yùn Qiān Kūn Tài became Shèng Wǔ Guāng Zhāo Shì, Shèng Dé Dàn Fū Yǔ Diàn Xiá Tōng, Rì Yào Zhōng Tiān Shèng Zhì Xiá Chāng.

sentences.zh: 改德隆舞為德勝之舞。

translations.literal: They changed the Dance of Virtue Ascendant to the Dance of Virtue Victorious.
translations.idiomatic: The Virtue Ascendant dance became the Virtue Victorious dance.

sentences.zh: 中和樂章皆增武成慶語，以誇膚績。

translations.literal: Harmonious Central hymns all added martial accomplishment and celebration phrases to boast of achievements received.
translations.idiomatic: Harmonious Central hymns gained martial triumph phrases to boast received achievements.

sentences.zh: 上又自作凱歌三十章，增鐃歌十六章，郊勞時奏之。

translations.literal: His Majesty also himself composed thirty chapters of triumph songs and added sixteen nao-song pieces, performed at suburban reward and consolation.
translations.idiomatic: He also composed thirty triumph songs and added sixteen nao-song pieces, performed at suburban reward rites.

sentences.zh: 聲容矞厖，邁隆古矣。

translations.literal: Sound and appearance were luxuriant and grand—surpassing antiquity's splendor.
translations.idiomatic: Sound and spectacle grew luxuriant—surpassing antiquity's splendor.

sentences.zh: 二十六年，江西撫臣奏得古鐘十一，圖以進，上示廷臣，定為鎛鐘，命依鍾律尺度，鑄造十二律鎛鐘，備中和特懸。

translations.literal: In the twenty-sixth year the Jiangxi governor memorialized obtaining eleven ancient bells and submitted drawings; the emperor showed the court and fixed them as bo bells; ordered casting twelve-pitch bo bells to bell scale for a special Harmonious Central suspension.
translations.idiomatic: In the twenty-sixth year the Jiangxi governor reported eleven ancient bells and submitted drawings; the emperor showed the court, identified them as bó bells, and ordered twelve-pitch bó bells cast to bell scale for a special Harmonious Central suspension.

sentences.zh: 既成，帝自製銘，允祿等又請造特磬十二虡，與鎛鐘配，鑿和闐玉為之。

translations.literal: When complete the emperor himself composed inscriptions; Yunlu and others also asked to make twelve special qing frames to pair with the bo bells, carved from Khotan jade.
translations.idiomatic: When complete the emperor inscribed them himself; Yunlu and others also requested twelve special qing frames paired with the bó bells, carved from Khotan jade.

sentences.zh: 三十三年，定關帝廟樂章，迎神、送神三獻章各一。

translations.literal: In the thirty-third year they fixed Guandi temple hymns—one each for welcoming spirits, sending spirits, and the three offerings.
translations.idiomatic: In the thirty-third year they fixed Guandi temple hymns—one each for welcoming spirits, dismissal, and the three offerings.

sentences.zh: 四十五年八月，高宗七旬萬壽，增喜起舞樂九章。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of the forty-fifth year, at the High Ancestor's seventieth-birthday longevity celebration, nine pieces of music for the Joyful Rising Dance were added.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of the forty-fifth year, for the Qianlong Emperor's seventieth-birthday celebration, nine musical pieces for the Joyful Rising Dance were added.

sentences.zh: 自是凡有大慶典，則增制樂章以為常……

translations.literal: From then on, whenever there was a great celebration, additional hymn pieces were composed as a regular practice, and so forth.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, whenever a great celebration occurred, additional hymn pieces were composed as a matter of course, and the like.

sentences.zh: 五十二年，命皇子永瑢與鄒奕孝、莊存與重定詩經樂譜，糾鄭世子載堉之謬。

translations.literal: In the fifty-second year, the prince Yong Rong, Zou Yixiao, and Zhuang Cunyu were ordered to re-fix the musical scores of the Book of Odes and correct the errors of Prince Zaiyu of Zheng.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-second year the prince Yong Rong, Zou Yixiao, and Zhuang Cunyu were ordered to revise the musical scores of the Book of Odes and correct the errors of Prince Zaiyu of Zheng.

sentences.zh: 五十八年，又命樂部肄演安南、廓爾喀、粗緬甸、細緬甸諸樂，故清之樂，終帝之世凡數變。

translations.literal: In the fifty-eighth year, the Music Office was again ordered to rehearse the music of Annam, Gurkha, coarse Burma, and fine Burma; thus Qing music underwent several changes throughout the emperor's reign.
translations.idiomatic: In the fifty-eighth year the Music Office was again ordered to rehearse the music of Annam, Gurkha, coarse Burma, and fine Burma; thus Qing music changed several times over the Qianlong Emperor's reign.

sentences.zh: 仁宗，增製太上皇帝三大節御殿中和韶樂二章，丹陛大樂一章，宮中行禮丹陛大樂一章，筵宴中和清樂一章、丹陛清樂二章、慶隆舞樂九章，又增皇極殿千叟宴太上皇帝御殿中和韶樂二章。

translations.literal: Under the Renzong, there were added: for the Supreme Emperor's three great festivals at the imperial hall, two pieces of Harmonious Central Shao music; one of Great Music of the Cinnabar Steps; one of Cinnabar Steps Great Music for rites within the palace; for banquets, one of Harmonious Central clear music, two of Cinnabar Steps clear music, and nine of Qinglong dance music; and two more pieces of Harmonious Central Shao for the Supreme Emperor's hall at the Thousand Elders banquet in the Hall of Imperial Supremacy.
translations.idiomatic: Under the Jiaqing Emperor were added: for the Retired Emperor's three great festivals at the imperial hall, two Harmonious Central Shao pieces; one Cinnabar Steps great music piece; one Cinnabar Steps great music piece for rites within the palace; for banquets, one Harmonious Central clear music piece, two Cinnabar Steps clear music pieces, and nine Qinglong dance pieces; and two further Harmonious Central Shao pieces for the Retired Emperor's hall at the Thousand Elders banquet in the Hall of Imperial Supremacy.

sentences.zh: 自後臨雍，幸翰林院、文昌廟祀，社稷壇祈晴及萬壽節，皆增制樂章。

translations.literal: Afterward, for imperial lectures at the National University, visits to the Hanlin Academy, sacrifices at the Wenchang Temple, prayers for clear weather at the altars of soil and grain, and the Longevity Festival, hymn pieces were all newly composed.
translations.idiomatic: Thereafter, for imperial lectures at the National University, visits to the Hanlin Academy, sacrifices at the Wenchang Temple, prayers for clear weather at the altars of soil and grain, and the Longevity Festival, new hymn pieces were composed in each case.

sentences.zh: 八年，命筵宴停止安南樂。

translations.literal: In the eighth year, banquets were ordered to discontinue Annam music.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth year banquets were ordered to discontinue Annam music.

sentences.zh: 十四年元旦，太和殿筵宴，命演朝鮮、回部、金川、緬甸樂舞等項，遇慶隆舞、喜起舞，即以承應。

translations.literal: On New Year's Day of the fourteenth year, at the banquet in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, Korean, Muslim, Jinchuan, and Burmese music and dance were ordered performed; when the Qinglong dance or Joyful Rising dance was due, these were used to answer the occasion.
translations.idiomatic: On New Year's Day of the fourteenth year, at the banquet in the Hall of Supreme Harmony, Korean, Muslim, Jinchuan, and Burmese music and dance were performed; when the Qinglong or Joyful Rising dances were called for, these items served in their place.

sentences.zh: 又增隊舞大臣四人，歲如故事。

translations.literal: Four ministers for formation dance were also added, annually according to precedent.
translations.idiomatic: Four ministers for formation dance were also added, appointed each year according to precedent.
